body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against illegal drugs, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested an individual for selling illegal drugs in Naga City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject. as IVY H. AGUILAR a.k.a. IVY O. HAROCHOC OIC Distor said the case stemmed from an information received by the NBI regarding a certain “IVY” who was allegedly involved in unauthorized selling, distribution, and trading of dangerous drugs particularly shabu in Naga City. According to the information, Subject “IVY” carries out her modus operandi by selling, trading, and distributing shabu to customers inside a rented room at Sampaguita tourist Inn, Magsaysay Avenue, Balatas, Naga City. The information added that “IVY” does such scheme in order to avoid detection by the authorities. It was further disclosed that “IVY” was staying at Room 206 of the said establishment. Informant also disclosed that he knows such facts because he had several previous transactions with the Subject. Operatives asked the informant if he could buy shabu from the Subject. Informant affirmed and said that since he had already previous transactions with the Subject, he could set a meeting with her on the same day to buy illegal drugs. With this, a buy-bust operation was hatched. At around 4:20 of June 29, 2021, informant went ahead of Room 206 and upon entering, he handed the marked money to “IVY” and the latter handed over the shabu. At this juncture, operatives entered the room and placed “IVY” under arrest. It was discovered that “IVY” was carrying the identities IVY H. AGUILAR and IVY O. HAROCHOC. Seized from Subject Ivy are 27 pieces of heat-sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, 4 pieces of aluminum foil, 8 pieces of improvised tooter, 8 pieces of lighters, 2 pieces of transparent sachet containing aluminum foils, 2 weighing scales, and 1 piece burner. Spot report on the operation was submitted to PDEA Region V as mandated by the implementing rules and regulations. Thus, within 24-hour period required by law, NBI-NADO operatives caused the immediate submission of the seized items to Camarines Sur Provincial Crime Laboratory for dangerous drugs examination. The next day, result of laboratory examination conducted by Camarines Sur Provincial Crime Laboratory Office on the seized items yielded positive for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride, a dangerous drug commonly known as shabu. Urine specimen of Subject IVY AGUILAR likewise gave positive result for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride. Subject IVY H. AGUILAR a.k.a. IVY O. HAROCHOC was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Naga City for violation of Sections 5, 11, 12, and 15 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002).

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI SEIZES MORE THAN P4M IN COUNTERFEIT AND SUBSTANDARD PRODUCTS The National Bureau of Investigation – Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) served search warrants at multiple locations in the NCR and in Iloilo City, Iloilo Province, on September 8, 14, and 15, 2026. The operation resulted in the seizure of counterfeit LPG products, AquaFlask products, and Galvanized Iron (GI) pipes valued at more than four million pesos. On September 8, the NBI-IPRD executed search warrants in Taguig, resulting in the confiscation of twelve (12) 2.7kg cylinder tanks of “Island Gas” and “M-Gas,” one (1) 11kg cylinder tank, 18 (eighteen) units of refilling scales, one (1) weighing scale, one (1) LPG compressor, and office devices, with an estimated value of Two Million Pesos (Php2,000,000.00). The operation on September 14, conducted at locations in Manila and Quezon City, resulted in the seizure of one thousand eighteen (1,018) pieces of products in various designs and sizes bearing counterfeit trademarks of “AquaFlask,” estimated to be worth One Million Two Hundred Ten Thousand Four Hundred Forty Pesos (Php1,210,440.00). The September 15 operation NBI-IPRD conducted at four locations in Iloilo City resulted in the recovery of seven hundred forty-two (742) pieces of substandard GI Pipes, with an estimated value of One Million Four Hundred Eighty-Four Thousand Pesos (Php1,484,000.00). The confiscated products from the three operations totaled Four Million Six Hundred Ninety-Four Thousand Four Hundred Forty Pesos (Php4,694,440.00). NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag reminds the public that counterfeit products pose a serious threat to users’ health and safety. Trademark infringement, the unauthorized use of a registered trademark, violates Republic Act No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). The sale and use of substandard steel are punishable under R.A. No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines). https://www.facebook.com/reel/1096039992817712

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 05, 2024 In accordance with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to boost the campaign against Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children, the NBI – Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested an individual for violations of Section 4 (c) (r) (f) of R.A. No. 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act); Section 4 of R.A. No. 9208, as amended by Section 4 par. (k) (2) of R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Person Act of 2012); and Section 9 of R.A. No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Director Santiago said that the arrest stemmed from the referral of the U.S. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Office regarding the child exploitation activities of the Subject. Agents of NBI-CEVRO participated in a Zoom meeting to witness and supervise the real-time interaction through Skype between Homeland Undercover Agent and the Subject using a certain Skype name, which confirmed that the Subject is indeed engaged in the distribution of Children Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Materials (CSAEM). Thus, the operatives of NBI-CEVRO together with the US Homeland Security Investigations officers and personnel from a non-governmental organization (NGO) immediately applied for a WSSECD against the Subject, which was granted by the court. On November 27, 2024, the operatives proceeded to the address of the Subject in Lapu-lapu City, Province of Cebu and duly implemented the WSSECD, which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. The operatives were able to seize from the Subject three (3) cellular phones containing CSAEM and sex toys. Moreover, three (3) minor children were rescued during the operation. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-CEVRO for the successful operation and encouraged the public to report to the NBI any form of child abuse.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI-SAU ARRESTS 6 VIETNAMESE NATIONALS INVOLVED IN MAKATI CITY ALLEGED ONLINE GAMBLING-RELATED FRAUD OPERATION The National Bureau of Investigation – Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) successfully conducted a cyber warrant operation against a group of foreign nationals allegedly involved in an online gambling-related fraud scheme operating within Makati City. In April 2026, the NBI-SAU received confidential information regarding the alleged activities of several individuals purportedly engaged in providing customer relations and support services for clients of an offshore online gaming platform. The alleged operation was reportedly being conducted within Units of Signa Designer Residences Tower 2, Valero Street corner Rufino Street, Salcedo Village, Makati City. Acting on the information received, NBI-SAU operatives conducted casing and surveillance operations to verify the reported activities. After establishing reasonable grounds to believe that illegal activities were being conducted within the subject premises, the operatives applied for Warrants to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSED) before the Regional Trial Court, Branch 148, Makati City. On May 09, 2026, NBI-SAU operatives conducted a pre-operational briefing in preparation for the implementation of the WSSECD against the occupants of the target condominium units. The operatives coordinated strategic operational procedures for the simultaneous service of the warrants. At approximately 7:00 P.M. of the same day, the operatives proceeded to the target location and implemented the operation. Each team proceeded to different units, where operatives found a total of six (6) individuals actively operating laptop computers. NBI-SAU conducted a plain view examination of the said laptop computers; it was observed that the devices displayed what appeared to be customer support platform, telegram chats, and websites linked to “Luck8,” an online gambling platform. Examination revealed that the websites displayed on the computers used different URLs from the legitimate platforms, indicating the operation of fabricated or imitation websites allegedly designed to deceive users into believing they were accessing the legitimate “Luck8” platform. Investigators likewise observed that the websites utilized unsecured “http” protocols instead of the more secure “https” protocol, further suggesting the unauthorized and potentially fraudulent nature of the websites. They allegedly discovered that the subjects were monitoring legitimate online casino players victims through Telegram groups in order to identify and recruit potential victims. The investigation further revealed that the subjects would allegedly send fraudulent links redirecting users to imitation websites designed to closely resemble the legitimate “Luck8” online gaming platform. Based on evidences gathered, NBI-SAU arrested the Subjects. They were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Makati City for violations of Section 4(b)(2) “Computer Related Fraud” of RA 10175.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) in an entrapment operation in La Union for Cyber-Estafa. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as SHYNA MAY VERGARA. Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by one of the victims of Subject Vergara, alleging that the subject enticed her to invest Php 5,000.00 for a payout of Php 9,000.00 every twenty-two (22) days, with a one-time payout for each investment. On February 24, 2022, the complainant met with Subject Vergara and handed Php 5,000.00 as her investment. On the next day, the victim learned from her sister that Subject Vergara is a fraud and she was a victim by the Subject’s scheme. Upon learning that several complainant/victims had already filed a complaint before the NBI and other Law Enforcement Agencies, the complainant sought the assistance of NBI-IRO. Thus, an entrapment operation was planned to capture the culprit behind the said illicit activities. As per the instruction of NBI-IRO, the complainant agreed to meet with the subject in a fast food chain in Agoo, La Union. On March 14, 2022, operatives of NBI-IRO proceeded to the target meeting place and strategically positioned themselves in the area. An hour later, Subject Vergara arrived and sat down with the complainant. Upon handing over of the marked money to Subject Vergara by the complainant, operatives of NBI-IRO immediately approached the subject and announced her arrest. The operatives were able to recover from the subject the marked money. Subject Vergara was immediately brought to NBI-IRO office for standard booking procedures. Subject was presented before the Prosecutor’s Office of Agoo, La Union for violation of Article 315 of the RPC in relation to Sec. 6 of RA 10175.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 05, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the agents NBI-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) seized a large volume of unregistered vape products in Guiguinto, Bulacan. On May 6, 2025, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) requested assistance with the investigation, potential law enforcement actions, and the eventual enforcement of BIR Mission Orders against individuals involved in the possession, advertisement, sale, and distribution of unregistered vape products online. An investigation conducted by NBI-OTCD agents revealed that some of these vape products either lacked BIR stamps or had stamps suspected to be counterfeit. This indicates that the proper taxes for these products have not been paid to the government. On May 29, 2025, following the investigation by NBI-OTCD, a Search Warrant was issued for the premises of the target individuals. On May 30, 2025, agents of the NBI-OTCD and BIR-LTS implemented a search warrant in Guiguinto, Bulacan, resulting in the seizure of Php36,000,000.00 worth of unregistered vape products. The individuals found at the establishments were invited for statement-taking to support the ongoing investigation. Charges for violation of Section 263 (Unlawful Possession of Vapor Products) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC), as amended by Republic Act No. 11346, were filed against the owners of the establishments.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of 2 individuals in Cebu City for smuggling medicines used for treatment of COVID 19. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as Dr. NELSON ONG y TIU and his daughter RAISA NICOLE ONG y CHENG, a third year medical student. Director Distor said that on September 14, 2021, NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) based in Cebu City received an information that shipment of unregistered and illegally imported Tocilizumab vials placed in a cold storage box is due to arrive from Manila to Cebu via PAL flight on that day at 5:30 pm. Tocilizumab is a medicine used for treatment of severely COVID 19 patients. It added that the shipment was consigned to a certain Raisa Ong, whose name had already cropped up in the intelligence report as one of the active distributors of Tocilizumab and other COVID-19 related medicines in Cebu. Acting under strict orders from Director Distor, NBI-CEVRO operatives proceeded to PAL Cargo arrival area at MCIAA Complex, Lapu-lapu City to validate and verify the information. The NBI operatives coordinated with Cargo personnel and conducted a visual inspection of the target package, then requested the Cargo personnel to separate the cargo and put it in a secured place until the arrival of the consignee/claimant. Later, a Chinese looking female, later identified as Raisa Ong, showed up to claim the package. Subject Raisa Ong was accompanied by Subject Nelson Ong while processing the release of the subject package. Upon withdrawal of the package, Subjects Raisa Ong and Nelson Ong proceeded to their vehicle. At this juncture, NBI-CEVRO operatives immediately approached Subjects. The operatives requested to the Subjects to open the cold storage box and they agreed. Subject Raisa Ong opened the box and found therein ten (10) pieces of Tocilizumab vials and 25 boxes of Baricitinib, also a medicine for CVID 19, tablets all placed in carton packaging which appeared to be imported from India but no local importer or distributor and without the FDA approved labelling and prints. When asked for authority to import said medicines, the Subjects could not present any document or license to import, distribute or sell the same. Thus, the 2 Subjects were placed under arrest. Certification issued by the FDA also revealed that no authority or license to operate as drug importer and/or any drug establishment of any pharmaceutical drugs has been granted to the arrested Subjects. The FDA further said that according to their examination,the seized medicines have been certified to be unregistered and illegally diverted. On September 17, 2021, the Subjects were presented fot Inquest proceedings before the Lapu-lapu City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of R.A. 3720 as amended by R.A. 9711, otherwise known as the “Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009” in relation to R.A. 10863 (Custom’s Modernization Act).

body: For the fifth consecutive year, the Philippines had been given Tier 1 ranking in the US government’s 2020 Trafficking in Persons Report or the TIP Report. It is an annual report issued by the US State Department’s Office to monitor and combat Trafficking in Persons. It ranks various governments based on their perceived efforts to acknowledge the existence of, and fight human trafficking. The Tier rankings are based on a country’s compliance with standards outlined in the Trafficking Victims Protection Act (TVPA) of 2000. The law provides a three-pronged approach that includes prevention, protection and prosecution. The rankings given are Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 2 Watch List and Tier 3. A Tier 1 ranking indicates that the Philippine government has acknowledged the existence of human trafficking, made efforts to address the problem, and complies with TVPA’s minimum standards. At the forefront is the Inter Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) of which the NBI is a member. According to the Report, the Philippine government fully meets the minimum standards for the elimination of trafficking as it continues to demonstrate serious and sustained efforts during the reporting period. The points raised in the Report on government efforts to eliminate trafficking include: Improving the coordination of services for returning Filipino migrant workers who are victims of trafficking overseas Convicting and punishing traffickers, including an official complicit in sex trafficking and labor trafficking Increasing assistance to survivors who provide testimony Increasing the use of prosecution procedures that reduce the potential for further harm to trafficking victims For the NBI, this will serve both as an inspiration and reward in our relentless fight against Human Trafficking. Despite challenging times, the NBI thru its Anti Human Trafficking Division, remains steadfast and committed to our mandate of protecting our citizens, especially the most vulnerable ones, against Human Trafficking, of all forms. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of 3 subjects in Tanay, Rizal for misappropriating and converting a sizeable area of land and falsely pretending to possess property in violation of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as WILSON VAFLOR DADULA, ROMMEL AMANDORON DADULA, and MARIO ORDONA RUANTO. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the heirs of the legal owner of the subject private land. According to the complaint, Subject Dadula together with Subjects Rommel and Mario disposed, sell, and offered for sale portions of the land owned by the complainants without their knowledge and authority. According to one of the complainants, he and his siblings are the legal heirs of the owner of the subject land as evidenced by a Transfer Certificate Title issued by the Registry of Deeds of Rizal. The complainant further alleged that Subject Dadula is a caretaker of their land hired by their father to oversee the property in 2000. In 2015, complainant’s father brought a complaint before the Barangay seeking the ouster of Subject Dadula. In turn, the Barangay issued a Certificate to file action in court against Subject Dadula. When their father died, the complainants pursued the ouster of Subject Dadula to no avail. To the dismay, they found out that the property is already occupied by more or less 90 families and was being sold by the subjects thru their organization called “ALPHA OMEGA WORLD DEVELOPMENT MARSHALL PROGRAM”. The said organization has a membership fee of Php 2,500.00 and the members may acquire a lot ranging from 100, 200, or even 300 square meters for the amount of P350.00 to P500.00 per square meter. After payment, the member will be issued a “Certificate of Occupancy” entitling them to possess and occupy portions of the subject property. NBI-RIZDO was able to strike a deal to purchase 100 square meters of land and a down payment of Php 50,000.00 was given to Subject Dadula. With enough evidence at hand, NBI-RIZDO planned an entrapment operation against the subjects. On April 26, 2021, NBI-RIZDO operatives proceeded to the agreed meeting area where the remaining balance will be paid. They tactically placed themselves in the vicinity and after the poseur buyer handed over the marked money to Subject Dadula, NBI-RIZDO operatives immediately arrested the three subjects. The three subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Rizal for violation of Article 315 paragraph 1 (b) (misappropriating and converting and paragraph 2 (a) (falsely pretending to possess property) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT November 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) formally held a turnover ceremony marking the transition of leadership from Retired Judge Jaime B. Santiago to Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno, who now assumes the role of the Bureau’s Officer-in-Charge. The ceremony, held at the NBI Main Office in Pasay City, was attended by the Bureau’s Directorial Staff, Regional Directors, Agents-in-Charge, Division Chiefs, Chiefs of Staff, and personnel from various departments. In his message, former Director Santiago expressed his gratitude for the steadfast support and cooperation extended to him throughout his term. He remarked that he is turning over the Bureau “to the capable hands of Atty. Magno,” wishing him continued success and objective leadership. The event featured the symbolic turnover of the Bureau’s insignia, signifying a smooth, united, and orderly transition of leadership within the NBI. In his inaugural address, OIC Director Magno reaffirmed his commitment to uphold the Bureau’s mandate with integrity, professionalism, and excellence in public service. He expressed his gratitude to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for the trust given to him. OIC Director Magno outlined five key pillars that will guide the Bureau’s direction under his leadership: 1) Sustain ongoing investigations and reforms ensuring that the pursuit of truth is never interrupted by fear or favor, 2) Modernize capabilities through enhanced training, technology, and teamwork; 3) Institutionalize transparency and accountability, recognizing that trust is the Bureau’s greatest currency; 4) Care for NBI personnel, emphasizing that the Bureau’s greatest asset is its dedicated men and women; and 5) Bring the NBI closer to the people by listening, engaging, and working alongside communities, as justice is strongest when it is shared. Atty. Magno also introduced Project LINANG (Leadership, Integrity, Nurturing Accountability Nationwide Grid) a strategic initiative to cultivate ethical leadership across generations of agents. The project includes advancing the digital justice initiative to modernize case management and forensic processes, strengthening the NBI Academy of Excellence to produce not only competent but also compassionate investigators, adapting an open policy framework that will promote transparency while safeguarding investigative integrity, and bringing the “justice-on-wheels” program to reach remote communities, proving that the arm of justice extends to all the Filipinos. OIC Director Magno likewise expressed his heartfelt appreciation to all NBI personnel for their quiet courage and unwavering dedication to service, reminding everyone to serve without seeking glory. “Tapat, tama, at tunay na paglilingkod honest in service, right in action, genuine in purpose – we will be there when justice is needed” OIC Director Magno concluded. With this transition, the NBI reaffirms its enduring commitment to uphold good governance, strengthen the rule of law, and deliver quality service to the Filipino people.

body: In line with the continuing anti-illegal drug campaign of the government, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NAGDO) arrested one of the notorious drug pushers in Mabolo, Naga City on June 12, 2017. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as RICHARD ESTRELLA y FRANCISCO a.k.a. CHABO, who operates in towns nearby Naga City. He said Estrella was arrested in his residence in Mabolo, Naga City by virtue of a Search Warrant issued by RTC, Iriga City, stressing “the operation yielded several sachets of methamphetamine hydrochloride or commonly known as shabu and drug paraphernalia including .38 caliber revolver, several live ammunitions, and bundles of cash believed to be drug money from the sale of the prohibited drug. Naga City expressed appreciation for the operation of the NBI since Subject had been a long time problem in their area because of his drug activities. Moreover, Subject had been the target of several Tokhang operations but managed to elude the authorities. Subject is currently detained at the NBI Naga District Office and will undergo Inquest Proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Naga City for violation of Section 11, Article II of R.A. 9165 or The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of the NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI – SAU) have arrested a Subject who is facing a string of Estafa cases in Mandaluyong and Paranaque Cities. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as LINO ESPINOSA LIM, JR., who was arrested by NBI – SAU operatives on June 16, 2017 in a coffee shop in Quezon City after continued surveillance and monitoring of the Subject. Director Gierran said that based on the information referred to the NBI in March this year, Subject represented himself as having close ties and connections with officials occupying key positions in the government such as President Rodrigo Roa Duterte, Senate President Coco Pimentel and Atty. Fred Lim of PAGCOR. Through sweet and cunning words, Gierran added, Subject LIM, JR. was able to convinced his victim to invest a total of P14,500,000 hard-earned money in various government projects and earn high interest therefrom. When his victim made follow-ups on Subject LIM, he kept on giving alibis and eventually could not find him anymore. Record check on LIM also showed that he has Standing Warrants of Arrest both for Estafa before the Regional Trial Courts of Mandaluyong and Paranaque. Three (3) other complainants have surfaced and filed their respective complaints against Subject LIM where a total of Ten Million (P10,000,000.00) where obtained from them using the same above-stated scheme. NBI-SAU operatives have devised a number of entrapment operations against Subject LIM but he did not appear on the set occasions. Continued surveillance and monitoring of the Subject were conducted by operatives until on June 16, 2017, thru the information provided to the NBI, a team of NBI – SAU operatives tailed Subject LIM from Cainta, Rizal until he reached Quezon City where he was arrested.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 9, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Seven (7) individuals identified as NORBERTO BOLOR CORACHEA, CARLO RYAN SIMBULAN GRATIL, ALLAN NICOLAS BASA, JOJO ISIP CRISOSTOMO, EDGARDO GUAN CAPUNO, ERNESTO OALN CRUZANA SR., and Alias LIMUEL VILLANUEVA were arrested for Usurpation of Authority and violation of R.A. No. 10591 in relation to Omnibus Election Code. On May 8, 2025, the above named Subjects coordinated with Pakil MPS and introduced themselves as NBI Agents, and that they are from NBI Main, Pasay City and will be conducting investigation on an alleged Vote Buying and Vote Selling Activity in Matikiw, Pakil, Laguna. After which, the PSSg Duty Desk Officer informed the Chief of Police regarding the said coordination, which he subsequently verified with the NBI Legal Service and Chief, NBI-Laguna District Office for the legitimacy of the presented ID and Badge. Verification conducted revealed that the above-mentioned individuals are not organic personnel of NBI. Upon receipt of information, hot pursuit operation was conducted by Pakil Local Police. Subjects’ vehicle was plugged down in front Kabulusan Elementary School, Brgy Kabulusan, Pakil, Laguna. Upon inspection of their vehicle, the following pieces of evidence were recovered: 1 pc leather wallet with Fake NBI ID and Badge, 1 pc Fake Badge with necklace, 1 pc Para-Ordnance 14.45 Limited Cal .45 pistol, 2 pcs Cal .45 Magazine, 44 pcs Cal .45 live Ammo, 1 pc Armscor model 200 Cal .38 revolver, and 6 pcs Cal .38 live Ammo. Arrested Subjects were brought to the Pakil Municipal Police Station for appropriate action and documentation, while appropriate documents were being prepared for filing to Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) implemented multiple search warrants in various locations in Manila, Pasay, Cavite and Laguna for violation of Section 155 (Trademark Infringement) in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No. 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” On July 21, IPRD agents implemented search warrants in three (3) establishments in Calamba, Sta. Rosa, Biñan in Laguna, and on July 26, five (5) stalls in Pasay City at the request of the authorized representative of Louis Vuitton. The operation resulted in the seizure of One Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty-Six (1,736) pieces of counterfeit “Louis Vuitton/LV” products with a total estimated value of One Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Forty Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty-Four Pesos (Php 198,040,744.00), as per LV representative. On July 26, search warrants were served against an establishment in Bacoor City, Cavite, at the request of Ms. Arabelle Lee on behalf of Mitsukoshi Motors Philippines Inc., “Makoto,” resulting in the seizure of counterfeit “MAKOTO” motorcycle parts: thirteen (13) pieces of Throttle Cable, twenty-four (24) pieces of Brake Cable, and twenty-seven (27) pieces of Speedometer Cable amounting to more or less Eight Thousand Pesos (Php 8,000.00). On July 28, agents enforced search warrants in four (4) establishments in Manila and five (5) stores in Pasay City, resulting in the seizure of Three Hundred and Twenty (320) pieces of assorted telecommunications equipment/products with an estimated value of Four Hundred Twenty-Seven Thousand and Four Hundred Pesos (Php 427,400.00). The search was conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner in the presence of the Respondent’s witnesses, Building Representative, and Barangay Representative. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing said warrants and their enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT June 8, 2022 DISTOR ORDERS INVESTIGATION ON BUS BOMBINGS IN MINDANAO The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has started the investigation on the series of Yellow Bus Line, Inc. (YBLI), Mindanao Star Bus, Rural Tours bombing attacks in Mindanao. There are already six (6) bombings attacks on bus lines in Mindanao in the last 2 years. NBI Director ERIC B. DISTOR leads the probe and calls on NBI Regional Directors and officials to take part in the said investigation. DISTOR, with the team of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) operatives, travelled to the areas of concerns in Mindanao, together with the NBI forensic experts and evidence response team. NBI Deputy Director for Forensic Investigation Service (DDFIS) Ferdinand Lavin and Deputy Director for Intelligence Service (DDIntS) Roel Bolivar also joined the NBI team in Mindanao. The series of bombing incidents started on January 7, 2021, with a hoax bomb threat and extortion demand being sent to YBLI Koronadal City, South Cotabato office. At the time of the call, YBL bus no. 2688 was at Kidapawan, Cotabato Overland Terminal and was searched by PNP EOD. The emplaced improvised explosive device (IED) was found thereat and was rendered safe. Footage taken from the YBL Bus no. 2688 CCTV camera showed two male passengers leaving the IED inside the bus. Twenty (20) days after, on January 27, 2021, a bomb exploded in YBLI bus no. 2988 at a stop over at National Highway, Crossing Sibsib, Tulunan, North Cotabato. One (1) civilian was killed and four (4) civilians were wounded in the incident. Extortion and terrorism were the motives of the bombing according to the military. Another bombing incident took place on June 3, 2021 where YBLI bus no. A-104 was burned at M’Lang, North Cotabato, killing three (3) civilians while six (6) others were injured. This year, four (4) bus bombings occurred in separate locations in Mindanao. On January 11, 2022, a Mindanao Star bus was bombed in Aleosan, North Cotabato where a five-year-old boy expired and three (3) individuals got injured. On April 24, 2022, a bus of Rural Tours Bus exploded in Parang, Maguindanao hurting at least three (3) passengers. On May 26, 2022, two (2) separate explosions transpired. Another YBLI bus (no. 2108) was bombed at Koronadal City, wounding two civilians. Reportedly, YBLI received an extortion demand before the attack. On the other hand, a roadside explosion took place at Exit Road, Brgy Calean, Tacurong City, Sultan Kudarat. Fortunately, no one was hurt in the incident. Extortion and terrorism are the motives of the bombing based on information gathered. The Bureau’s probe on the series of bombings is directed in ensuring national security as well as to prevent possible major attacks not only in Mindanao but also in the entire country.

NBI Deputy Director for Forensic Investigation Service (DDFIS) Ferdinand Lavin and Deputy Director for Intelligence Service (DDIntS) Roel Bolivar also joined the NBI team in Mindanao. The series of bombing incidents started on January 7, 2021, with a hoax bomb threat and extortion demand being sent to YBLI Koronadal City, South Cotabato office. At the time of the call, YBL bus no. 2688 was at Kidapawan, Cotabato Overland Terminal and was searched by PNP EOD. The emplaced improvised explosive device (IED) was found thereat and was rendered safe. Footage taken from the YBL Bus no. 2688 CCTV camera showed two male passengers leaving the IED inside the bus. Twenty (20) days after, on January 27, 2021, a bomb exploded in YBLI bus no. 2988 at a stop over at National Highway, Crossing Sibsib, Tulunan, North Cotabato. One (1) civilian was killed and four (4) civilians were wounded in the incident. Extortion and terrorism were the motives of the bombing according to the military. Another bombing incident took place on June 3, 2021 where YBLI bus no. A-104 was burned at M’Lang, North Cotabato, killing three (3) civilians while six (6) others were injured. This year, four (4) bus bombings occurred in separate locations in Mindanao. On January 11, 2022, a Mindanao Star bus was bombed in Aleosan, North Cotabato where a five-year-old boy expired and three (3) individuals got injured. On April 24, 2022, a bus of Rural Tours Bus exploded in Parang, Maguindanao hurting at least three (3) passengers. On May 26, 2022, two (2) separate explosions transpired. Another YBLI bus (no. 2108) was bombed at Koronadal City, wounding two civilians. Reportedly, YBLI received an extortion demand before the attack. On the other hand, a roadside explosion took place at Exit Road, Brgy Calean, Tacurong City, Sultan Kudarat. Fortunately, no one was hurt in the incident. Extortion and terrorism are the motives of the bombing based on information gathered. The Bureau’s probe on the series of bombings is directed in ensuring national security as well as to prevent possible major attacks not only in Mindanao but also in the entire country.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 02, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI, BOC SEIZE ₱35.4-M SMUGGLED ONIONS AND GARLIC IN NUEVA ECIJA The National Bureau of Investigation, through its Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), together with the Bureau of Customs (BOC) and the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), seized illegally imported agricultural products worth ₱35,437,198.00 from a cold storage facility in Talavera, Nueva Ecija. The operation stemmed from a complaint requesting investigation into the alleged illegal importation, storage, distribution, and sale of smuggled onions in local markets. Acting on the report, NBI-SAU conducted intelligence gathering, surveillance, validation, and a test-buy operation against Talco Cold Storage Corp., located along Bypass Road, Brgy. Calipahan, Talavera, Nueva Ecija. Samples obtained during the test-buy were submitted to the Department of Agriculture–Bureau of Plant Industry (DA-BPI), which confirmed that the onions were of imported origin. On April 24, 2026, by virtue of a Letter of Authority, NBI-SAU, BOC, and PCG personnel inspected the facility and discovered substantial quantities of imported onions concealed behind stacks of locally packed onions. Authorities observed that the manner of concealment indicated an apparent attempt to hide the imported goods from inspection. After Talco Cold Storage Corp. failed to satisfactorily justify its possession of the imported onions and garlic within the prescribed period, the BOC issued a Warrant of Seizure and Detention on May 21, 2026, directing the seizure and proper disposition of the agricultural products. The total value of the seized goods exceeded the threshold under Republic Act No. 12022, or the Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act of 2024, thereby constituting agricultural smuggling as economic sabotage. NBI-SAU will continue its follow-up investigation to identify all persons responsible and gather additional evidence for the filing of appropriate charges under RA 12022, RA 10863, or the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act, and other applicable laws

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 01, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI INAUGURATES NEW BICOL REGIONAL TRAINING CENTER The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) officially inaugurated its new Bicol Regional Office (BRO) and Training Center on May 21, 2026, marking a significant milestone in strengthening the Bureau’s operational and training capabilities in the Bicol Region. The inauguration ceremony was attended by NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, together with the Deputy Director for Operation, Deputy Director for Administration, Assistant Director for Intelligence, Assistant Director for Information and Communication Technology Service, Assistant Director for Comptroller and BRO Regional Director Atty. Yehlen Agus. Also present were former BRO Regional Directors Atty. Claro De Castro, ARD Olivo Ramos and RD Paterno Morales. Joining the occasion were distinguished government officials, including Hon. Alfredo Garbin, Representative of Ako Bicol Party-list; Hon. Hisham B. Ismail, Mayor of Legazpi City; Hon. Jerold Peña, Municipal Mayor of San Jose, Partido, Camarines Sur; and other LGU Officials of Bicol region, and Regional Directors from different Regional Offices of Bicol. The program was held at the Training Center Auditorium and was highlighted by the ribbon-cutting ceremony led by key officials, followed by the unveiling of the commemorative marker and the blessing of the new facility. In his inspirational message, Director Matibag expressed his sincere appreciation to Congressman Alfredo Garbin of Ako Bicol Party-list for their support and sponsorship of funding for the construction of NBI facilities in the Bicol Region. The Director likewise announced that the Bicol Training Center will be renamed as NBI Academy in Legazpi City, which is envisioned to become a premier training institution where future NBI agents, investigators, and leaders will be developed and prepared for public service. The inauguration of the new Bicol Regional Office and Training Center reflects the NBI’s commitment to strengthening its regional presence, improving operational readiness, and advancing excellence in law enforcement through quality training and modern infrastructure.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 12, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } As part of its continued effort to combat illegal quarrying and protect our natural resources, the National Bureau of Investigation-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested six (6) individuals in Morong, Rizal for illegal quarrying. The operation stemmed from the information received by the NBI-EnCD regarding an alleged illegal quarrying operation being conducted by certain individual in the Municipality of Morong, Province of Rizal, in violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of R.A. No. 7942 otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act of 1995. Information disclosed that individual was extracting and disposing of minerals without the necessary permits and clearances from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Rizal and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region IV-A (DENR-MGB). Surveillance and verification with the DENR-MGB and Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of Cavite (PMRB) confirmed the existence of the illegal quarrying operation. The Regional Director of MGB- Region IV-A issued a certification that based on their records, there are no valid and existing MPSA, Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit, Mineral Processing Permit, Special Minerals Extraction Permit, Exploration Permit or any Memorandum of Agreement issued by the DENR-MGB within Barangay Maybancal, Municipality of Morong, Province of Rizal, nor to Mr. Randy Efsiaca. Further, he also certifies that based on the Inventory of Local Government Unit-Issued permits in the province of Rizal as of 2nd Quarter of Calendar Year 2025, as provided by the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board, no valid and existing Quarry permit or Transport and Hauling Permit (THP) was issued by the Provincial Government of Rizal to Mr. Efsiaca within the aforesaid Barangay. Thus, on August 11, 2025, Agents of NBI-EnCD, together with the personnel from the DENR-MGB Region IV-A, conducted an operation against the illegal quarrying activity in Brgy. Maybancal, Morong, Rizal. The operation resulted in the arrest of ORIÑAS, ARMANDO y PANTOJA, GONZALES, JOHN ROBERT y TUMAGAN, ICALABIS, ERVEN y DE QUIROZ, BRIONES, RODEL y CELEMENCIA, CATAN, ALEXANDER y ILAW, and CADAVEZ, NESTOR y ALMIÑANA. Arrested Subjects were backhoe operators and dump truck drivers. It also led to the seizure of two (2) dumptrucks and two (2) backhoes, with a total estimated value of five million and twenty-five thousand pesos (Php 5,025,000.00) based on an inventory conducted by the DENR-MGB-Region IV-A. Based on the recovered Delivery Receipt from the possession of one of the arrested Subjects, the operator of the quarry operation is the Efsiaca Construction Supplies Trading, which, upon verification in Business Name Registration System of the DTI, is owned by RANDY MOLOD EFSIACA. This name was also identified by the arrested Subjects as the owner of the quarry operation. The arrested Subjects were presented before the Office Prosecutor General, DOJ, Manila for inquest proceedings. The operation is in line with the NBI’s commitment to upholding environmental laws and protecting the welfare of our citizens, as illegal quarrying not only depletes our natural resources, but also poses serious risks to public safety, such as landslides, flooding, and long-term environmental degradation

Director Santiago lauded the NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing said warrants and reminded the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI have arrested a Canadian national for human trafficking in Manila last night. In a Post Operation Report to the Deputy Director for Investigation Service, AIDD Chief, Atty. Joel M. Tovera, said the Canadian national, FRANK ORVILLE MADER, a tenant of UNIT 32R Tower 3 in Robinsons Adriatico Residences, was arrested in his condominium unit by operatives of the NBI-Anti Illegal Drugs Division and Anti Human Trafficking Division for violation of R.A. 7610 otherwise known as the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act. Atty. Tovera said his office received on October 09, 2015, a confidential information of on-going human trafficking and illegal-drug distribution activities at Robinsons Adriatico Residences in Manila. Promptly acting on the information, coordination and requests for information were made with the Building Administrator to validate the information. He added surveillance and casing activities were likewise organized which showed a foreign national in the company of minors. In the evening of October 15, 20125, Subject MADER was spotted in the company of a minor entering the condominium. Thereafter, operatives of AIDD and AHTRAD coordinated with the building security who accompanied the operatives to the condominium unit occupied by Subject MADER. The building security knocked at unit 32R which was opened by a minor. The operatives entered and found Subject MADER on the bed with a half-naked minor which led to his arrest for violation of R.A. 7610. Atty. Tovera also said preparations for inquest proceedings are underway and coordination with the DSWD and Canadian Embassy have been made.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 28, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI STATEMENT | ON THE CLOSURE ORDER AGAINST BLEU HOTEL IN PASIG With respect to the recent closure order issued against Bleu Hotel in Pasig by the local government, it must be emphasized that this development is not rooted in speculation or politics, but in serious allegations involving human trafficking and prostitution. They are offenses that carry grave legal and moral consequences. At the same time, in the spirit of due process and fairness, it must be underscored that the case is not yet final. All parties are entitled to the full protection of the law, including the opportunity to answer the charges, present evidence, and undergo proper judicial proceedings before any final determination of liability is made. Human trafficking is among the most heinous crimes under Philippine law. It exploits the vulnerable, strips individuals of their dignity, and turns human lives into sources of profit. As such, any establishment found to have been used as a venue for such activities must be held accountable in accordance with the law. It is also important to underscore that under existing laws, accountability extends beyond those directly managing day-to-day operations. Owners, incorporators, and those with legal and beneficial control over establishments may be held liable when their businesses are used as instruments of trafficking. The issuance of a closure order by the Pasig LGU reflects the government’s firm stance against all forms of exploitation. It also serves as a reminder that business permits and corporate structures do not shield anyone from liability when unlawful activities are involved. We urge all establishment owners and operators to ensure strict compliance with the law and to exercise diligence in the management of their businesses. The NBI remains committed to protecting victims, prosecuting offenders, and dismantling systems that enable human trafficking.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), conducted an entrapment operation at the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) – Main Office, Mandaluyong City, on October 10, 2025, resulting in the arrest of MARY JOCELYN BALUBAYAN y VERGARA for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code or (“Estafa”). The case stemmed from information received by the Department of Migrant Workers Operation and Surveillance Division (DMW-OSD) that Subject BALUBAYAN and her cohort, NIALMO A. LOVINA, have been victimizing Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) who were distressed and are eligible to claim assistance from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the DMW. Officials from DMW-OSD likewise alleged that the Subjects have been engaged in ambulant chasing (or ambulant soliciting/chasing) at the DMW office. According to information from the DMW-OSD, several complainants were enticed by Subjects BALUBAYAN and LOVINA to obtain a CERTIFICATE OF INDIGENCY from them, purportedly issued by Barangay Commonwealth in Quezon City. Complainants disclosed that Subjects demanded the amount of Php1,000 from the Php5,000 DSWD Cash Assistance and fifteen percent (15%) of the DMW Assistance of Php50,000 in exchange for the Certificate of Indigency. Initial investigation revealed that the reported Barangay Certificates of Indigency were all falsified, indicating the same address for all four (4) claimants. Further verification with the specified Barangay disclosed that the certificates were indeed spurious. DMW officials were thus prompted to temporarily put the Complainants’ claims for the Action Fund on hold. Acting on the information, NBI-HTRAD agents planned and executed an entrapment operation in coordination with the DMW-OSD and the DMW Complainants on October 10, 2025, to arrest Subjects while actively engaging in their fraudulent operations. Agents proceeded to the DMW – Main Office, where a female individual, matching the description of one of the Subjects, approached the victims seated at a coffee shop located inside the DMW Ground Floor Lobby. After confirming the Subject’s identity and receiving the pre-arranged signal—indicating that the marked money had been given—NBI-HTRAD agents approached and placed the Subject under arrest. The Subject was identified as MARY JOCELYN BALUBAYAN y VERGARA. Subject BALUBAYAN was presented for inquest proceedings on October 11, 2025, while Subject LOVINA remains at large. The NBI reminds the public to be cautious of offers from unauthorized individuals and report suspicious transactions immediately.

Officials from DMW-OSD likewise alleged that the Subjects have been engaged in ambulant chasing (or ambulant soliciting/chasing) at the DMW office. The accused is identified as Algaber Said alias Abu Talha, a member of the Abu Sayaff Group (ASG) under the command and leadership of Khadaffi Janjalani. On March 20, 2000, Said was among the 50 armed ASG group who kidnapped the 51 kids at the Tumahubong Elementary School and Claret High School both located in Barangay Tumahubong, Sumisip, Basilan Province. They were held captive by the ASG for more than three (3) months until their release on June 17, 2000 in Jolo, Sulu. One of the kidnapped victims successfully escaped from the band and sought government protection. Close and relentless coordination among government authorities resulted to a major breakthrough when on November 25, 2012 received reliable information that Said was sighted in Zamboanga City. It was learned that he was to meet a friend in a shopping mall in downtown Zamboanga City on November 27, 2012. Acting with dispatch, NBI Western Mindanao Regional Office (WEMRO) operatives contacted AFP and PNP-SAF authorities for augmentation. At 11 a.m., of said date NBI operatives joined by AFP and PNP elements rushed to the shopping mall in downtown Zamboanga City. One of the kidnap victims who was with NBI team identified Said. Then and there, NBI operatives closed-in and apprehended Said. He offered no resistance. Subsequently, he was brought to the NBI-WEMRO office in Zamboanga City where he was temporarily held. That night, NBI agents brought him to the NBI main office in Manila for detention.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 6, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) and the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) have intensified operations against human trafficking in the country. They successfully rescued ten victims of human trafficking, nine of whom were minors, in Sual, Pangasinan. The joint team arrested two Chinese nationals, identified as ZHONGGANG QUI and WENWEN QUI, along with three Filipinos: ANGIELYN V. RMAIREZ, MARICHELLE C. AMBROSIO, and JAY R. AMOR. The arrested individuals have been charged with Qualified Trafficking under Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364 and R.A. No. 11862. They also face charges for violating R.A. No. 9231 (An Act Providing For The Elimination Of The Worst Forms Of Child Labor), R.A. No. 8550 (The Fisheries Code of the Philippines), and R.A. No. 12022 for Economic Sabotage. The operation was initiated based on an intelligence report regarding a Chinese national named Hou Shilian, who was allegedly employing underage workers and harboring undocumented foreign nationals in his compound in Barangay Baquioen, Sual, Pangasinan. A joint team from the NBI-CCD and NBI-STF carried out surveillance, casing, and reconnaissance in the area, which confirmed the accuracy of the information. On May 1, 2025, the agents of NBI-CCD and NBI-STF, together with the agents from NBI-ALDO and local social welfare representatives, proceeded to the target compound in Sual, Pangasinan, which resulted in the rescue of the minor victims in the act of actively working and/or residing within the compound. According to the victims, several of them were recruited from Northern Samar and were subjected to forced labor, debt bondage, and threats involving the use of firearms. The victims were also engaged in hazardous labor, including hauling fish feed and tending to offshore cages in Lingayen Gulf. Meanwhile, the employees of the compound admitted that they were acting under the instructions of the two arrested Chinese nationals, who were directly managing operations and employing minors. During the operation, it was discovered that two of the rescued minor victims are pregnant by their live-in partners, who are 23 and 22 years old, respectively. This raises grounds for prosecution under statutory rape laws. Additionally, the agents found that the fish pen operations were primarily owned and controlled by Chinese nationals. Furthermore, the unregulated fish pens pose significant risks to the environment and public utilities. The individuals who were arrested were presented for inquest proceedings regarding these violations. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CCD and NBI-STF agents for their relentless efforts, which led to the arrest of the subjects, and assured the public that the NBI will continue its operation against all forms of criminality.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 18, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS SURROGACY CLINIC EXEC IN PAMPANGA The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), arrested an officer-in-charge of a surrogacy clinic in Mandaluyong City pursuant to a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court (RTC), Branch 52, in Guagua, Pampanga. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by a former surrogate mother against a surrogacy agency. The complainant alleged that the agency recruited financially disadvantaged women to serve as surrogate mothers for intended parents under agreements whose terms and conditions were allegedly not fully explained or disclosed to them. It was further alleged that the agency facilitated the transfer of children to prospective adoptive parents in exchange for monetary consideration. The RTC, Branch 52, Guagua, Pampanga, subsequently issued Warrants of Arrest against the Subject, who is one of the officers-in-charge of the surrogacy clinic, and her husband in connection with the complaint. The NBI-HTRAD received information from the staff of the “Raffy Tulfo in Action” public affairs show that the Subject had expressed her intention to surrender voluntarily to the authorities. Acting on the information, HTRAD operatives proceeded to Mandaluyong City to facilitate her voluntary surrender and implement the Warrant of Arrest. Upon coordinating with the Subject and the concerned parties, the operatives located her at the designated area in Mandaluyong City and duly served the Warrant of Arrest. She was thereafter placed under arrest. Following her arrest, Subject was informed of her constitutional rights and brought to the appropriate NBI office for documentation, booking, and proper disposition. NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag reiterated the Bureau’s commitment to enforcing the law, protecting individuals who may be vulnerable to manipulation, and ensuring that all persons involved in criminal proceedings are afforded their rights under the law. https://www.facebook.com/reel/2349606499114981

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 17, 2022 NBI ARRESTS TWO FOR MURDER AND FRUSTRATED MURDER The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of NORLITO RAMOS y CORDERO by the NBI-MIMAROPA in Pinamalayan, Oriental Mindoro for Murder and Frustrated Murder. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Ramos who alleged that he was stabbed by the Subject in the back multiple times. Subject also stabbed complainant’s wife which led to her untimely death. According to Complainant, in the afternoon of October 13, 2022, while he was watching television, he heard his dogs barking continuously so he went outside and saw a man standing outside their gate, whom later identified as Subject Ramos. Complainant alleged that Subject Ramos was borrowing money from him but the former refused. While walking towards his house, Subject Ramos suddenly stabbed Complainant causing the latter to fall to ground. The wife of Complainant saw what happened and thus screamed for help. Subject Ramos thereafter attacked Complainant’s wife to death then went back to Complainant to take the latter’s wallet. Unknown to Subject Ramos, the youngest daughter of the two (2) victims witnessed the stabbing. Agents of NBI-MIMAROPA questioned Subject Ramos and he outrightly denied his involvement in the incident. He told the investigating agents that on October 13, 2022, he was at his work in the Legislative Building of the Municipality of Socorro, and even came home late because he had to work overtime. Agents of NBI-MIMAROPA verified Subject’s claim with his employer and it was revealed that Subject did not come to work on October 13, 2021. The next day, NBI-MIMAROPA operatives proceeded again to the address of Subject Ramos. This time, they saw the latter and his family who are about to abscond. Subject Ramos was invited to the NBI-MIMAROPA office for further questioning. The victim who survived the attack immediately proceeded to the office of NBI-MIMAROPA after the treatment of his stabbed wounds and there positively identified Subject Ramos as the one who attacked him and his wife. At this juncture, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA immediately placed Subject Ramos under arrest. Subject Ramos was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor on October 21, 2022 for Murder and Frustrated Murder. Consequently, the Prosecutor’s Office filed the corresponding Information against the Subject for the said offenses.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } STRENGTHENING ‘FRIENDLY COOPERATIVE RELATIONS’: ATTY. MATIBAG WELCOMES CHINESE LAW ENFORCEMENT EXECS TO NBI National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Atty. Melvin Matibag welcomed a Chinese law enforcement delegation on August 4, 2026, at the NBI Headquarters Conference Hall in Pasay City. The delegation, led by Mr. Wang Xizhang, represented the Fujian Provincial Public Safety Department of China’s Ministry of Public Security, which was in Manila last week for a three-day working visit. The courtesy visit aims to strengthen the NBI’s international partnerships with neighboring countries to foster closer collaboration on shared issues. “The challenges facing law enforcement today are complex and multidimensional as technology continues to evolve at an unprecedented pace. As crimes, including cyber-enabled offenses and online gambling, have crossed geographical boundaries, we must collaborate with foreign law enforcement bodies because shared challenges require strengthened exchanges and cooperation,” Atty. Matibag said, adding that law enforcement cooperation between neighbors is the sine qua non of regional peace and order. Atty. Matibag then reaffirmed the Bureau’s dedication to enhancing cooperation that will promote regional peace, security, and effective law enforcement. He anticipates that the visit will strengthen friendly and collaborative ties between Beijing and Manila’s law enforcement agencies. The NBI chief has committed to organizing meetings, discussions, and visits for Chinese law enforcement officials with appropriate NBI divisions. To enhance cooperation and coordination, the visit underscores the need for law enforcement exchanges and interactions, including information sharing on transnational crimes such as online fraud; working-level expert exchanges; and intelligence sharing on priority crimes. The Chinese delegation also wishes to step up collaboration to protect its nationals in the Philippines and to improve the investigation of criminal elements who have exploited differences between the legal systems of China and the Philippines to evade prosecution.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 17, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) – Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) and the NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO), under the guidance and supervision of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested APRIL RODRIGUEZ FERNANDO in Taytay, Rizal for violation of Article 40(g) in relation to Art. 23(a)(7) of R.A. No. 7394, otherwise known as the “Consumer Act of the Philippines.” The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the authorized representative of Universal Robina Corporation (URC) regarding expired/adulterated URC food products that were being sold at a store and being kept at a warehouse in Taytay, Rizal. Subsequent surveillance and test-buy operations conducted confirmed the veracity of the information. On October 09, 2025, NBI-LAGDO, augmented by NBI-RIZDO, implemented a Search Warrant at a warehouse located in Brgy. Dolores, Taytay, Rizal. After which, an entrapment operation ensued at AIDEN LOUISE STORE, resulting in the arrest of Subject FERNANDO, who was caught in flagrante delicto of selling the products. Following the Subject’s arrest, another implementation of Search Warrant was conducted at the said store, which resulted in the seizure of two (2) truckloads of expired/adulterated URC products. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal on October 10, 2025. Director Santiago commended the joint operatives of LAGDO and RIZDO for acting swiftly, as these food products, which are popular among children, pose serious health hazards to the consuming public.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI- Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) have seized two hundred twenty two (222) pieces of brake shoe bearing the trademark “MAKOTO” in two cities in Cebu. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by Ms. Arabelle Lee, authorized representative of Mitsukoshi Motorcycle Philippines Inc. against LUIS R. TAN and occupants of TWIN MOTORCYCLE ACCESSORIES AND GROCERIES located at 243 A. Del Rosario St., Mantuyong, Mandaue City, Cebu, as well the owner and/or proprietor of TY RACING located at Benedicto Building, D. Jakosalem St., Cebu City. According to Ms. Lee, for the past few months, the sales of “Makoto” have dramatically plummeted due to the proliferation of counterfeit brake shoe bearing the “Makoto” trademark in the local market. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 5, 2022 NBI JOINS LAUNCHING OF INTER-AGENCY TASK FORCE ON ANTI-ILLEGAL REAL ESTATE PRACTICES The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has joined the launching of the newly-created Inter-Agency Task Force (IATF) on Anti-Illegal Real Estate Practices. Created under Joint Circular (JMC) No. 1, series of 2021, the primary aim of the TF is to put a stop on illegal Real Estate Practices committed by unscrupulous scammers, fly by night developers, unregistered real estate brokers and other individuals whose objective is to defraud unsuspecting buyers of their hard-earned money. The launching of the Task Force was held last June 17, 2022 at the Boardroom of the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development in Quezon City. The JMC is the result of joint effort among member agencies namely DHSUD, Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG), Department of Environmental and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Justice (DOJ), Land Registration Authority (LRA), Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), and Philippine National Police (PNP). body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) have arrested ten (10) individuals in two (2) separate operations for human trafficking and large scale illegal recruitment respectively. On March 20, 2017, NBI-AHTRAD operatives arrested three (3) Subjects, namely: DANICA BUCALING y DATUIN, MARY ANN BUAN y LLOSE, and JAYVY BADEO y LOPEZ for human trafficking. Based on a formal referral from the Immigrations and Customs Enforcement – U.S. Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-USHSI) concerning a person who was offering under-aged Filipino girls for sexually-related shows online in exchange for certain amounts payable through money remittance centers, the NBI-AHTRAD conducted an entrapment and rescue operation on the aforementioned date in Taguig City. In coordination with the PNP and with the assistance of City Social Welfare of Taguig City, the operation resulted in the rescue of three (3) children and the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Charges for violation of R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) and R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. In a subsequent operation on March 22, 2017, seven (7) Subjects, namely: MARIE L. ALVAREZ, MERCY G. GALEDO, CRISANTO H. DIROY, JOEL T. GALLEZO, KRISTINE L. FERNANDEZ, CLAUDIA L. ARNENTE, and RAMONA M. CASTRO were arrested in Pasay City for large scale illegal recruitment. Subjects, using an unlicensed agency named KAIRUS HUMAN RESOURCES, were recruiting applicants for overseas employment to work as food processors in Japan. In order to lure more applicants, Subjects were demanding from each applicant discounted amount of down payment for visa processing to Japan. As soon as their visas are released, the remaining balance will be collected. The total amount of Php 240,750.00 has already been received by the Subjects from the Complainants. In almost two (2) years of waiting, Complainants made constant follow up with Subjects regarding the release of their working visas in Japan but Subjects could not provide them positive result. Complainants were able to verify from the POEA that Subjects are not licensed and authorized to deploy workers for employment abroad and that the name of the agency, KAIRUS HUMAN RESOURCES, whom the Subjects were representing is also not licensed by the POEA. Furthermore, it was found out that one of the Subjects, MERCY GAMBOA GALLEDO, has several outstanding Warrant of Arrest for illegal recruitment and estafa. This prompted the Complainants to go to NBI-AHTRAD to seek assistance. The entrapment operation which took place in Pasay City resulted in the arrest of the seven (7) Subjects who were at that time executing their illegal recruitment activities. Charges for violation of R.A. 8042 (Syndicated and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment) and Estafa were filed against the seven (7) Subjects.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) have arrested five (5) individuals for illegal possession, collecting or cutting and selling various species of timbers in Sultan Kudarat. On February 9, 2017 DENR USEC Arturo T. Valdez, Head of the Department of Environmental Crime Task Force (NAECTF) requested the NBI to provide the necessary manpower complement during the enforcement operations to stop the rampant illegal logging activities in Region 12, covering the Provinces of Sultan Kudarat, Sarangani and South Cotabato. In order to coordinate and plan the implementation of the said request, NBI-ENCD operatives proceeded to General Santos City to linked-up with the Office of the Regional Director of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Region 12 and NBI Koronadal City. While thereat, it was revealed that there were illegal activities of cutting naturally-grown trees, gathering and collecting the square timber logs without the necessary license perpetrated by some establishments in Sultan Kudarat. Acting on the intelligence information, on February 24, 2017, the NBI environmental task force conducted surveillance and verification. Verification conducted revealed that establishments Boyet Furniture Shop, Oriel Upholstery and Furniture Shop, JP Furniture Shop, VN furniture Shop, and Shejay Furniture Shop had been operating without the necessary permit secured from the DENR and hence, not paying taxes. Owners of the aforementioned establishments namely VIVENCIO NECESITO SR. y ESCARO (owner of (VN Furniture Shop), RAMEL CASTRACION y CASTROVERDE (owner of Boyet furniture Shop), SANNY ORIEL y UNTAY (owner of Oriel Upholstery and Furniture), JERRY PAGLOMUTAN y GASPAR (owner of JP Furniture), and WIFREDO PABLEO JR. y MATOS (owner of Shejay Furniture Shop) were arrested after failure to present necessary DENR permits. Seized at the said establishments were timbers of various species such as Mariapa, Dao, Lamud, Lauan, Mahogany, Gmelina, Falcata, Yakal, Narra, Lavan, Ipil-Ipil, and Guijo. The amount of seized timbers totaled Php 623, 102.85. Seized items were duly turned over to the Office of the DENR-Kalamansig, Sultan Kudarat. Subjects were brought to NBI-Region 12 Office, Koronadal City for the booking procedures. Certification dated March 1, 2017 issued by Mr. Badjury H. Mustapha Cenro officer stated that aforementioned establishments have no clearance to operate wood processing from the DENR, no lumber dealer permit and log supply contract. Charges for violation of Executive Order No. 277 (Amending Section 28 of Presidential Decree No. 705, as amended, otherwise known as the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines), R.A. 460 of 1950 (Illegal Possession of Forest Products Act), and Section 7 (a) of R.A. 9175 (Chainsaw Act of 2002) were filed against the Subjects.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said Illegal Detention charges have been filed against officials and security personnel of a condominium tower in Quezon City for illegally confining and restricting three (3) nurses in their condominium unit. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as MEL TOSCO (Property Manager/Administrative Head of Victoria Towers Condominium), NAPOLEON BRIÑAS (Head, Security Management of San Jose Builders Inc.), ATTY. JERICH J. JUCABAN (Vice-President, SJBI), Security Guard SADAT MACABANDING , three (3) JOHN DOES and two (2) JANE DOES , and the assigned security guards of Victoria Towers Condominium (VTC), Quezon City. OIC Distor said on June 29, 2020, NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) received a complaint from three (3) individuals through their counsels relative to their illegal confinement and restriction of complainants in their condominium unit for more than three (3) days, from June 22, 2020 up to present by the management and security of VTC. OIC Distor added that complainants alleged that Subjects had been illegally confining and restricting them in their condominium unit despite the fact that they have already presented to Subjects their medical clearances certifying that they are COVID cleared and thus, fit to return to work. After verification of the complaint, OIC Distor added, NBI-SAU operatives hatched an operation to rescue the complainants. Upon arrival at the condominium tower, NBI-SAU operatives were met by MEL TOSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, and ATTY. NENETH DE PADUA, Legal Officer of SJBI. Despite explanation by the NBI operatives, specifically of the existence of the medical certificates issued to complainants who were being continuously detained at their unit, MEL TOSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, and ATTY. NENETH DE PADUA refused to free the complainants on the ground that they are still awaiting clearance from the Barangay. Considering the sensitivity of the issue, the matter was discussed privately in the conference room of VTC and agreed to invite Brgy. Chairman Cecilia Tiamson to shed light on the matter. Brgy Chairperson Tiamzon explained that the only role of the barangay in handling COVID patients and suspected patients is only monitoring and giving them assistance as to their basic needs and that they could not issue health clearance as they respect clearances issued by Infectious Control Consultants. After the NBI-SAU operatives presented the clearances issued by the ICC, Subjects MEL TOSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, and ATTY. DE PADUA called ATTY. JERICH JUCABAN thru the loudspeaker but they still refused to release the complainants, thus continue to commit violation of laws. It was then that the NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the 9 th Floor to rescue the complainants. A lady guard stationed at the hallway is guarding the movement of complainants. Subject MEL TOSCO was apprised of his constitutional rights under the circumstances and was placed under arrest. NAPOLEON BRIÑAS managed to flee from the condominium tower. The Operatives looked for him but to no avail. On the other hand, despite informing the operatives that ATTY. JUCABAN is coming over, did not show up. Subject MEL TOSCO was brought to NBI-SAU office for the proper booking procedures. The lady guard and the Security-In-Charge executed their statements that they were merely following orders from the condominium officials MEL TOSCO and NAPOLEON BRIÑAS. Orders, which they believed, are legal. Serious Illegal Detention charges under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended and Quezon City Executive Order No. 26 s.2020 (Protection of COVID-19 patients/frontliners from any kind of discrimination) were filed against MEL TOSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, ATTY. JERICH J, JUCUBAN, and security guard SADAT MACABANDING, three (3) John Does and two (2) Jane Does.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 23, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR INVESTMENT FRAUD The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said that operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NCR) arrested an individual in Kawit, Cavite for investment fraud. NBI Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the Subject as MARY ANN TEE HERNANDEZ. Director DISTOR said the case stemmed from a complaint filed by Spouses against the Subject on the alleged investment scam. Subject is continuously defrauding the complainant by soliciting and receiving money for investment in her non-existent business. Investigation disclosed that in 2019, Subject sent a personal message to complainant on Facebook (FB) messenger offering a “rare opportunity” to diversify complainant funds. Subject even sent personal messages to prove the legitimacy of her business. She represented herself to the complainant as the owner of Frontier Freight Forwarders (Frontier), a legitimate business existing for six (6) years in Pasay City. That, Frontier handles imports and exports, and arranges freights for shippers and importers; and that she gives two (2) percent interest for funds she receives. On February 09, 2019, Complainant met the Subject in Kawit to discuss the business proposal of a monthly return of 2% on the amount of money that complainant will invest. Relying in good faith and promises of Subject, Complainant accepted the offer and agreed to give the money in several tranches. Complainant’s money invested in the Subject totaled P16,282,631.00 as of April 2022 and if unpaid interests for 2022 promised by the Subject were to be included, the amount will total Php17,837,418.00. Subject paid the return on investment in April 2020, however, payments of return became irregular even with continuous follow- up of Complainant. Verification with government agencies showed negative results for Frontier Freight Forwarders. Convinced that they are defrauded, Complainant sought the help of NBI. They took the chance since the Subject is still contacting them for additional funds. Complainant then informed Subject that her brother was inquiring about the business. Subject then solicited money from the Complainant’s brother and continued to convince to invest money with the Subject’s business. Complainant then reported the matter to the NBI-NCR which then set up an entrapment operation. Thus, on June 9, 2022, NBI operatives and the poseur investor (complainant’s brother) proceeded to the agreed meeting place in Kawit, Cavite. Subject arrived and demanded the money demanded as initial investment. Immediately after receiving the marked money, the operatives introduced themselves and declared the purpose of their presence. Subject was arrested and was later presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Imus Cavite for Estafa under Art. 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 otherwise known as the “The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.”
