body: PRESS STATEMENT January 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to eliminate red tape in the Bureau, the joint operatives of NBI – Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) and NBI – Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrests four (4) NBI employees under the Information and Communication Technology Division (NBI-ICTD), who conspired with each other for Direct Bribery under Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC); Sections 3(b) and (e) of R.A. No. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act); Section 7(d) of R.A. No. 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees); and Section 21(c) and (h) of R.A. No. 11032 (Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The joint operatives also arrested seven (7) fixers outside the vicinity of the NBI Clearance Center for violation of Section 21(c), (g), and (h) of R.A. No. 11032 (Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018) in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). According to Director Santiago, the operation stemmed from an information, alleging that a certain NBI employee is in collusion with fixers in the issuance of NBI Clearance Certificates. The information also revealed that the said NBI employee was facilitating the expedite of the NBI clearance applications in exchange for a fee ranging from Php800.00 – Php2,000.00. Acting on the information, NBI-CCD immediately conducted covert inquiries and verification, which confirmed the veracity of the information. Thus, on January 6, 2025, joint operatives of NBI-CCD and NBI-STF proceeded to the NBI Clearance Center for the entrapment operation, which resulted in the arrest of four (4) NBI employees in the act of violating the above-stated laws and the arrest of seven (7) fixers outside the vicinity of the NBI Clearance Center. On January 7, 2025, the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice (DOJ), Padre Faura, Taft Avenue, Manila. Director Santiago emphasized that there is no place for corrupt practices in the NBI under his leadership and warned that he will be relentless in pursuing those individuals who will violate the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act Law.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT March 28, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES SECOND MINOR VICTIM OF ONLINE SEXUAL EXPLOITATION IN BATANGAS FOLLOW-UP OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 25, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) successfully rescued another minor victim of Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) in a follow-up operation in Tanauan, Batangas. The rescue was initiated following a previous successful NBI-VAWCD operation that resulted in the arrest of a facilitator and the rescue of an initial victim. Information provided by the first survivor led the NBI-VAWCD to the identity of the second minor being exploited by the same facilitator. In a coordinated effort with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of Tanauan, the Philippine National Police (PNP), and the Department of Education (DepEd), NBI agents conducted the rescue at a local public high school. With the assistance of the victim’s class adviser, the minor was identified and safely taken into protective custody. She has since been turned over to the CSWD for trauma-informed intervention and support. Evidence gathered from the minor-victims has led to additional charges against the Subject for violations of Republic Act No. 11930, also known as the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act, and Republic Act No. 9208, the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag praised the NBI-VAWCD for their relentless efforts that culminated in the successful rescue of the minor victim from trafficking. He highlighted that this operation signifies the Bureau’s commitment to pursuing every lead, emphasizing that the NBI will not stop at the initial arrest but will continue its operations until every victim is rescued and brought to safety. Director Matibag assured the public that the NBI will continue to work tirelessly to prevent further victimization and bring perpetrators to justice, calling for community support and vigilance in the collective fight against human trafficking. #NBIServes

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the arrest of an individual in Manila for swindling. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as KIRK GABRIEL BAUZA DAVID a.k.a. SARAH CRUZ (Facebook name). OIC Distor said that the victim appeared before the NBI- Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) to complain about the modus operandi of a certain “SARAH CRUZ”. The complainant narrated through his Sworn Statement that subject Sarah Cruz ordered from him through Facebook two (2) airsoft guns and one (1) Hard Case Scope in three (3) separate transactions. In the first transaction, the subject communicated with the complainant through Facebook Messenger ordering an EC843 airsoft gun with selling price of Php 17,350.00. As proof of payment, the subject sent through FB Messenger the screen shot of the online money transfer. Upon seeing the FB Messenger chat message that the payment has already been made, the complainant sent the airsoft gun to the subject at Tondo General Hospital (TGH) as the place of delivery via Lalamove. The modus operandi of the subject continued up to 2nd and 3rd transactions sending to the complainant the proof of payment through FB Messenger. When complainant checked his bank statement, he discovered that the three previous money transfers of Sarah were not credited to his bank account. Believing that the complainant is unaware of his modus operandi, Subject Sarah Cruz ordered again for the fourth time from the complainant a John Wick Xcortech and sent to him through FB Messenger the proof of payment. The next day Subject Sarah Cruz again ordered the same item and sent to the complainant another proof of payment. The complainant sought the help of the NBI-SOG and the entrapment operation was set up . On June 11, 2020, the two (2) orders of Subject Sarah Cruz were sent to TGH through a courier. NBI-SOG operatives proceeded to TGH and saw the courier handing over the items to a male individual. The operatives then arrested the male individual that was later identified as KIRK GABRIEL BAUZA DAVID. Recovered from him were two (2) John Wick Xcortech, one (2) Yamaha NMAX motorcycle, a cellular phone, Driver’s License and Lazada I.D. The operatives then instructed the driver of the delivery service company to dial the number of Subject Sarah Cruz after which the recovered cellphone from Kirk Gabriel Bauza David rang, positively identifying that Sarah and Kirk are one and the same person. Subject Kirk was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for violation of Article 315 (Swindling) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) in relation to R.A. 10175, otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has arrested an Iranian national accused of raping a 16-year old girl. The NBI said that on July 01, 2015, a complaint was filed by the victim, Keith Exequiel Holgado, against a certain MILAD who was later identified as REZA SABERMUGHADDAM for Rape under Art. 266 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 7610. Initial medico-genetalia examination result conducted by the NBI Medico-Legal Division showed that an extra-genital physical injuries were noted on the body of the victim at the time of the examination, among others. The NBI said that upon completion of the necessary documents and coordination, the NBI – Anti Organized Transnational Crimes Division 9NBI-AOTCD) proceeded to the NAAB Persian Restaurant located along Anaheim Libertad street in Mandaluyong City where Subject REZA SABERMUGHADDAM was waiting for Keith Holgado to arrive. As soon as the victim arrived and greeted the Subject, he was approached by the operatives and informed him of the cause of his arrest and his Constitutional rights. Subject was later brought to the NBI Head office for the usual standard operating procedures of fingerprinting and medical examination, among others.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT September 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On August 30, 2025, the Clark Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (CRK-IATFAID) composed of the PDEA, BOC, PNP, and NBI-PAMDO, under the supervision of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), conducted a controlled delivery operation which resulted in the arrest of DEXTER DESQUITADO and his driver, MACARIO GALDONES BIAG, for violation of Republic Act No. 9165 otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.” The operation stemmed from a drug interdiction conducted on August 28, 2025 in a courier warehouse inside Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga, wherein CRK-IATFAID intercepted 11.4 kilograms of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride (Shabu) with an estimated market value of more or less Php75,072,000.00. The illegal drugs were concealed inside a package consigned to one GUINTOROMMEL of San Isidro, Cainta, Rizal. Subsequent coordination with the Bureau of Customs revealed that a certain “DEXTER” had communicated on behalf of the consignee and was scheduled to claim the subject package on August 30, 2025. Accordingly, the task force hatched a controlled delivery operation. At around 5:27 P.M. of the same date, DESQUITADO and his driver BIAG arrived in a white Nissan van. Both subjects were immediately placed under arrest after claiming the package and while about to load the package into their vehicle. The arrested individuals are now under the custody of the PDEA for proper documentation and filing of charges.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT April 08, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation – Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested the co-accused of APOLLO C. QUIBOLOY identified as CRESENTE CANADA, PAULENE CANADA, SYLVIA CEMAÑES, JACKIELYN W. ROY, and INGRID C. CANADA in Davao City for Other Acts of Child Abuse under Section 10(A) of R.A. 7610. On March 14, 2024, RTC Branch 12 of Davao City issued a Warrant of Arrest against Apollo C. Quiboloy and the above arrested individuals. On April 3, 2024, Acting on the said Warrant of Arrest, NBI-SEMRO divided into three (3) groups and in joint operations with PNP Regional Office XI, Davao City, Davao City Police Office (DCPO), CIDG-XI, Davao City, and PNP-Regional Intelligence Unit-XI, Davao City, implemented the Warrant of Arrest in three (3) locations in Davao City where Quiboloy reportedly can be found. One of the three (3) teams proceeded to Barangay Tamayong, Calinan, Davao City where Subject Cresente was found and arrested. Subject Cresente was brought to the NBI-SEMRO office for standard booking procedure. An hour after the arrest of Cresente, Subjects Paulene and Sylvia who were also co-accused of Apollo Quiboloy, appeared before the NBI-SEMRO office in Davao City and voluntarily surrendered. While Subjects Jackielyn and Ingrid also appeared before the NBI-SEMRO office and surrendered themselves voluntarily on April 4, 2024. The five (5) subjects posted bail for their temporary liberty, which was granted by the court. During the implementation of the Warrant of Arrest, Apollo Quiboloy was nowhere to be found in the areas subject of the warrant. The NBI assured the public that it will not stop tracking Quiboloy until justice is served.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 01, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) with the NBI – Intellectual Property Rights Division (IPRD), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), enforced three (3) Search Warrants at a location in San Nicolas, City of Manila, for violation of Section 155, in relation to Section 170, of Republic Act 8293 or the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. Orion Support Incorporated (OSI) filed a complaint against SUGARLUCKYHALL.SHOP, COOLFANCY.SHOP, FASHIONSHE.SHOP, BEA SHE, and/or JIAN DIN LI, owners/operators/occupants of the location in San Nicolas, Manila, for storing, selling, and distributing counterfeit products bearing the KENVUE, GALDERMA, and BEIERSDORF HOLDINGS S.A. trademarks. On March 24, 2025, armed with three (3) Search Warrants, NBI Agents were able to seize Eight Thousand Eight Hundred and Eighty-nine (18,889) various counterfeit products (lotion, sunblock, facial cream, cologne, facial cleanser, liquid soap, etc.) of “Nivea”, “Johnson’s Baby”, “Aveeno”, “Aveeno Baby”, “Cetaphil”, and various business documents, receipts, Lazada parcel tags, and other pieces of evidence with an estimated worth of Fifteen Million Pesos (Php15,000,000.00). Appropriate criminal charges will be filed once all requisite documents have been completed and validated. Director Santiago lauded the operatives of NBI-NCR for successfully implementing said warrants and reminded the public to refrain from patronizing counterfeit products.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) proudly announces and welcomes its new leader , ATTY. ANGELITO DLP MAGNO. With the Malacañang’s acceptance of former Director Jaime B. Santiago’s irrevocable resignation, Director Magno now serves as the Officer-in-Charge of the NBI. Director Magno is a career officer, a seasoned investigator who has devoted more than thirty-three (33) years of service to the Bureau, beginning as a project worker in 1991, he steadily rose through the ranks as Special Investigator, Investigation Agent, Head Agent, Regional Director, to Assistant Director, prior to his designation as Officer-in-Charge. His progression through every level of responsibility has equipped him with full spectrum of Investigative, operational, and managerial skills necessary to lead the NBI. Over the course of his career, Director Magno has held some of the Bureau’s most crucial assignments. As Chief of the Special Action Unit, he led high-profile operations, including the pursuit and arrest of major fugitives. As Regional Director in Regions III, I, IV-A, and X, he managed wide jurisdiction in Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, refining his ability to oversee complex Investigations and large personnel complements. At the executive level, he successively led the Regional Operations Service, Investigative Service, Information and Communication Technology Service, and Legal Service, demonstrating both versatility and competence in handling the Bureau`s most critical functions. Under his leadership, the Bureau achieved major milestones, among them the interception of P3.8 billion worth of illegal drugs in Pampanga, the successful pursuit of the Degamo-Teves murder cases, the crackdown on falsified civil registry documents used by foreign syndicates, the dismantling of the Socorro Bayanihan child exploitation network, and the Investigation into the MT Princess Empress oil spill which held liable both government officials and private corporations. His earlier assignments at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) also underscored his operational depth, where he supervised interdiction against human trafficking, investigated terrorism-related threats, and coordinated closely with other security agencies. Director Magno embodies the qualities of an ideal NBI Director: integrity, competence, operational credibility, and proven leadership across all levels of the Bureau. His extensive service record, breadth of experience, and tested judgment uniquely position him to lead the NBI as the principal Investigative arm of the Department of Justice and as a strong partner of the government in advancing justice, law enforcement, and institutional modernization. Director Magno anchors his leadership on the core principles of the Bureau: Nobility, Bravery and Integrity guided with meritocracy, skill, teamwork, and accountability. As an insider-leader, it is his vision to renew the esprits de corps within the institution, to preserve the institutional knowledge, and reinforce the investigative capacity of the Bureau in order to ensure the public of a quality service. He urged all NBI personnel to consistently abide by the law and make ethical decisions. He reminded them that they can demonstrate their loyalty to the country through sincere and genuine service. He is confident that the men and women of the NBI are capable of rebuilding public trust in the government. His commitment to serving the public with integrity, competence and loyalty is his way of expressing his sincerest gratitude to President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for trusting him to lead the NBI and his heartfelt thanks to the former Department of Justice Secretary, now current Ombudsman, Jesus Crispin Remulla , for providing him the opportunity to continue serving the public as the Officer-in-Charge of this premier institution.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the government’s drive to fight all forms of criminality, the National Bureau of Investigation – Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID), under the supervision of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested JENNY MACANAS SAPAD a.k.a. “SHIELA CASTILLO” and “ANGEL ROXAS y SOTERO” in Tarlac City for Syndicated Estafa through Falsification of Public Documents in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), violations of Article 178 (Use of Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name) and Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority and Official Function) under the Revised Penal Code (RPC). The operation stemmed from a complaint alleging that a certain “Sheila Naransa Castillo”, who represented herself as a lawyer, deceived the complainant into giving Php5,000,000.00 in exchange for a favorable court resolution regarding a parcel of land. The Complainant was an interested party and was guaranteed to be the awardee of the property. To support her claims, Subject presented the complainant with fake receipts and documents signed by a Judge and a clerk of Court of the Regional Trial Courts (RTCs) of Tarlac and Camiling. This was done to give the impression that Subject and her cohorts had legitimate transactions with various government agencies and courts. Initial investigation revealed that the Subject’s name is not listed on the official websites of the Supreme Court Office of the Bar Confidant and the Integrated Bar of the Philippines as a lawyer. After confirming the illegal activities of the Subject and her associates, an entrapment operation was planned. Although the initial meeting was set to take place in the Hall of Justice in Tarlac, the Subject instructed the complainant to meet her in a fast-food chain in Tarlac City instead. Consequently, NBI-CRID Agents proceeded to the new location and conducted the entrapment operation, resulting in the arrest of the Subject. During the operation, an identification card from bearing the name “ANGEL ROXAS y SOTERO” was confiscated from the Subject. During the standard booking procedure, Subject wrote the name “JENNY MACANAS SAPAD” on the booking sheet. She was later presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Furthermore, Subject Sapad’s cohorts were also charged with Syndicated Estafa through Falsification of Public Documents in relation to R.A. No. 10175. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) commended the Agents of NBI-CRID for the successful operation that led to the arrest of the Subject.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against environmental crimes, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) have arrested four (4) individuals for illegal occupation of foreshore land in Botolan, Zambales. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as LOVELIAN REYES BOOL, RENATO MONSALUD y BOOL, MARCELINO GUSTERO MAÑOSA JR., and APOLLO TABIOS CONSTANTINO. Subjects were arrested in an operation which emanated from a report alleging occupation of foreshore land by Sunrise Paradise Resort in Botolan, Zambales. According to the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office, Iba, Zambales, the occupation of foreshore land of Sunrise Paradise Resort is illegal and despite the order to cease and desist from the on-going construction activities, Sunrise did not refrain from constructing and installing structures. NBI-EnCD operatives conducted surveillance and it was established that there are structures constructed in the seashore like floating cottages and a bridge made of steel. It was also noticed that there are on-going construction and installation of structures along the foreshore. On June 15, 2020, after coordinating with the local police, NBI operatives conducted the operation. Poseur-clients were allowed to take photos in the foreshore area and check the amenities of the resort. Poseur-clients also witnessed the on-going construction activities. When the NBI declared their authority, the workers were ordered to temporarily refrain from what they were currently doing. LOVELIAN REYES BOOL was in charge of the overall management of Sunrise Paradise Resort. LOVELIAN REYES BOOL, In charge of the over-all management of the resort and RENATO BOOL JR. presented some documents of the resort. When asked for Environment Compliance Certificate and Miscellaneous Lease Agreement/Foreshore Lease Agreement issued by DENR, they cannot produce any. MARCELINO GUSTERO MAÑOSA JR., the Engineer/Contractor, also showed up as he was in his regular routine of visiting and checking the overall progress of the project. Representatives from PENRO-Zambales and CENRO-Masinloc who arrived in the area to conduct ocular inspection for possible violations of the resort were able to ascertain that some of the structures built were already on the foreshore area, some were in the salvage area, and one structure was already offshore. With these, the NBI placed the 4 subjects under arrest for violations such as constructing a jetski port made of steel in the seashore, unauthorized obstruction of waterway by constructing a jetski port, and occupying foreshore land which under the law is owned by the state and an unclassified land of public domain. Charges for violations of RA 8550 (Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998), PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), and PD 705 as amended by EO 277 and RA 7161 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines) were filed against the subjects before the Department of Justice.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two (2) foreign nationals on 21 May 2025, in Parañaque City, for violation of Section 4 in relation to Section 19 of Republic Act No. 11900, otherwise known as the Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act. On 16 May 2025, the NBI-CCD received a tip about the illegal importation and online sale of unregistered products lacking BIR tax stamps and DTI registration. Thereafter, surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted on 19 May 2025, confirming the sale of the illicit products by foreign nationals in Metro Manila. An entrapment operation was launched on 21 May 2025. NBI-CCD Agents received the illicit products at a location in Pasay City, and upon confirmation of the unregistered status, arrested Subjects JONATHAN KHER JUN XIAN, a Singaporean, and NATKRITA PHAKHINNIPHAT, a Thai National. Subjects were booked, photographed, and medically examined at the NBI-CCD office. NBI-CCD recommends the filing of Section 4 in relation to Section 19 of the Republic Act No. 11900, otherwise known as the Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 22, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI, CICC, AND PCO CONDUCT JOINT PRESS CONFERENCE ON COMPLAINT INVOLVING ALLEGED ONLINE INCITEMENT AND CYBER-RELATED OFFENSES AGAINST ATTY. HAROLD RESPICIO PASAY CITY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), together with the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) represented by Undersecretary Aboy Paraiso, and the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) represented by Undersecretary Precious Hipolito-Castelo, conducted a joint press conference regarding the filing of a complaint affidavit against lawyer and social media personality Harold “Homer” Respicio, who also serves as Vice Mayor of Reina Mercedes, Isabela for alleged violations involving inciting to sedition, inciting to rebellion, unlawful use of means of publication and unlawful utterances, as well as possible cyber-related offenses. During the press conference, NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag said that CICC Undersecretary Paraiso executed the complaint affidavit with the support of the Presidential Communications Office and was subsequently transmitted to the NBI for appropriate investigation, case build-up, and evidentiary assessment prior to the filing of appropriate charges before the Department of Justice (DOJ). Atty. Melvin Matibag emphasized that Harold Respicio will be afforded due process and will be subpoenaed by the Bureau to explain his side and answer the allegations contained in the complaint affidavit. Undersecretary Paraiso thanked the NBI for its prompt action and coordination on the matter and stressed that the initiative forms part of the continuing collaboration between the CICC and the PCO in monitoring online activities, particularly social media statements and posts allegedly encouraging hatred against the government or inciting violence among the public. The officials clarified that the government’s actions are not intended to suppress freedom of expression or curtail legitimate dissent. However, they emphasized that freedom of speech carries corresponding responsibilities, and expressions that allegedly go beyond lawful and protected speech and may constitute incitement to violence, rebellion, sedition, or other cyber-related offenses may give rise to criminal liability under existing laws. The CICC further reminded the public to exercise responsibility and discernment in using social media platforms such as Facebook, Meta, TikTok, and other online channels, particularly in posting, sharing, and reacting to content online. Officials also underscored the importance of respecting the rights of others and maintaining responsible online conduct amid the growing influence of digital platforms in shaping public discourse. The NBI confirmed that all pieces of digital evidence related to the complaint have been preserved and are currently undergoing proper forensic and legal evaluation as part of the Bureau’s ongoing investigation. The Bureau likewise reiterated that every constitutional right carries a corresponding duty and responsibility, and that abuse of such rights in violation of existing laws may subject individuals to criminal and other legal consequences.

body: On May 3, 2021, operatives of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBIIAID) arrested ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD a.k.a. SANDRA LIPOLES for using passport with false information that Subject Mukamad was about to depart on May 3, 2021 for Saudi Arabia via Saudi Airlines but she was intercepted by an Immigration Officer and questioned her to verify her age and previous travels. According to Subject Mukamad, she is 30 years old, having been born on May 15, 1990. The Immigration Officer who conducted the interview did not allow the Subject to depart as she appears too young for a 30 years old. Subject was turned-over to NBI-IAID for further questioning and validation. Subject Mukamad told the NBI-IAID that she has already been to Saudi Arabia in 2017 using her current passport. However, the subject stated in the identification card voluntarily filled by her that her correct date of birth is May 5, 2000 and that her name true name ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD. Subject also revealed that she secured her passport from Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) in Cotabatao City. Subject Mukamad was then placed under arrest and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of Section 19 (b)(2) (Uses or attempts to use any passport which was secured in any way by reason of any false statements) of R.A. 8239 otherwise known as the Philippine Passport Act of 1996. · On May 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested FELMOR BALUGAY DUMAGAT for selling shabu. Subject was arrested in a buybust operation which stemmed from the information that Subject is selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro city. The operation yielded a net weight of around 1.1 grams of shabu with an estimated street value of Php 7,000. Subject is currently in jail for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). On May 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested VICENTE FAILON MARTINEZ in San Fernando City, La Union for Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim before the NBI-IRO regarding the crime committed against him by the subject. According to the victim-complainant, Subject Martinez was able to dupe him a total amount of Php 486,000.00. After sometime, the swindling elevated to extortion when Subject Martinez concocted a spurious Intelligence Report (IR) allegedly from NBI-IRO and NBI Manila. Using the same IR, Subject Martinez demanded P1 Million from victimcomplainant and forcing him and forced him to surrender his motor vehicle and was coerced to execute a blank Deed of Absolute Sale of a Motor Vehicle with a current Market Value of Php 500,000.00. Also, subject Martinez subsequently demanded an additional P500,000.00 to complete the P1Million by way of threat and coercion, threatening victimcomplainant he will be arrested by NBI-IRO and NBI Manila if he fails to produce the said amount at St. Jude Church, Poro, City of San Fernando, La Union. Thus, On May 4, 2021, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subject Martinez who was caught red-handed in the act of receiving the entrapment money from the victimcomplainant. Subject Martinez was then brought to the NBI-IRO Office and had undergone standard booking procedures. Documents are being prepared for the filing of Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority against the subject. On May 4, 2021, operatives of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBIIAID) arrested GRETCHEN ABLAN for using documents with falsified information. Subject was about to depart as a tourist for Dubai, UAE, when she was referred for secondary inspection after being discovered that she was previously off-loaded on April 22, 2021 for misrepresentation. During inspection, Subject claimed she was visiting her husband, JOEY DAMASCO MANALIGOD and showed copies of passport bio-page and UAE Visa sticker of MANALIGOD. With discrepancies and alteration in documents, different as reflected in the Central Query Support System of the Bureau of Immigration, Subject ABLAN admitted both verbally and in writing that she was not married and does not actually know MANALIGOD. She stated that all her documents for her May 4 flight were sent to her on May 3, 2021 by her recruiter through another person in Baclaran, Paranaque City. When confronted by the NBI regarding the COVID-19 Test Report issued by Dagupan Doctors Villaflor Memorial Hospital under her name, she said she had not undergone any COVID-19 test. Upon verification with said hospital on the COVID-19 of subject, the hospital declared that subject ABLAN did not appear in their list as one of their patients. Subject ABLAN was then placed under arrest for violation of Art. 172 in relation to Art. 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Use of Falsified Documents. Subject GRETCHEN ABLAN was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City. On May 4-7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized fake stamps and materials for making cigarettes with an estimated amount of Php 750 Million. Items were seized in Bacolod City during the implementation of BIR Mission Order for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). On May 5, 2021, operatives of NBI- Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested Spouses KONG, MA. ANGELICA y BELGA and KONG, XIANGCE (Chinese national) in Parañaque City for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report that a group of unidentified individuals are engaged in prostitution and human trafficking activities, particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims. According to the report, booking of women for sexual services is done through messaging in private group chats intended solely for Chinese Customers. The said group operates in NCR plus bubble area for easier transporting of women, as they are reportedly housed in an exclusive village in Parañaque City. Communication with the Subjects was established by sending a message through a contact given by the informant through mobile messaging app TELEGRAM as to the sexual services being offered. Subjects sent a ready list of prices of the sexual services being offered written in Chinese language. NBI-RIZDO requested the assistance of Destiny Rescue Philippines, an NGO which rescue children from sexual exploitation and human trafficking. With the help of a Chinese translator, NBI-RIZDO was able to secure a booking. Both the poseur-customer and subject agreed to meet in a motel in Pasay City. Two teams of NBI-RIZDO operatives were dispatched in Pasay City and Paranaque City. The operations resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of twenty (20) female victims, 2 of whom are minors. In the conduct of post-operation processing, 2 of the rescued victims were found to be positive for COVID-19 rapid antigen test that was conducted on them. All occupants of the accommodation house including the arrested subjects were recommended to be placed under quarantine pending the result of their RT-PCR tests. On May 6, 2021, operatives of NBI- Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) arrested as MERO MENDOZA SAGUID, ALEX P. NEGRILLO, ISAGANI B. FORNODA, and RANDY RAMIREZ y BENICO in three (3) different establishments in Solano, Nueva Vizcaya for selling chainsaws without necessary permit from the government. the operation stemmed from an information given by a reliable civilian informant that several establishments are selling chainsaws without permit in Solano, Nueva Vizcaya including; POWERSAW TRADING (Powersaw), GANIE SAW CENTER (Ganie), and BLANCO AGRICULTURAL FARM MACHINERY TRADING (Blanco). Validation made by the NBI-BAYDO operatives revealed that the above establishments are offering chainsaws and similar cutting implements for sale to the general public. Certification issued by the PENR Sub-office of the Department of National Resources Office, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya revealed that no authority or permit to sell and distribute the subject cutting machines were issued to Powersaw, Ganie, and Blanco. NBI-BAYDO operatives then proceeded to the business address of Powersaw, Ganie, and Blanco to conduct an entrapment operation. In the course of the operation the four subjects were arrested immediately after receiving the marked moneys. The operation also resulted in the seizure of two (2) local assemble chainsaws from Powersaw, two (2) big Stihl chainsaw from Ganie, and one (1) chainsaw from Blanco. The four (4) subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya for violation of R.A. 9175, otherwise known as the Chainsaw Act of 2002. On May 6, 2021, operatives of NBI- Central Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested ELOISA F. MENDOZA, Medical Representative of Genace Pharma Distributor, for possessing and intending to use sixteen (16) stolen/ falsified check. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint filed by the owner of the checks. According to the complainant, Subject Mendoza was intending to use the said stolen/falsified checks as payment to Genace Pharma Distributor (Genace) with a total amount of Php 417,471.00. On the above-mentioned date, on May 6, 2021, NBI-CELRO proceeded to the target area and arrested Subject Mendoza after she intended to transact the subject checks as payment to Genace. Subject Mendoza was presented for inquest proceedings for Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury or Bank Notes and Other Instruments of Credit under Article 168, in relation to Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents under paragraph 1 and 2 of Article 172 and Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. On May 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Counter-Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), together with AFP NISG-NCR, AFPJTF-NCR, and PNP Special Action Force-Rapid Deployment Battalion arrested WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI a.k.a. Ustadz Usman Halipa, a member of the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). In early April 2021, the NBI received information that an alleged ASG member was sighted in Maharlika, Taguig City where he reportedly resides. After investigation, it was learned that an ASG Subject alias Ustadz Usman Halipa was involved in Golden Harvest Plantation Kidnapping in 2001 at Tairan, Lantawan, Basilan Province, and is included in a Warrant of Arrest for his alleged involvement. On April 21, 2021, a witness identified a photo from CTD photo line-up as Ustadz Usman Halipa. On May 7, 2021, a joint operation was conducted by operatives of NBI-CTD, AFP NISG-NCR, AFPJTFNCR, and PNP Special Action Force-Rapid Deployment Battalion at Upper Bicutan, Maharlika Village, Taguig City, resulting in the arrest of Subject Ustadz Usman Halipa whose name was learned to be WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI. He was informed of his rights and underwent proper booking procedures. Subject WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI a.k.a. Ustadz Usman Halipa was then properly turned over to the NBI Detention Facility. On May 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested OLIVER ESTROPE Y HINGCO, MIKE ESTROPE Y HINGCO, and NIÑO DIOMAR MIRANDA y BARRIOS in Calinog, Iloilo for Robbery Extortion. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint of an owner/operator of a quarrying operation in Barangay Lonoy, Calinog, Iloilo, which was granted permit by the Office of the Governor of Iloilo. The complainant alleged that sometime in March 2021, Subjects put up barricades of woods, planks, and branches on the roads where complainant’s dump trucks and heavy equipment would pass. The three Subjects claimed that they are the legal owners of the bed and bank of the river where the dump trucks and heavy equipment passed-by and demanded Php 1,000.00 as fee for the “right of way” for each truck to gain entry and Php 300.00 for every truckload of extracted material they will remove and carry from their quarry site. Subjects also threatened the complainant and his workers with physical violence and damage to complainant’s quarry business should they refuse to give the demanded amount. Out of fear for their personal safety and not to hamper their operations, complainant caved-in to the demand of the Subjects on several occasions from March 28 to April 26, 2021. Aggrieved, the complainant was compelled to file a complaint before the NBI-WEVRO. NBI-WEVRO operative proceeded to the area of operation of the complainant to validate the complaint where he saw firsthand the extortion activities of the Subjects. On May 10, 2021, NBI-WEVRO operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject Oliver Estrope and his 4 companions. Two of his companions were later identified as senior citizens and gave statement that they were just invited by Subject Oliver Estrope because he has something to arrange with the complainant. They were allowed to stay with a promise that they will cooperate in the investigation. The claims of the Subjects that they own the far side of the river, the bed and the river bank is misplaced and has no sufficient basis in fact and in law. Thus, the three other Subjects were brought to the NBI-WEVRO and booked per standard operating procedure. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Iloilo Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery Extortion under Article 294 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended in relation to Cybercrime Law. On May 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested ACE BALINGIT y REYES and RYAN JOHN BALINGIT y TAGUBA in San Fernando, Pampanga for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against them. According to the complainants, Subject ACE BALINGIT and introduced himself as having the capacity to deploy workers abroad particularly in Poland as company drivers, hotel workers among others through his office Althanfio Visa Consultancy. Subject RYAN JOHN BALINGIT, on the other hand, introduced himself as staff of Althanfio Visa Consultancy. Subject ACE BALINGIT promised the complainants to earn a monthly salary ranging from Php 40,000 to Php 80,000. Relying with the Subjects’ promise and representation that they possess the capacity to deploy applicants to employment abroad, complainants paid a total of Php 478,000 purportedly intended to cover their processing fees for overseas employment. After receipt of the said amount, Subjects promised complainants for employment to Poland within 45-60 days. However, despite the lapse of almost four months, Subjects failed to deploy the complainants. Instead of refunding the money, Subject ACE BALINGIT even demanded additional payment of Php 20,000 as additional processing fee. Complainants eventually learned that Subjects are not licensed to recruit workers abroad so they reported the matter to NBI-CELRO and filed a formal complaint. Acting on the complaint and with the demand of Subject ACE BALINGIT for the additional placement fee, the entrapment operation was conducted at Althanfio Visa Consultancy resulting in the arrest of the Subjects after receiving the entrapment money. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, San Fernando, Pampanga for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment under RA 8042 as amended by RA 10022 and Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. On May 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-Agusan Del Sur District Office (NBI-ADSDO) arrested ANALIZA M. CONSTANCIO for illegal practice of dentistry. After validating the information provided by the Philippine Dental Association-Agusan del Sur Chapter that the family of Subject ANALIZA is engage in illegal practice of dentistry in their residence, operatives of NBI-ADSDO conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught placing a cast inside the mouth of the poseur customer in the makeshift clinic found in her residence. When Subject failed to show documents and valid professional identification card as professional dentist, ANALIZA was placed under arrest and was apprised of her constitutional and statutory rights. The tools used in the illegal practice were confiscated and inventoried. Subject was brought to NBI-ADSDO for proper disposition. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Agusan del Sur Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 9484 (Philippine Dental Act of 2007). On May 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), together with the personnel from Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), PNP Aviation Security Group and Bureau of Customs (BOC) arrested ROWENA EVANGELIO y CANAPIT and MICHAEL DE GUZMAN y LOMIBAO for RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On the aforementioned date, operatives proceeded to Central Post Office, NIA Road, Diliman, Quezon City for a controlled delivery operation. Three (3) parcels declared as baby clothes, handbag and shoes consigned to a certain GLORIE JOY LAMATAO BUZETA were intercepted by the BOC at NAIA. However, they were found to be tablets containing ecstasy. The consignee was expected to claim said parcels at the abovesaid post office. Operatives positioned themselves in the premises of the post office and about 1:15pm, a female claimed the parcels. She was discreetly followed until she approached a male companion waiting in his motorcycle. Upon placing the parcels on the motorcycle, operatives approached and arrested the two who were identified as Subjects ROWENA EVANGELIO y CANAPIT and MICHAEL DE GUZMAN y LOMIBAO. Seized were 9,243 pieces of ecstasy with current street value of Php 15,713,100.00. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violations of Sec.4 (Importation of Dangerous Drugs) and Sec.26 (Attempt of Conspiracy) of RA 9165 and Sec.1401 of RA 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). On May 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested ROSIELYN C. QUERON for violation of RA 6948 and Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the letter of the Director of Veterans Memorial Medical Center (VMMC) requesting for investigation and possible entrapment operation of the perpetrators involved in fraudulent transaction concerning the Veterans Hospitalization and Medical Care Program of the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office (PVAO) implemented through VMMC. The allegations of fraud consists of a scheme filing claims for reimbursement of hospitalization expenses of supposed veterans with spurious claim documents/attachments such as the Clinical Abstract, Statement of Account, and Official Receipts which were later on verified to be fake or inauthentic. On May 4, 2021, an information was received from Acting Chief, Accounting Section of VMMC that one of the above-mentioned veterans, through a representative, had made a follow up request on the status of his claim for reimbursement. The attachments/supporting documents provided in the said claim for reimbursement of the patient with a total sum of Php 578,258.714 were already confirmed to be spurious of fake prior to verification conducted. After proper coordination with the concerned authorities, NBI-AGD operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject ROSIELYN C. QUERON. Charges for violation of RA 6948 (An Act Standardizing and Upgrading the Benefits for Military Veterans and Their Dependents) and Estafa were filed before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City. Subject is currently under custody of NBI Detention Facility, Taft Avenue, Manila. On May 11, 2021, NAIA-IADITG composed of personnel from NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), PNPAviation Security Group and Bureau of Customs proceeded to Central Post Office along NIA Road, Diliman for a controlled delivery operation. Three (3) parcels declared as baby clothes, handbag and shoes consigned to a certain GLORIE JOY LAMATO BUZETA were intercepted by the Bureau of Customs at NAIA. They were found to be tablets containing Ecstacy. The consignee was expected to claim said parcels at the said post office. The operatives positioned themselves at the premises of the post office and waited for the arrival of the consignee. About 1:15 p.m., a female claimed the 3 parcels and approached a male companion waiting with his motorcycle. Upon placing the parcels on the motorcycle, the operatives approached and arrested the two Subjects and seized the illegal drugs. They were later identified as Rowena Evangelio y Canapit, authorized representative of the consignee, and her male companion, Michael De Guzman y Lomibao. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for violation of Sec, 4 (Importation of Dangerous Drugs), for Rowena Evangelio y Canapit and consignee, Gloria Joy Lamato Buzeta, and Sec. 26, (Attempt of Conspiracy) in relation to Section 4 of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) for subject Michael De Guzman y Lomibao. Subjects Evangelio and Buzeta was like charged for Sec. 1401 of R.A. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). On May 12, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested RICHARD RANA CASTINO for alleged rape. The case stemmed from the complaint of a minor victim. According to the victim, she was going to a friend in Pasay City and contacted Subject RICHARD RANA CASTINO after she saw the Facebook post of the Subject offering rent-a-car with professional driver. Subject RICHARD fetched and drove the victim to Pasay City using a car with plate number NGP-8270. Subject offered to drive the victim again the next time she will go to her friend in Pasay City, to which the latter agreed out of trust. On May 7, 2021, victim again hired Subject RICHARD to drive her to Pasay City. However, on their way home, the victim noticed that Subject RICHARD was driving towards a different direction and parked in a garage. Subject RICHARD alighted the car and forcibly took the victim in one of the rooms of a hotel in Pasay City. Subject then raped the victim inside the room. Because of fear and confusion, victim was only able to tell the incident to her parents on May 10, 2021. They then reported the incident to Manila Police District, however, the MPD does not have jurisdiction on the matter as it happened in Pasay City. They then opted to report the matter to NBI. With testimonial pieces of evidence and the report from the NBI-Medico-Legal Division, hot pursuit operation was hatched. Efforts were immediately made to locate the whereabouts of Subject RICHARD. Subject was contacted thru his Facebook account and the entrapment operation was hatched. NBI-AOTCD operatives, together with the victim and her parents, proceeded to West Avenue, Project 7, Quezon City. Upon arrival thereat, the victim positively identified the Subject. NBI-AOTCD operatives restrained the Subject and put him under arrest. Subject RICHARD was then informed of his alleged violation and was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject RICHARD RANA CASTINO was charged with violation of Article 336 (Acts of Lasciviousness) and Article 266 of the Revised Penal Code and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination). On May 12, 2021, operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested SANDY FRIAS y CABALIDA, an employee of the Local Building Office (LBO) of Taguig City, for alleged Robbery Extortion. a complaint was filed against the subject alleging that when complainant’s company applied for a Building Permit or Certificate of Occupancy on January 19, 2021 at the LBO of Taguig City, they paid the total fees of P108,743.60 and was issued the official receipt as payment for Certificate of Occupancy and Certificate of Electrical Inspection. When complainant asked for the release of the certificates, Subject Sandy Frias told them that the certificates can only be released in exchange for Php 800,000.00. Complainant pleaded for the amount be reduced. Subject Frias then told them that the Committee approved the amount to be reduced to P400,000.00, which should be directly paid to him. After more than 3 months of waiting and the same were still withheld by Subject Frias, Complainant finally decided to file a formal complaint before the NBI against the subject for extortion. NBI-TID operatives conducted an entrapment operation at the meeting place in Taguig City that led to the arrest of Subject Frias after he received the marked money from complainant. Subject peacefully submitted himself and was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Taguig City for Robbery Extortion in violation of Article 294 (5) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. On May 14, 2021, the NBI-Cordillera Administration Region (NBI-CAR) provided assistance in the resolution of a conflict concerning child custody. Reference is the endorsement of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) of a case handled by the Binan City Social Welfare and Development Office as regards the custody of a minor. A couple, Marife and Jake Bryan, both of legal age, cohabitated sometime in 2013 and had two children. In August 2016 Jake Bryan was gunned down by still unidentified assailant which resulted to his instantaneous death. Marife then left Baguio City and resided somewhere in Metro Manila taking her daughter into her custody while her son was left under the custody of Jake Bryan’s parents in Baguio City. When Marife got married, she and her husband established their residence in Binan, Laguna having Marife’s daughter still in their custody. In January 2021, Marife wanted to take into custody his son and sought the assistance of the CSWDO of Binan, Laguna. The said office coordinated with their counterparts in the City of Baguio and asked Jake Bryan’s parents to turn over the custody of Marife’s son. Adora C. Pascual, Chief of CSWDO of Binan, Laguna and Gladeewyn F. Decena, Social Welfare Officer of CSWDO together with Marife, went to Baguio City and coordinated with the Baguio CSWDO and the Baguio City Police Office but their negotiation thereat failed which prompted Adora Pascual to seek the assistance of NBI-Laguna District Office which then referred the case to NBI-CAR. After thorough evaluating the circumstances and with the concurrence of the CSWDO representatives, NBI-CAR explained that the custody of the minor son shall in the meantime remain with Marife being the biological mother. Accordingly, if Jake Bryan’s parents wish to have the custody of the minor son, they have the option to file a petition for custody in court which may grant or deny the said petition. After hearing the explanation of the NBI-CAR, Jake Bryan’s parents gave in and agreed to turn over the minor son to Marife, with the concurrence of Jake Bryan’s brother. Meanwhile, Marife gave an assurance that Jake Bryan’s parents and their relatives are allowed to visit their grandchildren in Binan City. On May 14, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (NBI-BARMM), together with CIDG-BARMM, PDEA BARMM, Regional Mobile force Brgade, and Philippine Marines, implemented Search Warrants issued against the premises of KAREM USOP ABEDIN, CAMAR MAUYAG, and EMEN MAUYAG PARTE all located at Brgy. Kabunturan, Picong, Lanao Sur for violation of RA 9165. During the implementation of said Search Warrants, Subject KAREM USOP ABEDIN was neutralized when she was shot by government forces. The two other Subjects managed to escape as the mobility of the operatives to reach their place was hampered by heavy downpour and rough terrain. However, fifteen (15) individuals were arrested inside the respective premises of the escaped Subjects. Said individuals were believed to have just sniffed “shabu” as evidenced by the presence of drug paraphernalia at the place. The search that ensued also yielded one (1) M16 Baby Armalite Rifle, one (1) Armalite Long Rifle, one (1) Hand Fragmentation Grenade, one (1) home-made Barret, several sachets of varied sizes containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, and drug paraphernalia. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) while the Subjects who eluded arrest will be charged for violation of RA 9165 and RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). On May 15, 2021, operatives of NBI-Puerto Princesa District Office (NBI-PUERDO) arrested WENZAR DASSAN y MAMAH a.k.a. WAWEN for illegal selling of imported cigarettes. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding a rampant selling and distribution of Fort, Bravo, L.A., Sorya, Garam, R.S., and other imported brands of cigarettes from Malaysia and Indonesia without paying the proper taxes and duties due to the government. Surveillance/test buy operation was conducted by NBI-PUERDO operatives to verify the said information and it was found out that the imported cigarettes can be purchased at stalls in almost all public market of Palawan. Test buy was also conducted on a certain WAWEN and ABDUL where Fort, Bravo, and New Berlin cigarettes were purchased. Based on the packaging, the products are manufactured in Malaysia and Indonesia but does not have the proper seal of tax stamps of the Bureau of Internal Revenue. Thus, on May 15, 2021, an entrapment operation was conducted and resulted in the arrest of Subject WENZAR DASSAN y MAMAH a.k.a. WAWEN. Seized from the Subject were several reams of imported cigarettes. Subject was bought to NBI-PUERDO where he was booked as per standard operating procedure. Subject WENZAR DASSAN was charged with violation of RA 1937 (Tariff and Customs Code as amended by RA 10863) before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Puerto Princesa City. On May 17, 2021, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), together with PDEA, BOC, and PNP Aviation Security Group, arrested KRISTOPHER CARLOS SEGUMBANG y SABALZA for receiving a package from Malaysia containing illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a controlled delivery operation participated by operatives of NBI-IAID as member of the NAIA-Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (IADITG). The operation stemmed from the discovery of an inbound parcel from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shipped by one Simon via FedEx and consigned to a certain NICK DIMAGIBA OF No. 165 Bagbaguin, Caloocan City. The package, which was declared snacks containing fifteen (15) pieces of sealed Kopiko L.A., contained a total of 622 grams of dangerous drugs Ketamine. The same was previously intercepted by the Bureau of Customs (BOC) at NAIA. The drugs have an estimated value of Php 3,110,000.00. The NAIA-IADITG was alerted of the said package and a controlled delivery operation was then put in place for the arrest of the named consignee and his possible cohorts. In the morning of May 17, 2021, operatives positioned themselves around the premises of Bagbaguin, Talipapa Wet and Dry Market, Caloocan City. At about noon, KRISTOPHER CARLOS SEGUMBANG y SABALZA, 34 years old, Filipino, resident of Kaingin St., Barangay Parada, Valenzuela City, claimed the package. At this juncture, he was arrested and informed of his rights under the law. The Immigration Officer who conducted the interview did not allow the Subject to depart as she appears too young for a 30 years old. Subject was turned-over to NBI-IAID for further questioning and validation. Subject Mukamad told the NBI-IAID that she has already been to Saudi Arabia in 2017 using her current passport. However, the subject stated in the identification card voluntarily filled by her that her correct date of birth is May 5, 2000 and that her name true name ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD. Subject also revealed that she secured her passport from Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) in Cotabatao City. Subject Mukamad was then placed under arrest and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of Section 19 (b)(2) (Uses or attempts to use any passport which was secured in any way by reason of any false statements) of R.A. 8239 otherwise known as the Philippine Passport Act of 1996. · On May 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested FELMOR BALUGAY DUMAGAT for selling shabu. Subject was arrested in a buybust operation which stemmed from the information that Subject is selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro city. The operation yielded a net weight of around 1.1 grams of shabu with an estimated street value of Php 7,000. Subject is currently in jail for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). On May 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested VICENTE FAILON MARTINEZ in San Fernando City, La Union for Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim before the NBI-IRO regarding the crime committed against him by the subject. According to the victim-complainant, Subject Martinez was able to dupe him a total amount of Php 486,000.00. After sometime, the swindling elevated to extortion when Subject Martinez concocted a spurious Intelligence Report (IR) allegedly from NBI-IRO and NBI Manila. Using the same IR, Subject Martinez demanded P1 Million from victimcomplainant and forcing him and forced him to surrender his motor vehicle and was coerced to execute a blank Deed of Absolute Sale of a Motor Vehicle with a current Market Value of Php 500,000.00. Also, subject Martinez subsequently demanded an additional P500,000.00 to complete the P1Million by way of threat and coercion, threatening victimcomplainant he will be arrested by NBI-IRO and NBI Manila if he fails to produce the said amount at St. Jude Church, Poro, City of San Fernando, La Union. Thus, On May 4, 2021, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subject Martinez who was caught red-handed in the act of receiving the entrapment money from the victimcomplainant. Subject Martinez was then brought to the NBI-IRO Office and had undergone standard booking procedures. Documents are being prepared for the filing of Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority against the subject. On May 4, 2021, operatives of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBIIAID) arrested GRETCHEN ABLAN for using documents with falsified information. Subject was about to depart as a tourist for Dubai, UAE, when she was referred for secondary inspection after being discovered that she was previously off-loaded on April 22, 2021 for misrepresentation. During inspection, Subject claimed she was visiting her husband, JOEY DAMASCO MANALIGOD and showed copies of passport bio-page and UAE Visa sticker of MANALIGOD. With discrepancies and alteration in documents, different as reflected in the Central Query Support System of the Bureau of Immigration, Subject ABLAN admitted both verbally and in writing that she was not married and does not actually know MANALIGOD. She stated that all her documents for her May 4 flight were sent to her on May 3, 2021 by her recruiter through another person in Baclaran, Paranaque City. When confronted by the NBI regarding the COVID-19 Test Report issued by Dagupan Doctors Villaflor Memorial Hospital under her name, she said she had not undergone any COVID-19 test. Upon verification with said hospital on the COVID-19 of subject, the hospital declared that subject ABLAN did not appear in their list as one of their patients. Subject ABLAN was then placed under arrest for violation of Art. 172 in relation to Art. 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Use of Falsified Documents. Subject GRETCHEN ABLAN was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City. On May 4-7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized fake stamps and materials for making cigarettes with an estimated amount of Php 750 Million. Items were seized in Bacolod City during the implementation of BIR Mission Order for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). On May 5, 2021, operatives of NBI- Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested Spouses KONG, MA. ANGELICA y BELGA and KONG, XIANGCE (Chinese national) in Parañaque City for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report that a group of unidentified individuals are engaged in prostitution and human trafficking activities, particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims. According to the report, booking of women for sexual services is done through messaging in private group chats intended solely for Chinese Customers. Subjects sent a ready list of prices of the sexual services being offered written in Chinese language. NBI-RIZDO requested the assistance of Destiny Rescue Philippines, an NGO which rescue children from sexual exploitation and human trafficking. The operation also resulted in the seizure of two (2) local assemble chainsaws from Powersaw, two (2) big Stihl chainsaw from Ganie, and one (1) chainsaw from Blanco. The four (4) subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya for violation of R.A. 9175, otherwise known as the Chainsaw Act of 2002. On May 6, 2021, operatives of NBI- Central Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested ELOISA F. MENDOZA, Medical Representative of Genace Pharma Distributor, for possessing and intending to use sixteen (16) stolen/ falsified check. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint filed by the owner of the checks. According to the complainant, Subject Mendoza was intending to use the said stolen/falsified checks as payment to Genace Pharma Distributor (Genace) with a total amount of Php 417,471.00. On the above-mentioned date, on May 6, 2021, NBI-CELRO proceeded to the target area and arrested Subject Mendoza after she intended to transact the subject checks as payment to Genace. Subject Mendoza was presented for inquest proceedings for Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury or Bank Notes and Other Instruments of Credit under Article 168, in relation to Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents under paragraph 1 and 2 of Article 172 and Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. On May 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Counter-Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), together with AFP NISG-NCR, AFPJTF-NCR, and PNP Special Action Force-Rapid Deployment Battalion arrested WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI a.k.a. Ustadz Usman Halipa, a member of the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). In early April 2021, the NBI received information that an alleged ASG member was sighted in Maharlika, Taguig City where he reportedly resides. After investigation, it was learned that an ASG Subject alias Ustadz Usman Halipa was involved in Golden Harvest Plantation Kidnapping in 2001 at Tairan, Lantawan, Basilan Province, and is included in a Warrant of Arrest for his alleged involvement. On April 21, 2021, a witness identified a photo from CTD photo line-up as Ustadz Usman Halipa. On May 7, 2021, a joint operation was conducted by operatives of NBI-CTD, AFP NISG-NCR, AFPJTFNCR, and PNP Special Action Force-Rapid Deployment Battalion at Upper Bicutan, Maharlika Village, Taguig City, resulting in the arrest of Subject Ustadz Usman Halipa whose name was learned to be WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI. He was informed of his rights and underwent proper booking procedures. Subject WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI a.k.a. Ustadz Usman Halipa was then properly turned over to the NBI Detention Facility. On May 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested OLIVER ESTROPE Y HINGCO, MIKE ESTROPE Y HINGCO, and NIÑO DIOMAR MIRANDA y BARRIOS in Calinog, Iloilo for Robbery Extortion. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint of an owner/operator of a quarrying operation in Barangay Lonoy, Calinog, Iloilo, which was granted permit by the Office of the Governor of Iloilo. The complainant alleged that sometime in March 2021, Subjects put up barricades of woods, planks, and branches on the roads where complainant’s dump trucks and heavy equipment would pass. The three Subjects claimed that they are the legal owners of the bed and bank of the river where the dump trucks and heavy equipment passed-by and demanded Php 1,000.00 as fee for the “right of way” for each truck to gain entry and Php 300.00 for every truckload of extracted material they will remove and carry from their quarry site. Subjects also threatened the complainant and his workers with physical violence and damage to complainant’s quarry business should they refuse to give the demanded amount. Out of fear for their personal safety and not to hamper their operations, complainant caved-in to the demand of the Subjects on several occasions from March 28 to April 26, 2021. Aggrieved, the complainant was compelled to file a complaint before the NBI-WEVRO. NBI-WEVRO operative proceeded to the area of operation of the complainant to validate the complaint where he saw firsthand the extortion activities of the Subjects. On May 10, 2021, NBI-WEVRO operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject Oliver Estrope and his 4 companions. Two of his companions were later identified as senior citizens and gave statement that they were just invited by Subject Oliver Estrope because he has something to arrange with the complainant. They were allowed to stay with a promise that they will cooperate in the investigation. The claims of the Subjects that they own the far side of the river, the bed and the river bank is misplaced and has no sufficient basis in fact and in law. Thus, the three other Subjects were brought to the NBI-WEVRO and booked per standard operating procedure. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Iloilo Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery Extortion under Article 294 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended in relation to Cybercrime Law. Subject RYAN JOHN BALINGIT, on the other hand, introduced himself as staff of Althanfio Visa Consultancy. Subject ACE BALINGIT promised the complainants to earn a monthly salary ranging from Php 40,000 to Php 80,000. Relying with the Subjects’ promise and representation that they possess the capacity to deploy applicants to employment abroad, complainants paid a total of Php 478,000 purportedly intended to cover their processing fees for overseas employment. After receipt of the said amount, Subjects promised complainants for employment to Poland within 45-60 days. However, despite the lapse of almost four months, Subjects failed to deploy the complainants. Instead of refunding the money, Subject ACE BALINGIT even demanded additional payment of Php 20,000 as additional processing fee. Complainants eventually learned that Subjects are not licensed to recruit workers abroad so they reported the matter to NBI-CELRO and filed a formal complaint. Acting on the complaint and with the demand of Subject ACE BALINGIT for the additional placement fee, the entrapment operation was conducted at Althanfio Visa Consultancy resulting in the arrest of the Subjects after receiving the entrapment money. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, San Fernando, Pampanga for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment under RA 8042 as amended by RA 10022 and Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. After validating the information provided by the Philippine Dental Association-Agusan del Sur Chapter that the family of Subject ANALIZA is engage in illegal practice of dentistry in their residence, operatives of NBI-ADSDO conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught placing a cast inside the mouth of the poseur customer in the makeshift clinic found in her residence. The tools used in the illegal practice were confiscated and inventoried. Subject was brought to NBI-ADSDO for proper disposition. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Agusan del Sur Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 9484 (Philippine Dental Act of 2007). On the aforementioned date, operatives proceeded to Central Post Office, NIA Road, Diliman, Quezon City for a controlled delivery operation. Three (3) parcels declared as baby clothes, handbag and shoes consigned to a certain GLORIE JOY LAMATAO BUZETA were intercepted by the BOC at NAIA. However, they were found to be tablets containing ecstasy. The consignee was expected to claim said parcels at the abovesaid post office. Operatives positioned themselves in the premises of the post office and about 1:15pm, a female claimed the parcels. She was discreetly followed until she approached a male companion waiting in his motorcycle. Upon placing the parcels on the motorcycle, operatives approached and arrested the two who were identified as Subjects ROWENA EVANGELIO y CANAPIT and MICHAEL DE GUZMAN y LOMIBAO. Seized were 9,243 pieces of ecstasy with current street value of Php 15,713,100.00. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violations of Sec.4 (Importation of Dangerous Drugs) and Sec.26 (Attempt of Conspiracy) of RA 9165 and Sec.1401 of RA 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). On May 4, 2021, an information was received from Acting Chief, Accounting Section of VMMC that one of the above-mentioned veterans, through a representative, had made a follow up request on the status of his claim for reimbursement. The attachments/supporting documents provided in the said claim for reimbursement of the patient with a total sum of Php 578,258.714 were already confirmed to be spurious of fake prior to verification conducted. After proper coordination with the concerned authorities, NBI-AGD operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject ROSIELYN C. QUERON. Charges for violation of RA 6948 (An Act Standardizing and Upgrading the Benefits for Military Veterans and Their Dependents) and Estafa were filed before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City. Subject is currently under custody of NBI Detention Facility, Taft Avenue, Manila. About 1:15 p.m., a female claimed the 3 parcels and approached a male companion waiting with his motorcycle. Subject offered to drive the victim again the next time she will go to her friend in Pasay City, to which the latter agreed out of trust. On May 7, 2021, victim again hired Subject RICHARD to drive her to Pasay City. Subject RICHARD alighted the car and forcibly took the victim in one of the rooms of a hotel in Pasay City. Subject then raped the victim inside the room. Complainant pleaded for the amount be reduced. Subject Frias then told them that the Committee approved the amount to be reduced to P400,000.00, which should be directly paid to him. Pascual, Chief of CSWDO of Binan, Laguna and Gladeewyn F. Meanwhile, Marife gave an assurance that Jake Bryan’s parents and their relatives are allowed to visit their grandchildren in Binan City. Kabunturan, Picong, Lanao Sur for violation of RA 9165. During the implementation of said Search Warrants, Subject KAREM USOP ABEDIN was neutralized when she was shot by government forces. The two other Subjects managed to escape as the mobility of the operatives to reach their place was hampered by heavy downpour and rough terrain. However, fifteen (15) individuals were arrested inside the respective premises of the escaped Subjects. Said individuals were believed to have just sniffed “shabu” as evidenced by the presence of drug paraphernalia at the place. The search that ensued also yielded one (1) M16 Baby Armalite Rifle, one (1) Armalite Long Rifle, one (1) Hand Fragmentation Grenade, one (1) home-made Barret, several sachets of varied sizes containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, and drug paraphernalia. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) while the Subjects who eluded arrest will be charged for violation of RA 9165 and RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding a rampant selling and distribution of Fort, Bravo, L.A., Sorya, Garam, R.S., and other imported brands of cigarettes from Malaysia and Indonesia without paying the proper taxes and duties due to the government. Surveillance/test buy operation was conducted by NBI-PUERDO operatives to verify the said information and it was found out that the imported cigarettes can be purchased at stalls in almost all public market of Palawan. Test buy was also conducted on a certain WAWEN and ABDUL where Fort, Bravo, and New Berlin cigarettes were purchased. Based on the packaging, the products are manufactured in Malaysia and Indonesia but does not have the proper seal of tax stamps of the Bureau of Internal Revenue. Thus, on May 15, 2021, an entrapment operation was conducted and resulted in the arrest of Subject WENZAR DASSAN y MAMAH a.k.a. WAWEN. Seized from the Subject were several reams of imported cigarettes. Subject was bought to NBI-PUERDO where he was booked as per standard operating procedure. The operation stemmed from the discovery of an inbound parcel from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shipped by one Simon via FedEx and consigned to a certain NICK DIMAGIBA OF No. 165 Bagbaguin, Caloocan City.
