body: PRESS STATEMENT February 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES FOUR MINORS IN LAGUNA HUMAN TRAFFICKING STING; ONLINE PREDATOR ARRESTED PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – CALABARZON Regional Office (NBI-CALABARZON) has successfully rescued ten victims of human trafficking—including four minors—during a high-stakes entrapment operation in San Pablo City, Laguna. The operation led to the arrest of a male Subject. The Subject is facing multiple charges for violations of the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act and the Special Protection Against Children Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, both cited in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. The crackdown began after NBI-CALABARZON received intelligence regarding an individual using Facebook to solicit sexual services. Cyber surveillance identified a Facebook group which served as a digital storefront for illegal activities. Investigators observed that the Subject utilized the platform to negotiate rates and share photographs of victims. Of particular concern to authorities were images of young-looking females, which raised immediate red flags regarding the exploitation of children. On February 12, 2026, NBI operatives acting as poseur-customers coordinated a meeting at a resort in Brgy. Sta. Veronica, San Pablo City. Upon arrival, the Subject presented ten females for “entertainment” at a rate of Php 3,000.00 per person. Once the pre-marked entrapment money was exchanged and the intent for sexual exploitation was confirmed, NBI agents moved in to arrest the Subject in flagrante delicto. The ten rescued victims, including the four minors, are being provided with necessary support and interventions. The Subject was brought to the NBI Office in Lipa City for processing and has been presented for inquest proceedings at the Office of the City Prosecutor of San Pablo City. The NBI remains unyielding in its commitment to dismantle trafficking networks and is focused on cases involving the digital exploitation of children, ensuring that those who target the vulnerable on social media face the full force of the law.

body: This pertains to a case involving a criminal elements led by a certain JARVIS GUY LOPEZ with residence address located at 20-C Saragoza Street, Brgy. Doña Imelda, Quezon City charged for series of Robbery with Intimidation, Robberry with Rape and Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention) before the National Prosecution Service, Quezon City docketed as XV-03-INV-14-B-01446 to 52. This stemmed from series of complaints of victims in the “escort service” whom the accused preyed upon in its criminal activities. The group was able to victimize a total of seven (7) females in its series of kidnapping and robbery activities. In the evening of December 02, 2013, Complainants reported the alleged robbery and kidnapping in the office of the Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) by unidentified male individuals in Manila. Acting on the said information, the CTD operatives conducted an investigation to verify the said information. A team of operatives of NBI-CTD conducted surveillance and discreet inquiries to ascertain the identities and whereabouts of the alleged perpetrators. However, despite diligent efforts to locate Respondent’s house where the victims were brought the operatives were not able to locate it on that day. While CTD operatives were conducting its investigation, the group relentlessly continued with its criminal activities with impunity victimizing several women in the process. Thereafter, through continuous and discreet inquiries, the NBI-CTD Operatives were able to locate and interview another victim, wherein she was able to shed light on the identity of Accused during her captivity. It was disclosed that in her captivity, the name “JARVIS GUY LOPEZ” was given by a woman alleged to be the common-law-wife of Accused. Subsequent verification with the Land Transportation Office, East Avenue Diliman Quezon City yielded a information for a certain “JARVIS GUY LOPEZ” with an address at No. 20 Saragoza Street Brgy Doña Imelda, Quezon City. Immediately thereafter, NBI-CTD Operatives conducted a surveillance operation together with another Complainant on the said address. During the surveillance operation, Complainant recognized Accused’s house as No. 20-C Saragoza Street, Brgy. Imelda Quezon City, as the place where she was brought by the Accused. Subsequently, on January 13, 2014, upon showing of the pictures of the Accused’s house and the photo from the LTO of one “JARVIS GUY LOPEZ”, Complainant was able to recognize “JANVIC” as “JARVIS GUY LOPEZ”. Hence, based on that information, NBI-CTD Operatives filed an Application for Search Warrant on the said house. On January 28, 2014, by virtue of Search Warrant issued by the RTC- Quezon City for violation of P.D. 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 and R.A. 10591, NBI-CTD operatives conducted a search of No. 20-C Saragoza Street, Brgy. Imelda Quezon City and took pictures of the Respondent’s house. Upon showing the pictures to Complainant, she was able to recognize the same as the same house where she was locked up and detained against her will. In view of the foregoing, the NBI-CTD Operatives were able to conclude that the Respondent JARVIS GUY LOPEZ and his cohorts were the same group who committed the abovementioned crimes against Complainants. The NBI-CTD was assisted by Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) in the conduct of case buildup.

Subsequent verification with the Land Transportation Office, East Avenue Diliman Quezon City yielded a information for a certain “JARVIS GUY LOPEZ” with an address at No. 20 Saragoza Street Brgy Doña Imelda, Quezon City. Imelda Quezon City and took pictures of the Respondent’s house. Upon showing the pictures to Complainant, she was able to recognize the same as the same house where she was locked up and detained against her will. In view of the foregoing, the NBI-CTD Operatives were able to conclude that the Respondent JARVIS GUY LOPEZ and his cohorts were the same group who committed the abovementioned crimes against Complainants. The NBI-CTD was assisted by Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) in the conduct of case buildup.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of four (4) individuals by the operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) in Pasay City for using falsified documents. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as RUBY ANN FRIVALDO y RAVARA, HELEN HIJONA y AMANTE, ZUSETTE MAGABANUA y MELANIO, and HELEN PANEN y PALMONES. OIC Distor said that the NBI-IAID received an endorsement from the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons (NAIA-TFATP) pertaining to the four subjects bound to Dubai, UAE. However, the subjects were not permitted by Immigration Officers at NAIA Terminal 3 to depart to Dubai, UAE on July 12, 2021 due to the dubious travel documents presented by the subjects. The subjects declared to be travelling as OFW with final destination to Albania but they could not answer questions pertaining to their declared work in Albania. They later admitted that they intend to work in Dubai, UAE as domestic workers. The four arrested subjects were turned-over to the NBI-IAID on July 14, 2021, where they were interviewed. The subjects narrated that they were recruited to work as household service workers in Dubai, UAE. Their travel and employment documents were handed to them on July 12, 2021, at the accommodation house in Las Piñas City by a certain Miriam Abas of SURE JOBS INTERNATIONAL MANPOWER AGENCY CO., a private recruitment agency. body: PRESS STATEMENT February 18, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Reaffirms Commitment to Impartial and Equal Treatment in All Investigations The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) reiterates its unwavering commitment to fairness, impartiality, and due process in the handling of all complaints brought before the Bureau. Recent public discussions have arisen following photographs of individuals who appeared at the NBI in connection with separate investigations. The Bureau clarifies that the presence of any individual — whether as complainant or respondent , does not imply endorsement, favoritism, or prejudice. In previous matters, public figure Michelle Dee appeared before the Bureau as a complainant and, in a separate case, as a respondent. Similarly, Alyas Totoy appeared as a complainant in connection with a complaint filed before the NBI. Most recently, another respondent appeared before the Bureau in relation to an alleged dissemination of false information concerning a medical certificate. In all instances, the NBI strictly followed standard investigative procedures. The same level of professionalism, courtesy, and due process is extended to all individuals — regardless of their status, political affiliation, social standing, or personal background. They reflect transparency and the routine conduct of investigative processes. The NBI does not discriminate based on disability, public image, or influence. body: A previously arrested fake lawyer who repeated the same offense and demanded a huge amount from a complainant was nabbed with her companion by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Cavite last week. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: MARHEA VICTORIA ARANETA-GONZALEZ DELOS REYES alias Marhea, Victoria, Jasmine, Shirley delos Reyes, a resident of Unit 103 Siblings St., B1 L11 Aldebaran St., Zapote, las Piñas City; and HENRY ANYAYA OCLIMA, driver, of 314 Lanzones St., Manuela 4B Subd., Las Piñas City. Investigation by the NBI National Capital Region (NCR) headed by Regional Director Elfren L. Meneses Jr. disclosed that on May 20, 2013, complainant Alexander Pascua filed a complaint with the NBI against a certain Atty. Victoria Delos Reyes for claiming to be a lawyer. Pascua said that suspect Delos Reyes who claims to be a lawyer was referred to him by a friend, who can represent him in the mediation/conciliation conference before the Public Attorney’s Office in Antipolo district and in his annulment case in Pascua’s favor within six (6) months without appearance. Delos Reyes asked for P234,800 package as attorney’s and miscellaneous fees which Pascua paid. On April 16 and 17, 2013 “Atty. Delos Reyes” went to Pascua’s house asking him about the Annulment case that will be filed on April 18, 2013. She also informed him that a Concubinage case had been allegedly filed against him by his wife. She can likewise facilitate the dismissal of this case for a fee of P20,000 which he again gave to the suspect. Three days later, de los Reyes sought Pascua demanding for another P51,000 for the alleged immediate settlement of the case lodged before the Antipolo City Public Attorney’s Office as well as the dismissal of Concubinage case against him. Thereafter, on several occasions, De los Reyes visited complainant and asked for more fees, — On April 23, 2013, P28,000 as filing fees for the case that will be filed against his wife and DNA testing of his child; April 25, 2013, P3,700 as payment for the help of DSWD personnel for the DNA test. Similarly, on April 29, 2013, suspect asked again for P32,000 for the alleged filing fees of the moral damages in the Adultery case he will be filing against his wife; May 4, 2013, P20,000 down payment for Psychological Evaluation for the Annulment Case; and May 11, 2013, P3,700 for the alleged speedy trial of the cases filed against him. Instead, Pascual asked for the documents Delos Reyes allegedly paid for but could not present any. All payments were personally received by Delos Reyes in cash as evidenced by the Acknowledgment Receipt signed by the suspect. Doubting on Delos Reyes identity, complainant thru the internet came to know that she has been previously arrested by the NBI as a bogus lawyer. This prompted Pascua to seek NBI assistance. In the afternoon of May 20, 2013, an entrapment was set. Suspect and complainant were to meet at Pascua’s residence at 6:30 PM in Binakayan, Cavite for the payment of P3,700. NBI agents proceeded to the place and a meeting took place between Pascua and Delos Reyes. Moments after, Delos Reyes received the marked money from Pascua, NBI agents inside the latter’s house approached and arrested the former. The suspect tried to bribe the arresting team but was refused. Instead, she was brought to the NBI for detention. Charges for Estafa, Falsification of Public Documents, Attempted Corruption of Public Official, and Resistance and Disobedience to a Person in Authority were filed against the suspect before the Provincial Prosecutor of Imus, Cavite.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of sixteen (16) individuals for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention of three (3) victims in Quezon City. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as ARSENIO BONIFACIO y CUADRA, AMADOR DOMINGO y BONIFACIO, NOEL BERNARDINO y BUCAD, ROBERTO SANCHEZ y BUCAD, FELIXBERTO RIVERA y PROTACIO, ANA MARIE REYES y AGUILAR, JANE IRIS BANGAHUN y VALLERA, ROLANDO RAMOS JR. y DURAN, SIDNEY CATACUTAN y GERASOL, SAHID SAINDUIN y SAMAD, JOVANIE PORAZO y PAYNANDOS, ROMMEL LOGRONO y ESTILLORE, REGINALD KOSCA y ESPIRITU, GARRY AMANTE y MENESES, WARREN MATEO y DEL MONTE, and EMIE PASTOLERO y CERBANIA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed against the subjects by the relatives of one of the victims. According to the complainants, when the COVID-19 broke out in March 2020, they decided to leave their DCB compound located at North Diversion Road, Brgy. Unang Sigaw Quezon City to be safe from the pandemic. However, their sister, Camille Bonifacio, her live-in partner, Mark Jason Magbanua and their 6-year old son, decided to stay in the compound. OIC Director Distor stressed that on July 10, 2020, without legal authority, Subjects Arsenio and Amador, together with 16 armed men and security guards, forcibly entered their compound, unlawfully occupied and took-over said compound, and, thereafter, illegally detained Camille, her live-in partner Mark and their son. According to Mark, who escaped from the compound on August 20, 2020 and filed a complaint before the NBI together with the siblings of Camille, they were threatened by the subjects that they will be shot mercilessly if they tried to escape. Mark also disclosed in the complaint that they were being held as hostages to compel Camille’s brother, BRUMMEL, to negotiate with the subjects for a “Royalty in DBC Compound. Fearing for the safety of his family, Mark decided to go back to the compound. Distor said that surveillance were conducted by the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) at DCB compound and observed that the area was heavily guarded by armed men. On August 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-NCR hatched an operation that resulted in the rescue of Mark, Camille, and their 6 year-old son. NBI-NCR operatives also arrested sixteen (16) individuals responsible for the kidnapping of the victims. During the operation, the operatives were able to seize three (3) pistols with magazines and live rounds, three (3) shotguns with live ammunitions, two (2) revolvers with live ammunitions, four (4) pieces handheld radios, and two (2) bullet vests. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for violation of Article 267 (Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention) punishable under the Revised Penal Code. In addition, since one of the victims is a six-year old boy, the subjects were charged for violation of R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse).

body: Acting with dispatch, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents arrested eight (8) members of a kidnap-for-ransom syndicate and rescued four (4) victims during an operation in Manila the other day. The suspects were identified as: HUNG-CHANG LAI, 35; TING-CHIEN LI, 23; LIN CHENG CHO; CHENG-HAO HUNG, 24; JYUN-KAI ZENG, 28; HUNG-CHUAN CHAN, 34; WEI MING LIO; and YAN PEN YANG, all Taiwanese and CATHERINE GENETIA TARUC, 28, Filipino, of F. Libamao St., Buliran, San Miguel, Bulacan. Victims were spouses Lai Yen Hung and Yin Hanbing; Hsu Hsin-Chung, and Jiang Nan. Investigation disclosed that in the morning of September 4, 2012, the NBI received a letter-request from an informant-resident of Bangkal, Makati City that one alias A-Hong, Taiwanese national and his wife and business partners were kidnapped by yet unidentified also Taiwanese national. According to him, a Taiwanese national called him up that same morning informing that his Taiwanese boss, A-Hong and several co-employees were being held against their will in a certain hotel along Quirino Ave., Malate, Manila and released only if the relatives in Taiwan pay PhP2 million. With this information, NBI agents coordinated with the local police and the management and security of the hotel. At 2 PM, of the same day, NBI operatives raided the said hotel and found in the rooms suspects and the victims. Victim Ah-Hong had head injuries and chained to the bed post, together with his wife. The suspects were immediately arrested and the victims rescued. Also found and seized were a baseball bat, a Ford Expedition van, sets of steel chains and padlocks used to kidnap and detain the victims. Several passports belonging to the suspects and the victims and mobile phones were likewise recovered. Charges for violation of Art. 267 (Kidnapping with Ransom) under the Revised Penal Code, as amended, were filed against the suspects before the City Prosecutor of Manila.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the Bureau’s Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested two (2) individuals for illegally keeping timbers or lumbers with an estimated amount of Php 50 Million in Barangay Bagbag, Novaliches, Quezon City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the two subjects as ERWIN VILLEGAS y QUIRAO and ROLLY MARTIN y LUTCHING. The joint operation of NBI-EnCD and Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the seizure of various timbers or lumbers of narra, yakal, molave, bolong, and other species, arose from the issuance of Search Warrant issued by RTC 94, Quezon City. Aside from the timbers, woodworking planer and chainsaw were also seized during the operation. The joint operation was conducted in compliance with the directive of the President of the Republic of the Philippines RODRIGO ROA DUTERTE to enforce total logging moratorium particularly, mandating the Department of the Environmental Crime Task Force (NAECTF) to formulate an OPLAN to be implemented in coordination with the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine National Police (PNP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Department of Justice (DOJ), the Ombudsman, and this Bureau. DENR USEC Arturo T. Valdez, Head of NAECTF, then wrote a letter addressed to Director Gierran requesting the NBI to provide the necessary manpower complement for the anti-illegal logging enforcement operations. Subjects will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Inquest Prosecutor, DOJ for violation of PD 705 as amended by Executive Order No.277 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines), violation of R.A. 9175 (An Act Regulating the Ownership, Possession, Sale, Importation and Use of Chainsaws, Penalizing Violations Thereof and for Other Purposes), and R.A. 1950 (An Act Regulating the Operation of Sawmills, Requiring Operators of Sawmills to Obtain from the Director of Forestry Permits for the Operation of Such Sawmills, and Providing Penalties for Violations Thereof).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two individuals by NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) in two operations in Pasay City for Falsification of travel documents. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as MINERVA OLIT y LARGO, an OFW who was about to depart to Duabi, UAE via Gulf Air in NAIA Terminal 1 on June 22, 2021 and NAIMA MAMA y BARAO, also an OFW bound for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia via Qatar Airways on June 26, 2021. Subject Olit was about to depart when she was referred by airport personnel for secondary inspection for the purpose of verifying her documents, as they appeared to be dubious. Subject Olit claimed that she was a former OFW and returning to her former employer named NASSER SAEED RASHED ALKAABI (Nasser). Subject Olit presented a 2019 Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC) and contract to prove her claim. However, POEA records showed that she was formerly employed to SHIRIN AMIN MOHAMED ANOU ELIN (Shirin) from 2017-2018 and was never employed to Nasser. Due to the inconsistencies, Subject Olit was referred to the NBI-IAID. NBI-IAID interviewed the subject and revealed that she worked as a domestic helper to her former employer Shirin from 2015 to 2018. After her contract ended, she then applied again to Dubai via online and met Vanessa who was allegedly in UAE, who processed all her travel documents. The subject added that she received the documents from the agent of Vanessa in the Philippines identified as Jasmin. Vanessa told the subject that all the expenses for her flight and documents were shouldered by her employer. Subject Olit also presented a Covid-19 Report issued by the Chinese General Hospital (CGH) in her attempt to depart. NBI-IAID verified the authenticity of the COVID-19 report and found out that CGH has no record in the name of Olit. Subject Olit admitted to the NBI-IAID operatives that she had not undergone a COVID-19 test before the CGH. Thus, the NBI-IAID operatives apprehended the subject for using falsified COVID-19 Report. Subject MAMA, on the other hand, was about to depart when she was stopped by airport personnel at NAIA Terminal 3. She presented her passport and KSA Standard Employment Contract. However, upon questioning, she gave inconsistent answers which led to the deferment of her departure. She was turned over to NAIA-Trafficking Against Persons and subsequently to NBI-IAID for investigation. During the interview, she stated that she previously worked in KSA as a household service worker from April 2018 to March 2021 and was born on May 25, 1996 in Maguindanao contrary to what is stated in her passport. In the NBI fingerprint card she filled out, she wrote her real name is NAIMA MAMA y BARAO. She used the birth certificate of her sister to procure her own passport and concealed her true name and real age fir her to pass the POEA requirements that those who intend to work in KSA should be at least 23 years old. With these, she was placed under arrest for use of fictitious name and concealing her true age. Subjects Olit and Mama were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City, for violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code and RA 8239 and Article 178 of the Revised Penal Code, respectively.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI SEIZES 78M WORTH OF MONSTER PRODUCTS On May 15, 2026, the NBI – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) and representatives from NBI – Intellectual Property Rights Division (IPRD) executed anti-counterfeiting raid across Metro Manila, resulting in the massive seizure of 13,407 pieces of counterfeit “MONSTER” trademarked merchandise valued at approximately Php 78, 834,000.00. Acting on the formal complaint filed by a brand representative, the NBI operatives conducted extensive surveillance and test-buy operations to confirm that the target warehouses are storing and distributing unauthorized products. Armed with search warrants issued by Regional Trial Court, Branch 28 of Manila, NBI operatives implemented the said search warrants at seven (7) various locations, consisting of five (5) stalls at 168 and 999 shopping malls in Binondo, Manila, as well as two (2) storage warehouses in Brgy. Maysan, Valenzuela City. The crackdown successfully disrupted an illicit distribution network that inflicted unfair competition and intellectual property theft against the authentic brand. The business owners and operators responsible for the illegal warehouses and stalls facilities are being processed to face criminal charges for violation of Section 155 (Trademark Infringement) in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No.8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila and Valenzuela.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 03, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested four (4) individuals in San Fernando City, La Union for violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Law). Information received from Project Rescue Children Philippines Inc. (PRC) revealed the trafficking activities of a certain individual, who has been offering young girls for sexual services in exchange for a fee ranging from Php2,500.00 – Php3,500.00. The information further revealed that said individual receives a commission of Php500.00 per girl and that the girls being offered are between the ages of 14 to 17. The individual also offers illicit substances such as dubi, marijuana and claims to have access to party drugs. Thus, on April 30, 2024, upon proper coordination with other government agencies, NBI-IRO conducted a rescue and entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of four (4) individuals and rescue of ten (10) trafficked victims, eight (8) of whom are minors based on the dental aging examination conducted on the victims. The trafficked victims were turned-over to the custody of the DSWD officers who were also present during the operation. However, upon arrival at the office of the NBI-IRO, three (3) of the arrested subjects revealed that they are likewise minors, which was confirmed thru dental aging examination. The three (3) minor Subjects were also turned-over to the custody of the DSWD. The adult Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of San Fernando, La Union for the above-mentioned violations.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 04, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation – Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) and Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO) arrested TIMOTHY JAMES TIBAJIA y SAPORTEZA and WILLIAM ANG y FERNANDEZ in an entrapment operation in Pulilan, Bulacan for Robbery/Extortion, Usurpation of Authority of Official Function, and Illegal Possession of Firearms. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 13, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR BOARD LICENSURE EXAMINATION FRAUD The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of MONAIDA DIMAKALING y GADI on October 2, 2022 by the operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office (NBI-PAGDO) for presenting herself as “NAZIA DIMAKALING y GADI in taking the Board Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers at Pagadian City National High School Danlugan Campus. The assigned proctor of the licensure examination at Pagadian City National High School discovered the impersonation. The proctor noticed the glaring discrepancy between the picture attached to the Permanent Examination and Registration Record Card (PERRC) and the Notice of Admission (NOA) of Examinee No. 3 in the name of NAZIA and of the person who is actually taking the examination. The observation was referred to the Floor Supervisor who also spotted the evident variance between the pictures attached to the PERRC and NOA, and the appearance of the person who took the examination. The matter was reported to the Building Supervisor who in turn sought the assistance of the NBI-PAGDO. During investigation, Subject Monaida immediately admitted that she is not the supposed board examination taker NAZIA DIMAKALING. The subject also revealed that NAZIA is her younger sister and that the latter asked her to take the examination in her behalf. Thus, agents of NBI-PAGDO apprehended Subject Monaida and were able to confiscate in the possession of the latter a BIR ID card and Quarantine ID, both under the name of NAZIA. Subject Monaida was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutors Office of Pagadian City for Falsification of Official Document under Article 172 in relation to Article 171, paragraph 2 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. In a resolution issued by the Office of the Prosecutor of Pagadian City, NAZIA DIMAKALING (at-large) was also indicted for the same offense who conspired with Subject Monaida in the execution of the said fraudulent act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI DISMANTLES ILLEGAL DETENTION DEN IN MUNTINLUPA CITY; TWO ARRESTED, VICTIM RESCUED PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) has successfully apprehended two Chinese nationals for Illegal Detention and rescued a foreign national following a targeted operation in a village in Muntinlupa City on 05 February 2026. The operation was initiated following a distress complaint from a friend of the victim. The victim, also a Chinese national, was reportedly being held against his will inside a villa and forced to work as an encoder for an online scamming syndicate. Investigation revealed that the victim was subjected to physical abuse and death threats to prevent him from escaping. The breakthrough in the case occurred when the victim managed to covertly send distress messages, including photographs and GPS coordinates, to his friend. NBI-NCR agents used this data to pinpoint the location and execute a swift rescue. During the operation, NBI-NCR agents successfully secured the victim and arrested two Chinese Subjects identified as the individuals responsible for supervising and detaining him. The Subjects are facing primary charges for the violation of Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal Detention) and have already been presented for inquest proceedings. Additionally, the operation led to the detention of eight other foreign nationals who were taken to the NBI Headquarters for verification after they failed to provide valid immigration documents or a legitimate explanation for their presence at the villa. NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno highlighted the operation as a testament to the bureau’s rigorous efforts to dismantle organized crime networks, reaffirming that the NBI remains a vigilant shield against forced labor and illegal activities in the country. Standing firmly as a guardian of justice, Acting Director Magno stated that the NBI is unequivocally committed to pursuing those engaged in unlawful activities. He further emphasized that with a steadfast dedication to integrity and public safety, the bureau will employ all necessary resources and strategies to bring offenders to justice and maintain the rule of law in society. The NBI is currently conducting follow-up operations to dismantle the scamming activities linked to the premises and to identify further members of the syndicate. #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } After evading the law for two years, expelled Congressman Arnolfo Teves Jr. has finally returned to the Philippines. On May 29, 2025, a team led by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Judge Jaime B. Santiago, together with representatives from the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Bureau of Immigration (BI), successfully brought Teves back to the Philippines. Following the Timor-Leste Deportation Order against Teves, the DOJ immediately formed a team to facilitate Teves’ repatriation. At 11:00 pm of May 29, 2025, a Philippine Air Force plane carrying Teves arrived at the Philippine Airforce (PAF) headquarters at Villamor Air Base in Pasay City. Teves, together with the arresting team, proceeded to the NBI Headquarters in Pasay City for standard booking procedures and medical examination. He was also afforded his opportunity to consult with his counsel and his mother. On May 30, 2025, the NBI, after a press briefing, brought Teves to the NBI Detention Facility in Building 14, New Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City. Teves shall remain there while awaiting the order of the courts having jurisdiction over his person. Teves Jr. was implicated in the assassination of Negros Oriental Governor Roel Degamo in 2023. He is facing multiple criminal charges, including murder, frustrated murder, and attempted murder in connection with the Degamo killing. Teves has also been implicated and charged in several other killings in Negros Oriental. Director Santiago acknowledge that this was a team effort of the Department of Justice (DOJ), the Bureau of Immigration (BI), and the Philippine Air Force (PAF). He also thanked the government of Timor-Leste for its cooperation in processing Teves’ deportation.

body: The NBI clearance finally has a permanent home, following the blessing of a four storey building in simple rites at the NBI main office compound today. Justice Secretary Leila M. de Lima was the guest of honor and cut the ceremonial ribbon assisted by NBI Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula and other NBI officials. The building houses a holding area for the clearance applicants and has a far better ventilation and the seats for queuing applicants. Construction began at the time of former NBI Director, Atty. Nestor M. Mantaring, and completed under the present administration of Director, Atty. Magtanggol B. Gatdula. In July 4, 2011, the NBI implemented the new Biometric clearance system which shorten the steps in securing an NBI clearance. An outstanding feature is the biometric reader used in taking fingerprints, thus doing away with the usual smudgy ink before. The process of application starts with a) filling up of form; b) data check; c) payment; d) encoding; and e) biometrics (fingerprints and photo). Aside from securing NBI clearances at the main facility, one can also apply at any of the five (5) Robinson’s mall branches in Ermita, Manila, Otis in Paco; Galleria in Ortigas Avenue, Quezon City; Metro East Pasig and in Cainta, Rizal. It has also clearance satellites in Ever Gotesco Monumento, Caloocan City; Grand Central, Caloocan City; Manila Plaza in C. M. Recto Avenue; and Ever Gotesco in Commonwealth Avenue, Quezon City. Likewise, clearance satellites in Quezon City Hall; Mandaluyong City Hall; and Muntinlupa City Hall can service the public. Fifteen (15) other satellite offices can serve the public in fifteen (15) provinces nationwide.

CRISTINA TAGLE y MADRID, owner of BIG NIGHT BOSS 108 KTV (KTV Bar) and BERNADETTE PINE y SANCHEZ a.k.a. “MOMMY B”, who offered female victims to the undercover agents to perform sexual services in exchange for a fee of Php5,000.00 each. The two (2) subjects were arrested in flagrante inside the KTV Bar by the NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) for violation of R.A. 9208, otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862. On October 21, 2022, after intelligence gathering and surveillance operations, NBI-BULDO together with representatives from Provincial Welfare Development Office of Bulacan, proceeded to the target KTV Bar for an entrapment operation. Two (2) poseur-clients were offered two (2) women to table with the former, while two (2) others were also offered to perform sexual services in exchange for a fee. Upon completion of the transaction, the NBI-BULDO operatives effected the arrests of the subjects. In the course of the operation, operatives were able to recover the marked money and rescue eighteen (18) trafficked victims. The arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Bulacan.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 26, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI LAUNCHES NBI CLEARANCE CENTER AT BATANES SATELLITE OFFICE Basco, Batanes – In a significant step toward bringing government services closer to the people, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) formally launched the NBI Clearance Center at Batanes Satellite Office on June 24, 2026, at the Provincial Capital Complex in Basco, Batanes. The launching ceremony was attended by provincial and regional officials, led by Governor Ronald “Jun” P. Aguto, Jr., Vice Governor Jonathan Enrique V. Nanud, Jr., and NBI Regional Director Jerry Y. Abiera, along with representatives from various local government offices and stakeholders. The establishment of the NBI Satellite Office and NBI Clearance Center marks a milestone for the province, providing residents clearance services without the need to travel outside the island province. The new facility is expected to improve public access to government services through faster and more convenient processing of NBI clearances. During the ceremony, officials emphasized the importance of collaboration between the NBI and the Provincial Government of Batanes in ensuring that public services reach even the most geographically isolated communities. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag welcomed the development, describing it as part of the Bureau’s continuing commitment to public service and institutional accessibility. “The opening of the NBI Batanes Satellite Office and Clearance Center brings our services closer to the people of Batanes. This reflects our commitment to making justice, public service, and government assistance more accessible to every Filipino, regardless of location,” Director Matibag said. Following the inauguration and ribbon-cutting ceremony, attendees witnessed a demonstration of the NBI Clearance application process, showcasing the streamlined services now available to the residents of Batanes. The launch of the NBI’s Clearance Center in the Province of Batanes forms part of the Bureau’s broader effort to expand its presence nationwide and ensure that efficient, reliable, and responsive public service reaches communities across the country.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation today announced it will host the first International Conference-Workshop on Borderless Justice. The 3-day Conference dubbed “BORDERLESS JUSTICE: A Conference-Workshop to Enhance Transnational Crime Investigation and International Law Enforcement Cooperation” will be held at the Pan Pacific Hotel in Manila on December 09 – 11, 2015. NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez said that the 3-day Conference will have delegates from about 24 foreign counterparts from Asia, Middle East, Europe and America. He also said that representatives from agencies of the government such as the Department of Justice, Bureau of Immigration, Department of Foreign Affairs, Philippine Center for Transnational Crime – NCB Manila, Philippine National Police and Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency are expected to attend the Conference. Mendez stressed that one of the objectives of the Conference is to strengthen greater cooperation among the various local and foreign law enforcement agencies to combat and neutralize, if not eradicate, transnational crimes. He emphasized “These strategies could be effective only if we and our foreign counterparts know how and where to file request for law enforcement or investigative assistance using fast, efficient, secured and real-time communication”. Mendez added that identifying the basic organizational structure of every participating country’s agency that is primarily involved in investigating transnational crimes will greatly contribute to maximize and obtain real time assistance. Among the topics to be covered during the international conference include EXTRADITION, MUTUAL LEGAL ASSISTANCE, (MLA) TRANSFER OF SENTENCED PERSONS (TSPA) and LAW ENFORCEMENT TO LAW ENFORCEMENT COOPERATION with emphasis on Human Trafficking, Cybercrime, Illicit Drugs, Terrorism and violations of Environmental Laws. Head Agents Auralyn Pascual, Chief of the Bureau’s Training Division and Daniel Daganzo, Chief of the International Operations Division, have been designated Chairperson and Vice-chairperson of the Steering Committee of the Conference, respectively.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In a simple ceremonies marking its 3rd Anniversary, the Philippine Internet Crimes Against Children Center (PICACC) will gather to forge a stronger partnership to end Online Sexual Exploitation of Children (OSEC). Now on its 3rd year, PICACC has recorded a total of 134 rescued victims and the arrest of 15 offenders from 51 operations from February 27, 2021 up to March 04, 2022. Established in 2019 to combat the increasing cases of online sexual exploitation of children, PICACC counts among its member-agencies the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), Philippine National Police (PNP), National Crime Agency (NCA), Australian Federal Police (AFP), Dutch National Police (Politie) and International Justice Mission (IJM). The first two years of collaboration among the member-agencies of PICACC show a record of 154 rescued victims and the arrest of 48 sexual offenders in 52 operations from February 27, 2019 up February 26, 2020. For the period February 27, 2020 up to February 26, 2021, total number of rescued victims has reached 238 and the arrest of 50 offenders in 76 operations. Atty. Janet Francisco, Chief of the NBI-AHTRAD currently heads the PICACC as Chairperson. Despite the pandemic brought about by COVID-19, the recorded accomplishments were achieved through the joint efforts of the NBI-Anti Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) and PNP Women and Children Protection Center (WCPC).

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NAIA-DRUG TASK GROUP INTERCEPTS OVER PHP 56.7-M WORTH OF SHABU IN DUAL INTERDICTION OPERATIONS; THREE SUSPECTS IMPLICATED The NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (IAID), in close coordination with the NAIA Anti-Illegal Drug Interdiction Task Group (NAIA-AIDITG), successfully neutralized two separate drug smuggling attempts in Pasay City, resulting in the total seizure of 8,402 grams of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride (shabu) valued at Php 56,720,200.00. The first operation took place on May 6, 2026, at the Customs International Arrival Area of NAIA Terminal 1. Authorities arrested two (2) female individuals, both residents of Novaliches, Quezon City, after arriving on Philippine Airlines flight from Phnom Penh, Cambodia. A customs inspection of their luggage uncovered 8,324 grams of shabu, with a drug price value of Php 56,603,200.00. Both Subjects are facing inquest proceedings at the Department of Justice for violation of Section 4 (Importation) of Article II of Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The second operation, a local cargo interdiction occurred on May 19, 2026, at the AP Cargo hub along Domestic Road, Pasay City. Task group elements intercepted an outbound parcel sent from Merville, Paranaque City, which was consigned to a recipient in Tagbilaran, Bohol. Upon inspection, law enforcers discovered 78 grams of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride (shabu), valued at Php 117,000.00, deliberately concealed inside three (3) “MOMOM” plastic containers and falsely declared as Foodstuff. This second incident constitutes a violation of Section 26 in relation to Section 5 (Transportation/Delivery), Article II of Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). In compliance with the legal protocols, all confiscated illegal drugs from both operations were formally marked and inventoried in the presence of required witnesses, including media representatives, and elected barangay officials, before being turned over to the PDEA Laboratory Service for forensic examination, custody and safekeeping.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 12, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested a Fire Inspector of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) for Robbery/Extortion. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by a BFP applicant against Subject ROY SANGUEZA MAT. CASTRO for alleged Robbery/Extortion. According to the complainant, Subject Castro demanded a large sum of money in exchange for the approval of her application. The complainant asserted that she had fulfilled all the necessary requirements and was fully qualified for the position, but, her application was denied, allegedly due to her lack of a “backer.” The complainant stated that Subject Castro demanded Php 400,000.00, explaining that the complainant was the third candidate for the Fire Safety Officer I position and the amount being asked was a “thanksgiving money” for her inclusion in the final roster of candidates to be sworn in as Fire Safety Officers. The demands were made through persistent phone calls and messages. As a result, on June 27, 2025, NBI-CEVRO agents conducted an entrapment operation in Cebu City, which led to the arrest of Subject Castro. Cases for violation of Section 3 of R.A. No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, Direct Bribery under Article 310 of Revised Penal Code, and Grave Misconduct under R.A. No. 6713 otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, were filed before the Office of the Ombudsman-Visayas. The arrest of Subject ROY SANGUEZA MAT. CASTRO reaffirms the NBI’s commitment to upholding integrity and accountability in its operations, underscoring that the Bureau does not tolerate any form of corruption committed by government personnel. In its Resolution dated June 30, 2025, the Office of the Ombudsman found ROY SANGUEZA MAT. CASTRO administratively liable for violating Section 7 (d) of R.A. No. 6713 and Grave Misconduct. Accordingly, Subject Castro was dismissed from service with perpetual disqualification from holding office, forfeiture of retirement benefits (except for accrued leave credits), cancellation of his Civil Service Eligibility, and a prohibition from taking Civil Service Examinations.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT September 01, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of JENALYN JOY G. HIERCO by the operatives of NBI-Anti Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) in an entrapment operation in Pasig City for violation of R.A. 9208 as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862, otherwise known as “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022” and R.A. 7610, otherwise known as “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act.” The operation stemmed from information received by the NBI-AHTRAD that a certain “Myka” has been recruiting and offering minor girls online to her clients for the purpose of sexual exploitation for a fee in Pasig City. Investigation conducted by NBI-AHTRAD confirmed that Myka offers female victims, ages ranging from of 15 to 17 years old for sexual intercourse in exchange for Php5,000.00. Thus, NBI-AHTRAD arranged and planned a possible entrapment operation to apprehend Myka and put an end to the exploitation of her minor victims. NBI-AHTRAD operatives were able to communicate with Myka thru Facebook and agreed to meet at a restaurant along Shaw Boulevard, Pasig City. On August 25, 2022, NBI-AHTRAD operatives proceeded to the said meeting place and were met by Subject Hierco, Myka’s cohort. A few moments later, minor victims arrived and were indeed offered to perform sexual services. Upon handing over of the entrapment money to Subject Hierco, the operatives immediately announced their authority and her arrest. The operation also resulted in the rescue of six female victims, five of whom are minors. The rescued victims were later turned over to the custody of the local Social Welfare Office. On August 26, 2022, Subject Hierco was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice, Ermita Manila. Meanwhile, further investigation is being conducted by NBI-AHTRAD on “Myka.”

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 31, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI HONORS “MODERN-DAY BABAYLANS”; RECOGNIZES 92 FEMALE LEADERS IN NATIONAL WOMEN’S MONTH CELEBRATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), led by Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, officially joined the nation in celebrating National Women’s Month, adopting the 2026 theme: “WE for Gender Equality and Inclusive Society – Lead Like the Babaylans, Filipinas!” Through its Gender and Development – Focal Point System (GAD-FPS), the Bureau launched a series of high-impact initiatives aimed at empowering its female workforce and reinforcing a culture of safety and professional excellence. The celebration commenced with the NBI’s active participation in the Philippine Commission on Women (PCW) kick-off held at the Rizal Memorial Stadium on March 06, 2026. Following this national launch, the Bureau rolled out a comprehensive set of activities for both Manila-based and regional office personnel. These efforts included the distribution of freebies to all female employees and the conduct of vital wellness seminars. These educational forums addressed frequently overlooked health concerns such as hyperacidity, gallstones, and HIV awareness, while also providing critical legal orientations on the Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313) and the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act (RA 9262). A significant highlight of the month-long observance was the formal recognition of 92 female NBI leaders, celebrated as the primary driving forces of change within the Bureau. The event featured Honorable Rene Ann Lourdes Matibag, Representative of the First District of Laguna, as the Guest Speaker. In her address, she emphasized that women were never intended to be secondary and have always been meant to lead. Demonstrating her commitment to the cause, Representative Matibag further supported the Bureau’s female employees by facilitating the distribution of free HPV vaccines. The program was further enriched by a lecture from Retired Justice Helen Sandoval-Gutierrez, who spoke extensively on the integration of leadership and integrity in women’s empowerment. In his closing remarks, Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag reaffirmed the NBI’s unwavering dedication to fostering an inclusive and progressive environment. He pledged that the Bureau will continue to build a workplace where women are safe, respected, and fully supported as they lead with strength, integrity, and compassion. #NBIServes #NWMC2026

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 04, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested FLORDELISA SPRINGAEL ALMODAL, JOCELYN ESTANISLAO CONSTANTINO, THERESA MARIE S. REYES, MERCY YÑGOC LIMBO, MARIE ANN YÑGOC BACULO, and RONNIE VIRATA TAN in an entrapment operation in Mandaluyong City for alleged Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. In addition, Subjects Tuazon and Reyes (both at-large) were included in the charge.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On May 27, 2024, the National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) conducted an entrapment/rescue operation against BREATHINGSPACE HEALTH SPA located at France St., Betterliving, Don Bosco, Parañaque for violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended. Information received from a confidential informant revealed that the subject establishment is owned and managed by a certain “Nelson”, and offers female sex workers. The operation resulted in the rescue of three (3) female trafficked victims, and seizure of unused and used condoms and other items. During the operation, the owners/operators of the said establishment were nowhere to be found. NBI-OTCD will conduct thorough investigation against the reported owner NELSON CALIMOSO, and a certain ABIGAEL D. PISTON who was identified based on the business permit/s and certificates found in the premises.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 01, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against the local terrorist groups in the country, the NBI-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (NBI-BARMM) has arrested LUTRE AMAN in Cotabato City. Subject Aman was arrested by virtue of a Warrant of Arrest for Murder and Multiple Frustrated Murder issued by the Regional Trial Court (RTC), Branch 23, Kidapawan City and Destructive Arson under Section 2 (4) in relation to Section 5 of Presidential Decree 1613 issued by RTC, Branch 16, Kabacan, Cotabato. The operation arose from information received by the NBI-BARMM that a certain Lutre Aman, a known member of Daulah Islamiyah – Hassan Group, a local terrorist group involved in a series of bombings in Maguindanao and nearby provinces, is roaming around Cotabato City. Subject Aman, a known bomb expert, was responsible for the bombing of a bus in January 2021 in Tulunan, North Cotabato, which resulted in the death of a fruit vendor and wounding of many others. Additionally, he was responsible for the burning of another bus in June 2021 in Miang, Cotabato. Verification made with the Regional Trial Courts in Cotabato confirmed that Aman has standing warrants of arrest. Thus, through a confidential informant, the agents of NBI-BARMM were able to locate the current whereabouts of Subject Aman, who was seen in Penafrancia Village, Rosary Heights 11, Cotabato City. On June 19, 2025, NBI-BARMM agents went to the location of Subject Aman who was spotted standing by at the parking area of an establishment in Cotabato City and implemented the warrants, which resulted in his arrest. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-BARMM for the successful operation leading to the arrest of the terrorist group member.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation-Anti Graft Division (NBI-AGD) has filed graft charges against 20 officials and employees of National Center for Mental Health (NCMH) and 3 private individuals for violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), and Gross Negligence and Serious Dishonesty in relation to the procurement and payment of a CT Scan Project amounting to Php 30,407,706.25. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said among those charged before the Office of the Ombudsman include DR. BERNARDINO VICENTE, retired NCMH Medical Center Chief II; and incumbent officials and employees of NCMH, namely: DR. BEVERLY A. AZUCENA, CLARITA A. AVILA, DIONISIO A. TOLENTINO, DULCE V. VALERIO, CPA, GODOFREDO S. VALLES, MPA, DR. JENKIN L. GO, ENGR. ESTEBAN L. GAMUROT, DR. ALDEN CUYOS, DR. JUMELYN PEREZ, DR. CYNTHIA AGUSTIN, MS. BELMA CRUZ, MS. PUBLIO PLOTENA, DR. CHRISTOPHER CHRISTIAN S. CHU, JERRY RODRIGUEZ, ARTURO C. SALCEDO, DR. EVELYN P. BELEN, ENGR. DARWIN P. PASTOR, SOLIDAD G. YAMBAO, MA. CHARINA CONCEPCION O. ABERIN, and private individuals PORTIA BAVIERA of Technomed International Inc., RONALD T. TAN, General Manager of RJJL Construction and Trading and RONALD ALLAN GACOSCOS, General Manager of GACOSCOS Construction. Director Gierran said the case stemmed from the complaint of the Employees Association of NCMH. Investigation disclosed several irregularities in the procurement of CT Scan Equipment which includes non-compliance with the requirements of RA 9184 and Department of Health. He said the investigation also disclosed that notwithstanding the inoperability and non-functionality of the CT Scan Equipment, NCMH accepted and paid Php 24,500,000.00 to Technomed Int’l Inc. Moreover, the CT Scan Project was split into four (4) contracts with aggregate cost of Php 30,407,706.25 despite only an approved budget cost of Php 26,800,000.00 as per Sub-Allotment Advise (SAA) No. 2017-08-1646, purposely to circumvent the requirements of the law and the necessity of competitive bidding. Further, it can be gleaned from the procurement documents of the CT Scan Building that it was intended to be constructed and to be bid by phases. However, there is no clear delineation of work for each phase and no detailed engineering activities that would justify implementation of infrastructure project by phases. Subject NCMH officials accepted the delivery made by Technomed Int’l Inc. and RJJL Construction and Trading despite failure of the contractors to comply with provision of “Testing and Commissioning” as mentioned in the contract. The contractors were paid in full amount. In addition, liquidated damages amounting to Php 4,753,000.00 and Php 62,503.44 were not imposed upon Technomed Int. Inc. and RJJL Construction and Trading for the delay in the delivery of the CT Scan Equipment and Building. What is more disadvantageous to the government is that the warranty provision lapsed while the entire CT Scan Project is neither functioning nor operational, the NBI investigation showed. It may be recalled that last July 15, 2019, criminal cases were filed before the Office of the Ombudsman against retired and erring NCMH officials and Subject contractor, Octant Builders, with regard to irregularities in the procurement and payment of NCMH Pavilion 6 amounting to Php 60,415,183.22. It was revealed that NCMH Chief Administrative Service Clarita A. Avila was an incorporator of Octant Builders. The Office of the Administrative Service has direct supervision and control over the Engineering Section and Bids and Awards Committee which has direct access to substantial information relative to NCMH bidding. Perusal of NCMH Infrastructure Projects disclosed that from year 2013 to 2018, a total of fourteen (14) infrastructure projects amounting to Php188,718,184.10 were awarded to NCMH’s preferred contactor, Octant Builders.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 18, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested KIM THI TA, RIA NUÑEZ STO. DOMINGO, and MARY JOY LLAMERA STO. DOMINGO in an operation in the City of Manila for violation of R.A. 11934 (SIM Registration Act). Information received by the NBI-OTCD revealed the illegal sale or transfer of Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) card, which are allegedly being used in illegal activities at one of the units in Orchard Residences, Masangkay Street, Tondo, Manila. The operatives of NBI-OTCD applied for a Warrant to Search the target condominium unit, which was granted by RTC Branch 15 of Manila. Thus, on April 15, 2024, the NBI-OTCD implemented said Search Warrant, which resulted in the seizure of pre-registered SIM cards, cellular phones, computer sets and GSM Modem/Text Blaster. During the operation, the operatives arrested the three (3) above-named Subjects, who were occupants of the said unit. The arrested subjects were charged for the above-mentioned violation of law.

body: “Mothers are supposed to be the protectors of their children; unfortunately, some exploit them for their own personal gains”. Thus, said NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor as he announced the rescue of two (2) Minor Female Victims in Tarlac. This is in line with the directive of Director Distor to protect the children from exploitation and other forms of abuse. Director Distor said that the rescue operation stemmed from the information relayed by Austrian Police that the two (2) female subjects communicated with an Austrian-based male citizen sending him child exploitative materials in exchange for money. Austrian Police also revealed that the subjects sent the Austrian Suspect around 100-150 videos and 500 nude pictures of children between 2017 and February 2021. The Austrian Suspect travelled to the Philippines in 2017, 2018, and 2019 where he met with the subjects together with the minor victims. Based on the intelligence report, the minor victims are most likely in the custody and control of the Subjects because they are related to each other and one of the victims is the daughter of one of the female Subjects. Thus, on March 3, 2022, NBI-AHTRAD together with the Municipal Social Workers Development Office (MSWDO) of Capas, Tarlac and Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) proceeded to the residence of the subjects, which resulted in the rescue of the two (2) female minor victims. NBI-AHTRAD positively identified the rescued victims as the same ones indicated in the intelligence report that has existing Child Exploitive Materials (CEM). The victims were taken under the custody by the Social Workers and were brought to Metro Manila for appropriate turnover to a shelter.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the celebration of SAFER INTERNET DAY which emphasizes in creating a safer digital space for children, the NBI Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) arrested three (3) individuals for violation of Republic Act 11930 or the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.” and RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act. Through foreign law enforcement collaboration, the NBI HTRAD received an information about individuals involved in exploitation of children for production of Child Sexually Abuse Materials (CSAMs) and for live streaming act in the form of sexual abuse and exploitation. These materials and live streaming content were being offered for sale across in various platforms. Following a thorough verification, NBI-HTRAD confirmed that there is indeed offering of these illicit materials made by one of the Subjects. In addition, the aforementioned Subject offered sex tourism package that involves her minor daughters for escort and sexual activities as enticement for her customers. On February 03, 2025, NBI-HTRAD applied for, and consequently secured a Warrant to Search. Seize and Examine Computer (WSSECD) issued by the Regional Trial Court, Angeles Pampanga. Then on February 06, 2025, NBI-HTRAD received an information that the Subject was again offering her four (4) minor daughters for live streaming act of sexual abuse and exploitation. Acting swiftly on the information, NBI-HTRAD launched a counter-action operation to arrest the Subject, implement the WSSECD and rescue operation. The said operation resulted in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects that were confederating in carrying out the said illicit activities. Also, NBI-HTRAD rescued eight (8 minor victims, four (4) of which were identified as victims offered for sexual exploitation. Initial forensic examination on the device showed possession of CSAMs and chatlogs that involves offering of minor victims for sexual exploitation. NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) and the NBI Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD) have answered the call to action, joining government sectors in efforts to make the internet a safer space for all, with a special focus on protecting children online.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to “dig deeper in the Alice Guo case”, the NBI-Task Force Guo has filed additional charges against twenty three (23) officials of the Local Government Unit of Bamban, Tarlac, including GUO HUA PING a.k.a. “ALICE LEAL GUO”, JOSE ANTONIO FELICIANO, WILLIAM P. CURA, LEONARDO C. ANUNCIACION, JOHNNY M. SALES, ERNESTO M. SALTING, ALVIN DALE M. SIBAL, NOEL S. RIVERA, DANILO L. LUGTU, REYNALDO L. PANGILINAN SR.,ARIEL R. ALIMURONG, ERNESTO P. GO, JOSE M. SALTING JR., NIKKO T. BALILO, FORTUNATO V. MEJIA, JAYSON S. GALANG, NESTOR C. PENA, EDUARDO D. GUTIERREZ, ROBIN S. MANGILIMAN, JOSE C. AGUILAR, RAINER Q. RIVERA, MARY ANDREI S. LACSAMANA, and MAR ANTONIO TAN. Also included in the charge were five (5) incorporators and officers of BAOFU LAND DEVELOPMENT, INC identified as BERNARD CHUA CHUA, RUIJINZHANG, BAOYING LIN, RACHELLE JOAN CARREON, and ZHIYANG HUANG a.k.a. “BOSS WANG”, five (5) incorporators and officers of HONGSHENG GAMINGTECHNOLOGY INC identified as THELMA BARROGO LARANAN, ROWENA GONZALES ENVANGELISTA, RITA S. YTURRALDE, MERLIE JOY MANALO CASTRO, and YU ZHENG CAN., and three (3) incorporators and officers of ZUN YUAN TECHNOLOGY INC identified as JAIMIELYN SANTOS CRUZ, RODERICK PAUL BERNARDO PUJANTE, and JUAN MIGUEL ALPAS. The individuals listed above were charged before the Ombudsman for violations of Section 3(e) and 3(g) of Republic Act No. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), and for the possession of prohibited interest by a public officer, as defined and penalized under Article 216 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC). The twenty-three officials of the Municipality of Bamban, Tarlac, were also administratively charged for Gross Misconduct, Serious Dishonesty, and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service. The charges stem from an investigation conducted by the NBI-Task Force Guo, which revealed several irregularities: • A 79,146-square-meter agricultural land in Anupul, Bamban, was hastily reclassified into commercial/residential use in 2019 without proper hearings, agency clearances, or compliance with the Comprehensive Land Use Plan; • Massive construction was undertaken in the BAOFU Compound despite lacking full conversion clearance. This compound later became the site of a scam hub; • Despite developments valued at approximately Php3.9 billion, only Php10,000.00 in Real Property Taxes were paid from 2019 to 2024, which is clear evidence of the Municipal Assessor’s failure to perform required assessments; and • Resolutions favoring Hongsheng and Zun Yuan were approved without supporting documents or proper deliberation. These corporations were later found to be operating large-scale human trafficking and online fraud schemes. Director Santiago commended the NBI-Task Force Guo for their diligent efforts, highlighting the meticulous investigation that uncovered crucial evidence and resulted in the additional charges against Guo Hua Ping and her cohorts.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three individuals by operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) for illegal transport of minerals in Barangay Candauai, Dumaguete City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as JOHN P. CALLAO, RANDY L. MAPA, and JOSEPH L. CALLAO. In the morning of April 28, 2021, operatives of NBI-DUMDO were patrolling at Barangay Candauai and happened to chance upon two (2) Chariot cargo vehicles travelling and loading sand and gravel. The drivers were flagged down and were asked to present their transport receipts. Examination of their delivery receipts bared to be expired as they were dated March 15 and 22, 2021. They, however, contented that at the back of the delivery receipts was written the estimated quarry/sale for the day at .5 cu.meters of April 28, 2021. This was written by the permittee known to be JJUN SUASIN. The subjects were transporting about 10 cubic meters of minerals with an estimated value of about 20 Thousand pesos. The delivery receipts were recycled which is an illegal maneuver to defraud payment of taxes due to the government. Hence, they violated RA 9175 otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act. Subjects were arrested and presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office of Dumaguete City on the same day.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two individuals in Paranaque City for trafficking of minors and rescued eleven (11) victims. Two Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted by HTRAD Agents together with representatives from a non-governmental organization on March 22, 2025. Poseur-customer met with the Subjects in a fast food chain in Sucat, Paranaque, where the Subjects presented the minor victims to the poseur-customer, who in turn was to choose among the victims. The subject told the poseur-customer that the fee for sexual service of the chosen victim is Php 2,500.00. After receiving the Php 2,500.00 boodle money, the Subject and his cohort were placed under arrest. A total of eleven (11) minor victims, with ages 14 to 16 years old, were taken to HTRAD office for their sworn statements under the supervision of DSWD Social Workers. They will undergo rehabilitative and protective programs and will be provided counselling and temporary shelter. Subjects were brought to NBI-HTRAD office for the standard operating procedures. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice, Task Force Against Trafficking for violation of R.A. No. 9208 otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, R.A. No. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act and R.A. No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 07, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Congratulations to our NBI colleagues who passed the recent Bar Examinations! The practice of law is no easy feat, nor is the journey towards it. Passing the bar while serving in the Bureau demands discipline, sacrifice, and courage, often tested in moments unseen and uncelebrated. The long nights, quiet doubts, and unwavering commitment required to endure this path are testaments not only to intellect, but to character. You chose to deepen your legal grounding not only for personal growth, but to better serve the mission of the NBI. We extend our warmest congratulations to our newly admitted members of the Philippine Bar: Atty. Joel R. Ayop – BARMM Atty. Jess D. Gadaingan – EVRO Atty. Ariel B. Nuñez – LAGDO Atty. Eingelbert E. Pulan – CTD Atty. Toni Joy A. Solano – Accounting Division Atty. Moises G. Tabcao – WEMRO Atty. Ace G. Ramoso – CARAGA We likewise acknowledge former NBI colleagues who have passed the Bar and continue to serve the public in other agencies: Atty. Baden Francis Y. Alonzo – NBI Batch 49 (now with the AMLC) Atty. Mayumi Estacio – NBI Batch 47 (now with the ADB) The opportunity to study law and to take the Bar Examinations is already a victory in itself; to pass the Bar is a grace earned through perseverance, sustained by faith, and crowned by purpose. It is a milestone that reflects both personal resolve and the support of those who believed in you along the way. We also recognize our colleagues who took the Bar and did not succeed this time. This outcome does not diminish your effort or your resolve; it simply means that the path is still being prepared for you. The courage to take the examination while carrying the responsibilities of public service is itself worthy of respect, and the Bureau stands with you as you continue your journey. To our newly passed Attorneys, the National Bureau of Investigation is proud to have you. Your success strengthens the Bureau and renews our collective dedication to truth, accountability, and justice in the service of the Filipino people. The NBI celebrates your hard-earned success. Congratulations, Pañeros and Pañeras! — Atty. Angelito DLP Magno Director National Bureau of Investigation #NBIServes

body: Four (4) suspects in the cold blooded murder of Italian missionary priest Fr. Fausto C. Tentorio were recommended for prosecution by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) before the Provincial Prosecutor of Kidapawan City, North Cotabato last week. In a report submitted to NBI Officer-in-Charge, Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas, the suspects were identified as: 1. JOSE SULTAN SAMPULNA , of Doroluman, Arakan, North Cotabato, who drove the black Yamaha DT motorbike ridden by the gunman; 2. DIMA MALIGUDAN SAMPULNA , of Purok Rang-ayan, Lower Paatan, Kabakan, North Cotabato; 3. ROBERT ATO , of Sitio Mahiwak-hiwak, Kulaman, Arakan, North Cotabato, was the driver of the blue Honda XRM motorbike ridden by JIMMY ATO; 4. JIMMY ATO , of Sitio Mahiwak-hiwak, Kulaman, Arakan, North Cotabato, who in his statement, admitted inter alia, as having acted as a “look-out” for the team of SAMPULNA, who allegedly killed Fr. Pops; Several JOHN DOES who are principals by Inducement (masterminds) by conspiring with the assassins were also included and recommended for prosecution. The recommendation for prosecution was transmitted to the Provincial Prosecutor on February 14, 2012, and docketed as IS# XII-06-INV-12B-00089 for charges of murder. A joint probe conducted by the NBI Region 12 (Koronadal Regional Office and Saranggani District Office), Region 10 (Cagayan de Oro City) and Region 11 (Davao City) in coordination with the PNP Region 12 Task Group Fausto disclosed that at about 7:20 in the morning of October 17, 2011, Fr. FAUSTO C. TENTORIO was found lying in the parking area inside the church compound. At the time of the incident, Fr. Pops (an Italian Priest) as he was fondly called, was the Parish Priest of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church in Arakan, North Cotabato. It was later discovered that Fr. Pops was murdered by unknown assasins for unknown reasons. Nine (9) eyewitnesses before, during and after the incident and were near the crime scene identified the suspects. Some of them saw DIMA SAMPULNA ride in the black motorcycle driven by JOSE SAMPULNA. Another eyewitness saw ROBERT ATO drove the Honda XRM where JIMMY ATO rode with him. Minutes after the shooting, an ambulance arrived at the crime scene and immediately brought Fr. TENTORIO to the Antipas Medical Specialists, where Fr. Pops was declared ‘Dead-on-Arrival’. In the early morning of December 29, 2011, NBI Agents, pursuant to a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court (Br.13) in Cotabato City, apprehended Subject JIMMY ATO, who stands charged for Destructive Arson with Homicide (No Bail). JIMMY ATO duly assisted by his counsel, in his sworn statement admitted that he was part of the assassination team, allegedly compose of JOSE SAMPULNA, DIMA SAMPULNA and ROBERT ATO. That, he acted as a look out and for his participation he was paid by JOE SAMPULNA the sum of One Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P1,500.00) a few days after the killing. Considering the gravity of the allegations implicating high profile personalities in the assassination of Fr. Pops, a deeper probe is being undertaken by the Task Force to firmly establish these accusations of JIMMY ATO. At present, leads are still being pursued by the Task Group that may eventually unmask other co-conspirators/cohorts in this crime.

body: In the relentless crackdown against syndicated swindling, agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) busted a Budol-Budol Gang victimizing foreigners of millions of pesos, following the arrest of the mastermind and two members during a buy-bust in Manila late last week. In a report submitted to DOJ Secretary Leila M. De Lima by Atty. Edmund Arugay, NBI Deputy Director for Special Investigation Services, the suspects were identified as: 1. ISAGANI CAMSON Y COLONA , 43, residing at AFP Officer Village, Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City, leader & financier; 2. EDILBERTO CORDETA Y NOQUERA alias JOSE CANETE , 54, with address at Punta Baja, Rizal, Palawan, back-up & lookout; and 3. ALEX ARCA Y ROMAL alias DODONG , 42, residing at Mabuhay, Gen. Santos City, South Cotabato, driver & switcher. The NBI recently received information about a group selling gold bars. Investigation disclosed that it was actually a Budol-budol gang peddling fake gold bars to foreign nationals. A buy-bust operation was planned after they were contacted during which an undercover agent with a Japanese national will buy their stuff. In the evening of January 6, 2012, NBI Reaction, Arrest and Interdiction Division (RAID) operatives under Head Agent Jonathan Ross Galicia proceeded to a 5-star hotel in Adriatico St., Ermita, Manila. With them were an undercover agent and a Japanese national who were able to convince the gang that they were interested in buying a gold bar which was priced at P5 million. Thereafter, the duo were brought to a Nissan car parked along Adriatico St. where they were shown the gold bar and tested and trailed by NBI agents. The gang then demanded for payment, and as the amount was being given to suspect Camson a pre-arranged signal was made. Operatives rushed and arrested Camson , who alleged to be an ISAFP operative. Identification cards seized from him shows that he is the President of CHRISMU Philippines, Inc., an NGO soliciting funds for underprivileged Christians and Muslims allegedly with accreditation with the PNP, NBI, DEPED, DENR, Supreme Court, AFP, Office of the President, and the United Nations. He is also the Vice-president for operations of Hideya Waste Management Corp., in Proj. 6, Quezon City. Suspect, Edilberto Cordeta, appears to be the Operations Manager of Cordealic Industries, Inc. in Punta Baja, Rizal, Palawan. Several driver’s licenses with his photos were confiscated from him with the names Jose Canete, Noel Canete, and Augusto Nunez. The third suspect, Alex Arca has several derogatory records to his name including service of sentence for swindling in Davao City. The modus operandi of the gang starts with alluring a prospective victim (usually foreign nationals) and the syndicate would pass themselves as well-off and conduct business in a 5-star hotel. They would show pictures of gold bars, researched materials and identified locations of hidden treasures. A sample of the gold bar would be shown and tested before the prospective buyer. It yields positive for gold by switching gold dust bought in a jewelry store from the one perforated from the fake gold bar. Once payment is made, the group vanishes. The group was brought before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings for Estafa under Art. 315 of the Revised Penal Code, Usurpation of Authority of Official Function (Art. 177 of RPC), Using Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name (Art. 178). Additional charges will be filed as soon as the requested documents from other government agencies arrive. They are presently in NBI custody while awaiting the disposition of their cases.
