body: In a series of Anti-Kidnapping for Ransom (KFR) and Gun-for-hire operations, Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) have arrested 4 individuals who are part of a syndicate responsible for strings of kidnap for ransom and killings of Chinese nationals. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor commended his men for the successful operation as he identified the Chinese nationals as LI TAO TAO and HUANG BAO JIAN who were arrested in a Chinese restaurant in Pasay City for selling 3 unlicensed firearms, Glock 22 cal. 40, Glock 30 cal. 45 and a Springfield XD-9 Subcompact 9mm. Follow up operation in Villamor Pasay City likewise resulted in the arrest of MARK ROVEL DE OCAMPO alias ERICK ISAYTONO DE OCAMPO whom the Chinese Subjects pointed to as their gun supplier. This led to another follow-up operation in Aseana City Paranaque on March 25, 2022 against the financiers and crime group leaders who are both foreign nationals. When the NBI-IOD operatives ordered the Subjects to disembark from their heavily tinted vehicle, they refused and instead rammed the vehicles of the operating team and tried to run over those who approached their vehicle. Thereafter, a firefight ensued and the Subjects managed to narrowly escape. The operatives immediately alarmed the Philippine8 National Police (PNP) to apprehend the subject vehicle should it pass through their areas of responsibility. Later, NBI-IOD operatives were informed that the subject vehicle was found at a nearby parking area. Subject YU JINGDONG, also a Chinese national, was brought to a hospital due to the wounds he sustained during the firefight. Unfortunately, Subject SY, TUAN DAT, later identified as Vietnamese was found lifeless inside the vehicle. NBI-Forensic Investigation Service personnel were immediately dispatched to conduct the necessary forensic examination, analysis, and processing of the crime scene. NBI Director Distor stressed that he ordered the intensification of the campaign against all forms of criminality. Just a month ago, on February 15, 2022, Subject YU JINGDONG was arrested in Okada hotel for illegal possession of firearms and ammunition and charged before the Paranaque Prosecutor’s Office. Also in the same month, Subject MARK ROVEL DE OCAMPO alias ERICK ISAYTONO DE OCAMPO, on the other hand, was charged with Kidnapping for Ransom and Serious Illegal Detention as defined and penalized under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code, R.A.8353 (Rape) and Violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act of 2012 and Sec 261(q) of BP 881 (Omnibus Election Code in relation to Comelec Resolution No.120728).

Distor commended his men for the successful operation as he identified the Chinese nationals as LI TAO TAO and HUANG BAO JIAN who were arrested in a Chinese restaurant in Pasay City for selling 3 unlicensed firearms, Glock 22 cal. 40, Glock 30 cal. 45 and a Springfield XD-9 Subcompact 9mm. Follow up operation in Villamor Pasay City likewise resulted in the arrest of MARK ROVEL DE OCAMPO alias ERICK ISAYTONO DE OCAMPO whom the Chinese Subjects pointed to as their gun supplier. This led to another follow-up operation in Aseana City Paranaque on March 25, 2022 against the financiers and crime group leaders who are both foreign nationals. When the NBI-IOD operatives ordered the Subjects to disembark from their heavily tinted vehicle, they refused and instead rammed the vehicles of the operating team and tried to run over those who approached their vehicle. Thereafter, a firefight ensued and the Subjects managed to narrowly escape. The operatives immediately alarmed the Philippine8 National Police (PNP) to apprehend the subject vehicle should it pass through their areas of responsibility. Later, NBI-IOD operatives were informed that the subject vehicle was found at a nearby parking area. Subject YU JINGDONG, also a Chinese national, was brought to a hospital due to the wounds he sustained during the firefight. Unfortunately, Subject SY, TUAN DAT, later identified as Vietnamese was found lifeless inside the vehicle. NBI-Forensic Investigation Service personnel were immediately dispatched to conduct the necessary forensic examination, analysis, and processing of the crime scene. NBI Director Distor stressed that he ordered the intensification of the campaign against all forms of criminality. Just a month ago, on February 15, 2022, Subject YU JINGDONG was arrested in Okada hotel for illegal possession of firearms and ammunition and charged before the Paranaque Prosecutor’s Office. Also in the same month, Subject MARK ROVEL DE OCAMPO alias ERICK ISAYTONO DE OCAMPO, on the other hand, was charged with Kidnapping for Ransom and Serious Illegal Detention as defined and penalized under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code, R.A.8353 (Rape) and Violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act of 2012 and Sec 261(q) of BP 881 (Omnibus Election Code in relation to Comelec Resolution No.120728).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said more than P113 Million worth of various counterfeit products of known brands were seized in Manila by operatives of the NBI – Anti Fraud Division (NBI-AFD). body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (STF) have arrested in Paranaque City a subject who has a standing Warrant of Arrest for investment scam that has victimized thousands of investors. NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as RICO JOHN COLORINES GARCIA, founder of RIGEN Marketing, an investment company based in Tagum City, Davao Del Norte and whose operations have expanded to Davao Del Sur, Davao Oriental, General Santos City and other neighboring areas in Mindanao. Distor said RIGEN Marketing is believed to be one of the biggest investment scams that ever took place in the Philippines having raked at least Eight (8) Billion Pesos from its investors in a span of 6 months. Distor said RIGEN Marketing entices the public to invest with a guaranteed return of 400% in a month or so. Allegedly, the firm is known to be operated by Foreign Exchange Players and Cryptocurrency Players. In May 2019, when the SEC issued an advisory against Rigen Marketing in consonance with the pronouncement of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte to shut down all Pyramiding Investment Schemes offering hefty returns, subject RICO JOHN COLORINES GARCIA a.k.a RICO JOHN or JOHN RIGEN announced that payouts to their investors will not be released until issues with the SEC are settled. This outraged thousands of investors of RIGEN Marketing who filed cases in court. After Warrants of Arrest were issued by the court in Tagum City on November 25, 2019 against subject RICO JOHN or JOHN RIGEN and officers of RIGEN Marketing, they absconded and had been hiding since. Based on reliable information, subject RICO JOHN is often seen in Las Piñas City. NBI-STF conducted nearly 2 months’ surveillance which it was later discovered that subject RICO JOHN bought another property in Paranaque City. On March 5, 2020, after confirming subject’s positive identification, operatives of NBI-STF proceeded to the area and announced their authority to arrest the subject. Seeking to prevent the operatives from entering the house prompted the operatives to forced open the main door. A foot race ensued but subject RICO JOHN was eventually arrested on the street leading to the exit of the subdivision.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested an individual for physical abuse and threatening a minor victim pertaining to a private video. Minor complainant, together with her parents, came to NBI-CCD to file a complaint against the Subject for Grave Threats, Slight Physical Injuries, and violations of RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004) and RA 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act), both in relation all in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On May 21, 2024, complainant told the CCD that Subject threatened her again that he would post their private video if the former would refuse to meet him. Thus, CCD operatives immediately conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought to NBI-CCD office for proper documentation, and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City on May 22, 2024.

body: In line with government’s intensified campaign against illegal gambling, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives of Anti-Organized Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested twelve (12) individuals for illegal gambling in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Arrested during the entrapment operation conducted by the NBI-AOTCD operatives were Subjects GEORGE REYES VELASCO (Supervisor), ROLAN ALLAN DE LEON RAMOS, JIM PHILIP CESAR CONCHA (Bet Collectors), EDITHA SILVESTRE CHAN (Personnel), ANTONIO ADRIANO BALORAN, BENITO HAO DY, BONIFACIO OROLFO ARBOLEDA JR., ROLANDO TUANO ORTEGA, SANNY BELLO BOBARES, ERIC CUNANAN DELA CRUZ, CHRISTIAN DE GUZMAN LANDICHO, CHUA CHI BEN (Bettors). On April 11, 2017, the NBI received a letter from Abraham Kahlil B. Mitra, Chairman, Games and amusement Board (GAB), requesting action on suspected bookie joints. One of the areas identified to have illegal bookie operations is at Park View Hotel Restaurant, KTV and Coffee Shop Co. in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Under strict orders from NBI Director Dante A. Gierran to immediately act on the request, AOTCD operatives conducted surveillance operations to validate the information. After confirmation of information, an entrapment operation was conducted last night, May 18, 2017, resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Number Games, amending certain provisions of P.D. 1602, and for other purposes), with an expected penalty of Prision Mayor or six (6) years up to twelve (12) years. All the arrested Subjects have been charged before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila. ante A. Gierran said the Korean nationals were arrested as a consequence of the implementation of a Search Warrant for violation of PD 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties on Illegal Gambling) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The arrested Subjects were identified as CHEONJI KIM, ILHWAN YANG, WONSUP YANG, JEONG HYEOK KIM and MOON KYU KANG. The NBI said the Subjects operate or manage an administrator web page for online sports betting, sports toto, and online casino. They also used this kind of modus to facilitate money laundering activities. Moreover, Subjects usually choose exclusive subdivisions as their operation venue to hide from the law enforcement arm of the government. After due coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), CCD operatives conducted the operation in the target area wherein Subjects were caught in the act of operating the said illegal activity. Director Gierran stressed that unlicensed operations as that of the Subjects deprive the government millions of pesos in revenue adding that they are in effect robbing from Philippine government. Charges for violation of P.D. 1602 in relation to R.A. 10165 were filed in an inquest against the arrested Korean nationals before the Prosecutor’s Office in Pasig City, with an expected penalty of Prision Mayor or six (6) years and one (1) day to twelve (12) years if found guilty by the Philippine Court.

Found and seized were Two Thousand Sixty-one (2,061) pieces of counterfeit LV products worth P 79,770,000.00. Charges for Violation of R.A. 8293 are being prepared against the proprietors and owners of the stalls and warehouses.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 18, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES EXPLOITED 16-YEAR-OLD MINOR; THREE ARRESTED FOR QUALIFIED HUMAN TRAFFICKING IN LA UNION PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation – Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO), in coordination with the NBI-Vigan District Office (NBI-VIDO) and the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of San Fernando, La Union, successfully arrested three individuals for Qualified Human Trafficking and rescued a minor victim during an operation in Brgy. San Francisco on February 10, 2026. The operation was the result of a referral from the CSWD involving two minor victims from Bukidnon who had escaped from a local bar. Investigation revealed that the victims were initially recruited under the pretext of restaurant work in Manila but were instead transported to La Union and coerced into working as bar girls. Exploiting their vulnerability, the suspects allegedly forced the victims to engage in sexual acts with customers for a fee of ₱1,500.00 under a “bar fine” arrangement. The establishment owner further claimed the victims owed him for airfare and other recruitment expenses. Upon confirming that another minor was still being exploited at the establishment, NBI operatives immediately conducted an entrapment and rescue operation. The mission led to the safe recovery of a sixteen (16) year old minor and the arrest of three (3) Subjects. During the search, operatives seized a sales record detailing alcoholic drinks and bar fines, as well as two notebooks containing handwritten logs of female names and corresponding transaction fees. On 12 February 2026, the City Prosecutor’s Office of San Fernando issued an Inquest Resolution affirming the legality of the operation. A Criminal Information charging the Subjects, along with two “John Does,” with Qualified Trafficking in Persons was subsequently filed before the Regional Trial Court. The charges were filed pursuant to R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). The rescued minor is currently under the care and custody of the CSWD. The Subjects have been committed to the San Fernando City Jail following a Commitment Order issued by the Regional Trial Court. NBI Acting Director stated that “The rescue of these minors and the arrest of the Subjects involved in this trafficking scheme underscore our unwavering commitment to eradicating the exploitation of the vulnerable. It is deeply concerning that recruitment for legitimate work is being used as a front for the heinous crime of human trafficking. The NBI, in close coordination with our partners in the CSWD, will move with full force to ensure that those who profit from the abuse and illegal detention of our youth are held accountable to the highest extent of the law.” #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested a Korean national for physical abuse. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric Distor identified the Korean national as KANG MIN SEOK, residing in a condo hotel in Malate, Manila. OIC Director Distor said the case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject for physical abuse and maltreatment. According to the complainant, in the evening of August 23, 2020, Subject brought a woman engaged in escort service or paid sex to their unit in the condo hotel. This upset the complainant so a fight ensued between her and the Subject, and she ended up getting beaten by Subject KANG MIN SEOK. In her sworn statement, complainant recalled how the Korean national had subjected her to physical, psychological, and economic abuse in the course of their relationship. Subject’s insatiable appetite for sexual activity which the complainant could not keep up had led her to tolerate the Subject to obtain the services of women engaged in paid sexual services. There were times, however, that she could no longer take that set up so it would lead to arguments and eventually, physical altercation. Complainant’s refusal to engage in sexual activities with him had prompted the Subject to turn his frustration on their hapless pet cats which caused the complainant so much anguish and emotional pain upon witnessing how the pets were being maltreated and mishandled by the Subject. Subject also required the complainant to join him in his use of illicit drugs which she acceded to so as not to cause further arguments. Further, Subject economically abused the complainant by purposely withholding money intended for everyday household expenses. Should she ask for it, Subject would hurl insults at her. After being positively identified by the complainant, Subject KANG MIN SEOK was placed under arrest for violation of Section 5 of RA 9262 otherwise known as Anti-Violence against Women and their Children Act of 2004. body: PRESS STATEMENT April 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI PARTNERS WITH CHILD RESCUE COALITION TO INTENSIFY FIGHT AGAINST ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION Manila, Philippines – On April 20, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), led by Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag has formalized a strategic partnership with the Child Rescue Coalition, Inc. (CRC) through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and a Deed of Donation aimed at strengthening efforts against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children (OSAEC). As part of the agreement, CRC has donated advanced digital forensic technology, including the MSAB XRY system, to support the operations of the NBI’s Violence Against Women and Children Division (VAWCD) and Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD). These tools will enhance the Bureau’s capability to extract and analyze digital evidence, enabling faster and more effective case investigations. The partnership also covers intelligence sharing, specialized training for NBI personnel, and improved coordination with international law enforcement agencies. “This collaboration significantly boosts our ability to combat child exploitation in the digital space and protect vulnerable victims,” Director Matibag said. The NBI reaffirms its commitment to relentlessly pursue offenders and strengthen partnerships that advance child protection #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2022 In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) OIC-Director ERIC B. DISTOR to eradicate the proliferation of counterfeit/fake products, the NBI announces the seizure of significant numbers of various fake products in three (3) separate operations in the City of Manila, Pasay, Caloocan and in the Provinces of Tarlac and Pangasinan. Director DISTOR said that the operations stemmed from complaints filed by the companies whose products are being counterfeited by unscrupulous individuals and being sold in the market. On May 19 and 23, 2022, NBI-NCR implemented 10 Search Warrants against NALD CONSUMER GOODS TRADING located in Pasay City; six (6) stores located in Baclaran Terminal Plaza; various warehouses located on the 6th Floor of Madrid Tower in San Nicolas, Manila; three (3) stores in Binondo, Manila; and an unnamed store located in Pasay City. The service of the Search Warrants resulted in the seizure of counterfeit/fake Gillete products (razors and blades) with an estimated value of Php 2,407,480.00. In another operation dated May 20 and 21, 2022, operatives of NBI-NCR implemented eight (8) Search Warrants against 699 BESTY ENTERPRISES CORP. located in Concepcion, Tarlac; NEW LOOK DRY GOODS store and its warehouse located in Tarlac City; SAM KEN General Merchandise located in Tarlac City; unnumbered house owned by ROSE RAMOS located in Zaragosa, Nueva Ecija; ATAW MARKETING located in Malasiqui, Pangasinan; WINSUN MARKETING located in Villasis, Pangasinan; and GOLDEN HAPPY MARKETING located in Alcala, Pangasinan. The implementation of the Search Warrants resulted in the seizure of counterfeit/fake BUTIKI aerosol spray cans worth Php 502,000.00 Lastly, on May 26, 2022, NBI-NCR culminated their anti-counterfeit drive by implementing eight (8) Search Warrants against Warehouses in the Cities of Manila and Caloocan; four (4) stalls of LUCKY STAR MASSAGE ENTERPRISE located in 168 Mall; and RENLAINE TRADING located in Pasay City. The operation resulted in the seizure of substantial numbers of counterfeit/fake Victoria Secret products and Pantene shampoo and conditioner Php 57,170,664.00. In the operations, NBI-NCR seized counterfeit/fake products with an aggregate value of Php 60,080,144.00. Director DISTOR reminded the public to refrain from buying counterfeit/fake products as these products do not undergo quality control and testing, which is harmful to health and safety of everyone.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a Cebu City local government employee in Cebu City by the NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) for Graft and Corruption. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as KARA MARIE ARCILLA BARGAMENTO. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by a vendor alleging that Subject Bargamento is a regular employee of the local government of Cebu City and Officer-In-Charge of Freedom Park Market in Cebu City. According to the complainant, Subject Bargamento is in charge with the assignment of market stalls and allegedly, the Subject unlawfully sells the right to the market stalls situated in prime locations. The right to market stalls are assigned free of charge and should have never been sold because it is a public market. The complainant also added that Subject Bargamento assured her that if she can hand in the payment of Php 100,000.00, she could own a stall of her own choice situated on her desired location. On November 23, 2021, thru Facebook Messenger the complainant and the Subject agreed to meet the following day for the payment of Php 100,000.00. Thus, on November 24, 2021, NBI-CEVRO together with the complainant proceeded to the agreed meeting place. After the complainant gave the marked money to the subject, NBI-CEVRO operatives immediately approached Subject Bargamento and announced her arrest. Subject Bargamento was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Cebu for violation of Sections 3 (b) and (c) of R.A. 3019, otherwise known as the “Anti-Graft and Corruption Practices Act”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) – International Airport Investigation Division (IAID), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested JARWIN SATINITIGAN y DE LEON on October 19, 2025, in Pasay City for Large-Scale Illegal Recruitment under Republic Act No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. No 10022, and Qualified Trafficking in Persons committed in Large-Scale under R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. No. 11862. On October 18, 2025, the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Task Force Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT) endorsed four (4) passengers, namely, EDMAR OTASIN BESING, REJOBAR CELESTE GADON, EBRAHEM LIBUCAN HADIOLA, and JERWIN DE LEON SATINITIGAN, who had arrived from Laos via Bangkok, Thailand. The aforementioned passengers had previously departed as Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) to work as Customer Service Representatives in Brunei but eventually traveled to Laos and became scammers who pretended to be Tiktok shop trainers encouraging people to invest in a fake business. Investigation disclosed that Subject SATINITIGAN recruited Victims BESING, GADON, and HADIOLA to work as online Customer Representatives in Laos in March 2025. The Victims knew Subject SATINITIGAN as a friend and GADON’s former high school teacher. Further, Subject claimed they would receive a salary equivalent to Sixty Thousand Pesos (Php60,000.00) once they started working in Laos. To facilitate an easy departure for Laos, Subject told the Victims that he would contact a certain Filipina with the nickname “AYIE” and an Arab national “RAFA”, who would secure their OFW documents from RAPID MANPOWER CONSULTANCY. Subject reasoned that by using OFW documents for Brunei, they could easily pass the strict Philippine immigration protocol, even without personally applying as OFWs for that country. On April 23, 2025, AYIE and RAFA met the Victims at a hotel near the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) Terminal 3 and provided their respective OFW documents. According to Subject, the documents were for Brunei to ensure they easily passed the immigration pre-departure formalities. Subsequently, Victims successfully departed and landed in Laos via Thailand, where they were trained not as CSRs, but as scammers. They were instructed to chat with people from America, France, UK, Malaysia, and Indonesia, encouraging them to invest in a fake TikTok Shop that sold various products. Victims sought the help of the Philippine Embassy in Vientiane, Laos, because they could no longer tolerate the fraudulent activity they were forced to do while being overworked, given low wages, and denied their salary when they failed to scam. Certification issued by the Licensing and Regulation Bureau of the Department of Migrant Workers (LRB-DMW) revealed that Subject SATINITIGAN is neither authorized nor licensed to recruit workers for overseas employment. Subject committed Qualified Trafficking in Persons by recruiting and transporting his kababayan under false pretenses, exploiting their socio-economic vulnerability, and forcing them to work under coercion and abuse for labor exploitation purposes, while facilitating their movement across borders. Thus, Subject JARWIN DE LEON SATINITIGAN was placed under arrest and was presented before the City Prosecutor, Pasay City for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested an individual in Taytay, Rizal last Tueday morning for Robbery and Hacking. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as CHRISTIAN GIL GUAVEZ y DENIEGA a.k.a. KAEL BUSTAMANTE , a Grade 12 student who works as part time bug hunter in the internet. The case stemmed from a complainant who alleged that she received messages through Facebook Messenger containing her nude photos and videos and the Facebook account that sent her those photos was using the name KAEL SATO. Complainant was threatened that if she won’t pay Php 10,000.00, her nude photos and videos will be uploaded in the internet. Complainant was then instructed by the subject to send the money to a certain money transfer code via Smart Padala which was located at Taytay, Rizal, as discovered by the operatives. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted in coordination with the owner of the money transfer. The Subject was arrested upon confirmation from the owner of the money transfer that Subject, using the name KAEL BUSTAMANTE had claimed the money using the reference number provided by the Complainant. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-CCD for the booking procedures wherein his real name, CHRISTIAN GIL GUAVEZ was revealed. It was also discovered that Subject was able to hack Complainant’s Facebook account and it was his girlfriend, JANA MIKAELA SIMBRE, still at large, who transacted with the Complainant using the name KAEL SATO. Charges for Robbery in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and violations of R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), and Commonwealth Act 142 as amended by R.A. 6085 (Anti-Alias Law) were filed against the arrested Subject.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said charges of Estafa thru Falsification of Public Document has been filed yesterday against a Quezon City employee before the Office of the City Prosecutor’s Office in Quezon City. NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) Director Max B. Salvador said the employee, later identified as ADRINANNE PATRICK C. OBALDO, was charged following his arrest in an entrapment operation in front of the QC Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) at the Quezon City hall. Salvador said the case was based on the complaint-affidavit filed before the NBI-NCR on July 20, 2015 by two (2) individuals, Julius Ramos and Maria Felisa Abel. The complainants alleged that they met Subject Obaldo, an employee of the Quezon City Government, who claimed that he has connections inside the Firearms and Explosives division (FED) of the Philippine national Police (PNP) and can facilitate the release of Permit to Carry Firearms Outside of Residence (PTCFOR) and Gun renewal License within three to four (3-4) days. The complainants also alleged that because of Subject Obaldo’s sweet words and connections, they were lured to accept Subject Obaldo’s offer and even convinced their friends to have their license facilitated because of the expedited release. They gave Subject Obaldo the total amount of P80,000.00 to facilitate the release of two (2) Gun License renewal (P10,000.00 each) and four (4) Permit to Carry Firearms Outside of Residence (PTCFOR) for P15,000.00 each. Salvador also said, as alleged in the complaint, after a visual inspection of the alleged PTCFOR, it appeared to be fake. One of the complainants, Julius Ramos decide to verify with the FED, which later certified that said gun license was still expired hence the firearms license card given by Subject Obaldo is of spurious origin. On July 21, 2015, operatives of the NBI-NCR set up an entrapment operation at the Quezon City hall BPLO. After a brief talk with complainant Abel and handing over 2 expired license cards for renewal and the entrapment money to Subject Obando, he was arrested. Likewise found in his possession were his cellular phone, which when inspected contained still pictures of PTCFOR and gun license which were falsified by Subject Obando.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Painstaking efforts of over thirty (30) National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) forensic experts and technical support personnel dispatched to Compostela Valley resulted to 342 processed bodies who where victims of Typhoon Pablo in December last year. After the onslaught of Typhoon Pablo in Mindanao last December 4, 2012, the NBI dispatched the 1st NBI-Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) team composed of medico-legal officers, DNA/forensic chemists and support personnel from NBI Manila office and regional and other field offices on December 9-15, 2012 in Compostela Valley. The group coordinated with the local government units of the province, especially the Municipality of New Bataan. The main base of operation was at Nabunturan, Compostela Valley where the team processed a total of 55 unidentified cadavers. On January 13-19, 2013, the 2nd NBI-DVI team of 13 members was deployed. The New Bataan Public Cemetery was the location of the construction of the temporary collective mass burial site and makeshift mortuary. A total of 289 unidentified bodies were processed. Each body was properly tagged and placed in a marked coffin then entombed in a correctly denominated apartment-type concrete niche above the ground pending their full identification. A month later, on February 17-23, 2013 the 3rd NBI-DVI team was sent to New Bataan, Compostela Valley for the interview and DNA sampling of relatives. A total of 342 living individuals were interviewed and their DNA samples taken. The team was augmented by local DOH personnel of New Bataan and Compostela consisting of doctors, nurses and midwives. Still numerous relatives failed to come for the scheduled and DNA sampling because of Typhoon Crising. A 4th NBI-DVI team is being planned to cover the remaining relatives for the antemortem phase, and the processing of the newly retrieved six (6) unidentified bodies which are temporarily stored in New Bataan Public Cemetery. In the past years, several natural and man-made disasters occurred which resulted to countless deaths where the NBI sent its DVI teams to help identify almost unrecognizable cadavers. Foremost of these incidents are the Cebu Pacific, Asian Spirit and Air Phil. plane mishaps, and Superferry 14 bombing, Wowwowee ULTRA stampede, Phuket, Thailand tsunami, Bgy. Guinsaugon, St. Bernard Southern Leyte landslide, Typhoon Reming in Albay province, Typhoon Sendong in Cagayan de Oro and Iligan cities, CO2 tanker explosion in Togbao, Zamboanga del Sur, Princess of the Star ship sinking, and many others. The team also worked hand-in-hand with foreign forensic experts specifically from the Interpol and ICMP to help in this process of disaster identification.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the operatives of NBI- Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) in a buy-bust operation in Iligan City for selling illegal drugs. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JESTY ESTEFANIO y ALBERT, a 31 year old carpenter and resident of Flinstones St., Celdran, Brgy. Tubod, Iligan City. OIC Director Distor said that on July 3, 2021, NBI-ILDO, conducted a buy-bust operation at Purok 24A, Zone 10, Brgy. Maria Cristina, Iligan City which resulted in the arrest of Subject Estefanio. The operatives were able to buy from the subject one (1) piece Large Size Heat-sealed plastic sachet containing shabu weighing seven (7) grams with an estimated value of Php 47,600.00. The operation also resulted in the seizure of the marked money, one (1) identification card (I.D.) one (1) improvised pipe “Babing”, one (1) cellphone, and one (1) black and white surgical mask. Subject Estefanio was then brought to NBI-ILDO where he was booked, fingerprinted, photographed, and temporarily detained. The confiscated drug evidences were forwarded to NBI-Regional Office 10, Forensic Chemistry Division for quantitative and qualitative examination. The arrested subject was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office of Iligan City for violation of R.A. 9165 for selling illegal drugs.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) enforced Search Warrants at establishment in the cities of Manila, Pasay, and Valenzuela, for violation of Republic Act No. 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” On August 05, 2025, NBI-NCR, together with the NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD), enforced ten (10) search warrants in four (4) targets located in Binondo, Manila, and one (1) in Baclaran, Pasay City, for unlawfully storing, selling, and distributing counterfeit products. The operation resulted in the seizure of 19,546 pieces of counterfeit sunglasses and prescription glasses bearing various “OAKLEY” trademarks, 42,258 pieces of counterfeit “RAY-BAN” sunglasses and prescription glasses bearing the trademarks of LUXOTTICA, and various business documents, receipts, sales invoice, including other pieces of evidence with an estimate worth of more or less 800 Million Pesos (Php 800,000,000.00). On the same date, NBI-NCR agents, along with NBI-IPRD, served two (2) warfants at a warehouse in Valenzuela City for unauthorized reproductions. The operation resulted in the seizure of 6.293 pieces of finished and unfinished products bearing counterfeit “WD-40” trademarks, 270 pieces of counterfeit canisters resembling the general appearance of WD-40 trademarks, and various business documents, including other pieces of evidence with an estimated worth of more or less 3 Million Pesos (Php 3,000,000.00) Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR and NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing the search warrants and for their law enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. The NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to protect the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against syndicated pilferages and theft of imported Customs containers, the NBI-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) arrested JOHN M. AVELES MENDOZA and ANGELO RAMOS in a hot pursuit operation on July 12, 2025, at the Arctic Cold Storage in Cainta, Rizal, for Qualified Theft and violation of Republic Act No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed against JOHN A. MENDOZA and ANGELO RAMOS, driver and helper, respectively, of JBIZ Cargo Services, who hauled the Customs’ sealed and GPS tracker-equipped container for delivery to the said cold storage facility. Investigation by the NBI-OLDO agents revealed that en route to Cainta, Rizal, Subjects tampered the Customs seal and GPS tracker, opened the container, pilfered its contents, and thereafter carried on their trip. An anomaly indicative of a breach on the GPS registered in the monitor of the Bureau of Customs, which alerted the broker, who immediately filed a Complaint with the NBI-OLDO. Agents of the NBI-OLDO, along with the BOC Examiners, proceeded to the Arctic Cold Storage and in the presence of the Department of Agriculture-BAI Personnel, the owner of the truck and herein Subjects, opened the above container. A spot inventory was conducted, showing that 224 boxes of imported meat products were missing, with the approximate amount of P1,614,000.00. Subjects Mendoza and Ramos were placed under arrest and were presented for Inquest Proceeding before the DOJ in Manila for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-OLDO for the successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subjects. He said that this operation strengthens the NBI’s commitment against Syndicated pilferages and theft of imported Customs containers.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Pursuant to the directive of NBI Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), to intensify the Bureau’s campaign against the illegal drug trade, the National Bureau of Investigation-Cebu District Office (CEBDO) arrested ALVIN PLANDO y TABANAS in a buy-bust operation in Sitio Manga, Barangay Tisa, Cebu City on June 16, 2025. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 16, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Special Task Force (NBI-STF), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested four individuals in Sta. Cruz, Manila for falsifying public documents. Director Santiago said that STF received an information regarding certain individuals allegedly engaged in falsifying public documents. Accordingly, these individuals are offering fake NBI Clearance, land titles, passport, and other documents in Santa Cruz, Manila, for a price ranging from Php 700- Php 2,500. After confirming the said illegal activity through surveillance and test buy operations, an entrapment operation was hatched. In coordination with the local police, STF operatives proceeded to the target location on October 14, 2024. The operation resulted in the arrest of PAUL CHRISTIAN ABELLERA y CALA, EDGARDO CARPIO y CRUZ, JENNY BADE TRAJANO y CEPEDA, and a minor who were caught in the act engaging in falsification of public documents. Recovered from the possession of the arrested Subjects were computers, office tools, and spurious documents such as NBI Clearance, PSA Certificate, land titles, and LTO Certificates, among others. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

Subject identified herself to be an owner of at least 32 condominium units at Birch Tower, J. Bocobo, Malate, Manila. Subject solicited from the Complainants an investment business venture wherein complainants would just pay her ranging from Php 100,000 to Php 150,000 each. In return, complainants could either occupy the property for 6 months with their investment returned after the said period or have it leased to another person, the monthly rental or proceeds of which will be payable to them. However, after paying, complainants found out that the units assigned to them were occupied by either another investor or the real owner. Verification with the Building Administrator of Birch Tower Condominium showed that Subject is not a registered unit owner of any unit of the said condominium. Apparently, one of the complainants at the time of filing, was still being persuaded by Subject LIM. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was charged for Estafa and abovementioned violations. On December 18, 2017 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized 14,118 pairs of assorted counterfeit KEDS rubber shoes and 38,666 pairs of assorted counterfeit NIKE and CONVERSE rubber shoes. The counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants. The operation stemmed from the complaints of I-Data consolidators representing NIKE and CONVERSE and BCCS Law representing KEDS. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Subjects Jay-R Go, Jimmy Ong, et.al. On December 20, 2017 , operatives of Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested TOMAS NECASIO NAZARENO in an entrapment operation in Manila for Estafa. The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who allegedly has an account wherein 30 Billion US Dollars was being deposited. According to the complainant, he was informed by a certain Pastor Gavino M. Ronquillo about the assets pertaining to the bank accounts which has deposits amounting to 30 Billion US Dollars and maintained at HSBC Thailand, and that the original signatory to the aforesaid accounts had passed away and the deposits were transferred to Subject TOMAS NECASIO NAZARENO. Pastor Ronquillo then asked the complainant if he would be interested to be financier or investor wherein he needed to provide Php 2 Million to be utilized allegedly for travel expenses and logistical needs and in turn, would be given profit or proceeds equivalent to 1% of the deposit or about 300 Million US Dollars monthly based on the guaranteed profits on the investment trading activities. After being presented with several documents, complainant was convinced and enticed that Subject’s offer of investment is valid and legitimate. Complainant transmitted an initial amount of USD 7,0000 to the Subject via Western Union and even remitted money in several tranches. However, even after the remittances, the complainant did not receive the Memorandum from Subject’s depository bank and the Standby Letter of Credit that the Subject promised. Complainant then told the Subject that another financier is willing to give the amount he was requesting and reported the matter before the NBI. Subject agreed to meet with the complainant to deliver the money amounting to Php 500,000.00 An entrapment operation was then set up that resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Cruz, Manila. On December 11, 2017 , operatives seized counterfeit NOKIA and APPLE products with an estimated amount of Php 17,800,000. Items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24 and 46, Manila. Manila. Violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various stores and stalls in Manila City Plaza, Quiapo, Manila. On December 12, 2017 , operatives seized 149,228 pieces of counterfeit medicines/drugs bearing the name of United Laboratories, Inc. (Unilab Group) amounting to about Php 1,250,000. The counterfeit medicines which were about to be distributed to the different drugstores in the provinces of Rizal and Calabarzon were seized inside the residence of ZALDY A. LOPEZ located at Block 10, Lot 6, Phase 2, Southville, Brgy. Pinugay, Baras, Rizal. Appropriate criminal charges will be filed against the Subject. On December 14, 2017 , operatives seized Php 12 Million worth of counterfeit LACOSTE items in Angeles City, Pampanga. The fake products were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does,et.al of Parkson Duty Free/Clark Trading Corporation, Clark Liberty Warehouse Club/Clark Liberty Duty Free Plza Building, and ECS Boutique. On December 15, 2017 , operatives seized Php 1,140,000,000.00 worth of counterfeit Rayban and Oakley eye wears in Sta. Cruz and Quiapo, Manila. Counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Janeth Mae General Merchandise, John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various stalls and stores all of which are located in Emerald Circle Building, Sta. Cruz , Manila, and Mabuhay Optical Supply located in Quiapo, Manila.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT August 12, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) conducted a joint operation with the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordination Center (CICC), Bureau of Immigration (BI), and government agency. The operation was initiated after a request for assistance from Deputy Executive Director of the CICC regarding the alleged distribution and use of illicit transceivers by foreign nationals staying at a top hospitality establishments in Cebu City. On June 28, 2025, the joint operation led to the arrest of CHONG HONG YEE and KIM CHUI TAN, two (2) Malaysian nationals accommodated in the hotel. They were found in possession of and operating illegal transceivers and sniffing devices (IMSI Catcher). Based on this discovery, an application for a Wattant to Search, Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSEC) was applied for the devices. On August 08, 2025, a composite team of NBI agents and officers from the CICC, the Department of Information and Communication Technology (DICT), and the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) served the cyber warrant at the Cebu City hotel. During the seizure, the Regional Cybersecurity Head of DICT-7 and a Cybercrime Investigator from the CICC confirmed that the laptops, Raspberry Pis, antennas, and other modular setups were cellular and data sniffers. They noted that the strength of the modules and antennas could capture data up to the 5G network. These findings were concurred with by the Attorney of NTC, who added that some of the tools necessitated approval from NTC prior to usage. The seized equipment will undergo an in-depth forensic examination to bolster the pieces of evidence already gathered. Meanwhile, cases for violation of Republic Act No. 10175 or the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012” are being prepared for filing.

body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On September 1, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested ENRICO LEGASPI y DELA CRUZ for Robbery-Extortion, violation of R.A. 10175 (Cyber Crime Prevention Act of 2012, and violation of R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children 2004). Subject threatened the Complainant that he will post their photographs on social media when the Complainant was trying to split up with him. Complainant begged the Subject but when the former did not follow some of the latter’s instructions, he uploaded photographs showing them kissing. Subject then demanded money from the Complainant and she sent money to the Subject via mobile banking cash deposits. When Subject demanded Php100,000.00, an entrapment operation was planned resulting in the arrest of the Subject. • On September 4, 2017, operatives of Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested EUGENIO ILAGAN y YTE for selling fake NBI Clearance in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Information from a reliable source said that Subject was offering NBI Clearance to clients along C.M. Recto Avenue, Sta. Cruz, Manila. An entrapment was then set after validation and case build. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject ILAGAN who asked for Six Hundred Pesos (Php600) in exchange for the fake NBI Clearance. Certification from the NBI-ICTD confirmed that NBI Clearance certificates from the Subject were not duly issued by the NBI. Charges for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject. • On September 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 62,442,414.90 or US$ 1,222,055.00. The fake products were seized at Greenhills Shopping Center, San Juan, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Atty. Anthony Francis L. Manankil representing Louis Vuitton. RODRIGUEZ, JOHN CLYDE M. ANGELES and CHRISTOPHER S. FERNANDEZ for violation of R.A. 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act) in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Ortiz representing Saturn Gaming N’ Entertainment Corp. and First Golden Fortune Leisure Inc., the Authorized Agent Corporations (AAC) of Mandaue City and Cebu province respectively. Paredes, Diffun, Quirino, where they were exposed in hazardous working condition and paid below minimum wage. During the operation, eleven (11) child workers were rescued and now under the protective custody of DSWD. Child labor and human trafficking charges will be filed against the incorporators of the farm. • On September 20, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), together with the PDEA II, NBI-Bayombong District Office and NBI-Isabela District Office, discovered and destructed two (2) marijuana plantation sites with a street value of Ten Million (Php 10 Million) in Brgy. Luccong, Tinglayan, Kalinga. During the operation, no apprehensions were made since there were no occupants nor tillers found in the area. Nevertheless, charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) will be filed against those who are responsible for the cultivation of the marijuana plantation. • On September 22, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JEFFREY ANDREOUS CADORNA CLAROS in Makati City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa and Qualified Theft. The case stemmed from the letter request of Roxas Delos Reyes Laurel Rosario Leagogo Law Office c/o Atty. Benjamin B. Fernando Jr to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued against the Subject who is a former accountant of their law firm, for the aforementioned crimes. Subject is temporarily detained at the NBI Jail awaiting Court Order committing him to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, Makati City. • On September 22, 2017, Subject CARLITO AMOROSO y BAGALACSA, who has an Order of Arrest for Murder issued by RTC Branch 55 of Manila, surrendered to the NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD). Subject Amoroso is one of the ten (10) accused in the death of Navy Ensign Philip Pestaño on September 27, 1995. Pestaño, a 1993 graduate of Philippine Military Academy was found dead aboard BRP Bacolod City. All of the accused were charged for Murder and Warrant of Arrest was issued against them. Upon his surrender, Subject was booked, fingerprinted, photographed, and was turned over to the NBI Jail. • On September 22, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested SPO1 JOSHUA BARILE y TUPAS for violation of PD 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 and 9516 (Codifying the Laws on Illegal/Unlawful Possession, Manufacture, Dealing in, Acquisition or Disposition of Firearms, Ammunition or Explosives or Instruments Used in the Manufacture of Firearm, Ammunition or Explosives, and Imposing Stiffer Penalties for Certain Violations Thereof, and for Relevant Purposes), violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) and R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). • On September 22, 2017, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested EDILBERTO SALAS ASIS, IVAN CHESTER MESA LOZADA, and JOSE DARAING PALEVINO for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). NBI-TFAID received information that a certain “Eding” later identified as Edilberto Salas Asis, together with Ivan Lozada y Mesa, Aaron Lozada and their cohorts are using Unit 536 of Tenement Building, Brgy. 902, Zone 100, Punta, Sta. Ana, Manila as a drug den. Series and surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City was implemented. The operation resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in flagrante having a pot session. Found and seized in the premises were methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, other drug paraphernalia, two (2) pieces live ammunition and one (1) folding knife. Based on tactical interrogation, Subject Edilberto Salas Asis was previously imprisoned for Murder while Subject Jose Daraing Palevino was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Homicide. On the other hand, Subject Ivan Chester Mesa Lozada was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Theft. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. • On September 24, 2017, operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office arrested AYNA KAMILAH ALI de MINDAMOAO y BOTERIE and MERLINDA JUMANDOS GOLANDRINA for Falsification of Official Documents. While conducting inspection to different testing centers of Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), Licensure Examination for Teachers, operatives received information of an impersonation in Pagadian City Pilot School. While thereat, they were able to apprehend the impersonator, Subject MINDAMOAO. Furthermore, Subject GOLANDRINA, the person who applied for the PRC Licensure Exam for Teachers, was also apprehended based on the information provided by the PRC Over-all Coordinator. Both were brought to the NBI-PAGDO office for proper booking procedures. • On September 26, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ALLAN LUCBAN y BALANDAY in Imus, Cavite by virtue of an alias Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 42, Manila Violation of P.D. 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 (Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunitions) with bail recommended at Php 80,000.00. Subject LUCBAN was the subject of a letter complaint of Canyon Ranch Homeowners Association Inc. (CRHAI), Carmona, Cavite, headed by its President Benjamin E. Branson, American national, for being unruly and creating a very hostile environment in the community. Subject is presently detained at the NBI detention center. • On September 26, 2017, operatives of NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested spouses REZIL ESTOY and JOELAN ESTOY for violation of R.A. 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Carlos T. Capitan II, DMD, MPD of Davao City Dental Chapter. Oh Ikjoon, Police Liaison Officer of the Korean National Police Agency, requesting for investigation, arrest and deportation of Subject YU, YONGSEOK. Dave and interpreter, Kim Junghyun. • On September 27, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested AURELIA PERALTA y VALLEJO, ELISEO DENIEGA, MARTIN PORFINIO JR, AND WILSON VALEROZO for human trafficking. Arenas, Bank Officer II of Currency Issue and Integrity Office and Currency Investigation Division of the BSP, requesting assistance for the planning of anti-counterfeit operation against certain individuals who are said to be violating Articles 166, 168 and 176 of the Revised Penal Code. Aside from the timbers, woodworking planer and chainsaw were also seized during the operation. Valdez, Head of NAECTF, then wrote a letter addressed to Director Gierran requesting the NBI to provide the necessary manpower complement for the anti-illegal logging enforcement operations. On September 21, 2017, EDUARDO ELVINA y SOLMIO and eight (8) others were arrested in Muntinlupa City while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors. Seized from them were several pieces of betting list and bet money. On September 27, 2017, RONILO AYAPANA y PAREJA and five (5) others (all jueteng Kubrador) were arrested while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors in the areas of Cupang, Alabang and Putatan, Muntinlupa City. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are several pieces of betting list and bet money. On September 4, 2017, forty one (41) counterfeit window films bearing the 3M trademark with an estimated amount of Php600,000 were seized in Davao city by virtue of Search Warrant. On September 5, 2017, counterfeit Lacoste shoes/footwears with an estimated amount of Php 19 Million were seized in Pasay and Paranaque City on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 15, 2017, counterfeit Marlboro and Fortune cigarettes with an estimated amount of Php 294,000 were seized in Tondo, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. On September 19, 2017, counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 51,934,000 were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 22, 2017, counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 21,800,000 were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various warehouses where the counterfeit products were seized.

Subject is temporarily detained at the NBI Jail awaiting Court Order committing him to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, Makati City. • On September 22, 2017, Subject CARLITO AMOROSO y BAGALACSA, who has an Order of Arrest for Murder issued by RTC Branch 55 of Manila, surrendered to the NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD). Subject Amoroso is one of the ten (10) accused in the death of Navy Ensign Philip Pestaño on September 27, 1995. Pestaño, a 1993 graduate of Philippine Military Academy was found dead aboard BRP Bacolod City. All of the accused were charged for Murder and Warrant of Arrest was issued against them. Upon his surrender, Subject was booked, fingerprinted, photographed, and was turned over to the NBI Jail. • On September 22, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested SPO1 JOSHUA BARILE y TUPAS for violation of PD 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 and 9516 (Codifying the Laws on Illegal/Unlawful Possession, Manufacture, Dealing in, Acquisition or Disposition of Firearms, Ammunition or Explosives or Instruments Used in the Manufacture of Firearm, Ammunition or Explosives, and Imposing Stiffer Penalties for Certain Violations Thereof, and for Relevant Purposes), violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) and R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). • On September 22, 2017, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested EDILBERTO SALAS ASIS, IVAN CHESTER MESA LOZADA, and JOSE DARAING PALEVINO for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). NBI-TFAID received information that a certain “Eding” later identified as Edilberto Salas Asis, together with Ivan Lozada y Mesa, Aaron Lozada and their cohorts are using Unit 536 of Tenement Building, Brgy. 902, Zone 100, Punta, Sta. Ana, Manila as a drug den. Series and surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City was implemented. The operation resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in flagrante having a pot session. Found and seized in the premises were methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, other drug paraphernalia, two (2) pieces live ammunition and one (1) folding knife. Based on tactical interrogation, Subject Edilberto Salas Asis was previously imprisoned for Murder while Subject Jose Daraing Palevino was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Homicide. On the other hand, Subject Ivan Chester Mesa Lozada was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Theft. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. • On September 24, 2017, operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office arrested AYNA KAMILAH ALI de MINDAMOAO y BOTERIE and MERLINDA JUMANDOS GOLANDRINA for Falsification of Official Documents. While conducting inspection to different testing centers of Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), Licensure Examination for Teachers, operatives received information of an impersonation in Pagadian City Pilot School. While thereat, they were able to apprehend the impersonator, Subject MINDAMOAO. Furthermore, Subject GOLANDRINA, the person who applied for the PRC Licensure Exam for Teachers, was also apprehended based on the information provided by the PRC Over-all Coordinator. Both were brought to the NBI-PAGDO office for proper booking procedures. • On September 26, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ALLAN LUCBAN y BALANDAY in Imus, Cavite by virtue of an alias Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 42, Manila Violation of P.D. 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 (Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunitions) with bail recommended at Php 80,000.00. Subject LUCBAN was the subject of a letter complaint of Canyon Ranch Homeowners Association Inc. (CRHAI), Carmona, Cavite, headed by its President Benjamin E. Branson, American national, for being unruly and creating a very hostile environment in the community. Subject is presently detained at the NBI detention center. • On September 26, 2017, operatives of NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested spouses REZIL ESTOY and JOELAN ESTOY for violation of R.A. 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Carlos T. Capitan II, DMD, MPD of Davao City Dental Chapter. Surveillance operations were conducted leading to the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for the aforementioned violation were filed against the Subjects. • On September 27, 2017, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested YU, YONGSEOK, a Korean national who is wanted for prosecution for Special Robbery as he and his cohorts committed robbery with abduction against three (3) Korean victims in Cebu City, Philippines last 2013. Warrant of Arrest against the Subject has been issued by the Seoul Central District Court of the Republic of Korea. The NBI received a letter request from PSupt. Oh Ikjoon, Police Liaison Officer of the Korean National Police Agency, requesting for investigation, arrest and deportation of Subject YU, YONGSEOK. An Interpol Red Notice was then issued against the Subject. After securing an authorization to apply for Provisional Arrest Warrant pursuant to the provisions of the Treaty on Extradition between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of the Philippines, in relation to P.D. 1069, an Ex-Parte Application for Provisional Arrest of Subject YU, YONGSEOK was filed. Thus, RTC Branch 45. Manila issued a Provisional Arrest prelude to a Formal Request for Extradition. On the above-mentioned date, joint operatives of NBI-IOD and NBI-IPRD proceeded to Lucksea Global Corp. located at the Penthouse of Shaw Center Mall, Shaw Blvd., Mandaluyong City and served the Provisional Warrant of Arrest against YU, YONGSEOK. Subject was then brought to NBI where he underwent the proper booking procedures in the presence of his counsel, Atty. Jose Valentino G. Dave and interpreter, Kim Junghyun. • On September 27, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested AURELIA PERALTA y VALLEJO, ELISEO DENIEGA, MARTIN PORFINIO JR, AND WILSON VALEROZO for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation wherein Subject PERALTA was caught en flagrante delicto sexually exploiting women while Subject DENIEGA was facilitating the trafficking of victims. Meanwhile, Subjects PORFINIO JR and VALEROZO were arrested after being caught en flagrante delicto having carnal knowledge with two (2) trafficked victims. The operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding the alleged illegal activities at Angie’s Kambingan and Restaurant located in Ramon, Isabela. Said establishment is allegedly being used as a prostitution den. Validation of the intelligence report was conducted confirming the said report. Entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and rescue of the victims. Charges for violation of R.A. 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were prepared against the arrested Subjects. • On September 28, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) rescued two (2) minors and a twenty-two year old woman who were victims of pornography in Batangas City. An information was provided by the Australian Federal Police (AFP) that a certain facebook user with an account username “Gyeong Aerum” believed to be Subject Angelica Camille Vilaruz y Custodio who is working in Malaysia was engaged in the distribution of child pornography materials. A surveillance operation was conducted confirming the information. Coordination with the Barangay Officials and the parents of the victims were made. Surrounding circumstances were explained to the parents and guardians of the victims. The victims were then peacefully turned over to the DSWD for custody. • On September 28, 2017, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested CHARLIE QUINTANA y LANTICSE alias DARLING for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit). The case stemmed from the letter of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas thru Nestor H. Arenas, Bank Officer II of Currency Issue and Integrity Office and Currency Investigation Division of the BSP, requesting assistance for the planning of anti-counterfeit operation against certain individuals who are said to be violating Articles 166, 168 and 176 of the Revised Penal Code. Said individuals, accordingly, proliferate counterfeit Philippine, United States and other foreign currency bank notes in Cagayan de Oro City and nearby provinces, cities and municipalities. Entrapment operation was then conducted against the Subjects resulting in the arrest of Subject CHARLIE QUINTANA. Seized from his possession were several counterfeit bills. • On September 28, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested ERWIN VILLEGAS y QUIRAO and ROLLY MARTIN y LUTCHING for illegally keeping timbers or lumbers with an estimated amount of Php 50 Million in Barangay Bagbag, Novaliches, Quezon City. The joint operation of NBI-EnCD and Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the seizure of various timbers or lumbers of narra, yakal, molave, bolong, and other species, arose from the issuance of Search Warrant issued by RTC 94, Quezon City. Aside from the timbers, woodworking planer and chainsaw were also seized during the operation. The joint operation was conducted in compliance with the directive of the President of the Republic of the Philippines RODRIGO ROA DUTERTE to enforce total logging moratorium particularly, mandating the Department of the Environmental Crime Task Force (NAECTF) to formulate an OPLAN to be implemented in coordination with the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine National Police (PNP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Department of Justice (DOJ), the Ombudsman, and this Bureau. DENR USEC Arturo T. Valdez, Head of NAECTF, then wrote a letter addressed to Director Gierran requesting the NBI to provide the necessary manpower complement for the anti-illegal logging enforcement operations. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Inquest Prosecutor, DOJ for violation of PD 705 as amended by Executive Order No.277 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines), violation of R.A. 9175 (An Act Regulating the Ownership, Possession, Sale, Importation and Use of Chainsaws, Penalizing Violations Thereof and for Other Purposes), and R.A. 1950 (An Act Regulating the Operation of Sawmills, Requiring Operators of Sawmills to Obtain from the Director of Forestry Permits for the Operation of Such Sawmills, and Providing Penalties for Violations Thereof). • In three (3) separate operations, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested a total of thirty (30) individuals engaged in illegal gambling operations. The operations stemmed from the request of Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) Chairman to curb illegal gambling and based on the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) that operates small town lottery in Southern District of National Capital Region that illegal number game still proliferates and remained unabated in Muntinlupa City. On September 20, 2017, ANNIE REYES y PANTIG and thirteen (13) others were arrested while engaged in jueteng operations in Taguig City. Seized from them were jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. On September 21, 2017, EDUARDO ELVINA y SOLMIO and eight (8) others were arrested in Muntinlupa City while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors. Seized from them were several pieces of betting list and bet money. On September 27, 2017, RONILO AYAPANA y PAREJA and five (5) others (all jueteng Kubrador) were arrested while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors in the areas of Cupang, Alabang and Putatan, Muntinlupa City. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are several pieces of betting list and bet money. Subjects in all the operations shall be charged for violations of P.D. 1602 (Simplifying and Providing Stiffer Penalties for Violations of Gambling Laws) as amended by R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) before the City Prosecutor Office of Muntinlupa City. • In five (5) successive operations, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit items with an aggregate amount of Php 93,628,000.00. On September 4, 2017, forty one (41) counterfeit window films bearing the 3M trademark with an estimated amount of Php600,000 were seized in Davao city by virtue of Search Warrant. On September 5, 2017, counterfeit Lacoste shoes/footwears with an estimated amount of Php 19 Million were seized in Pasay and Paranaque City on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 15, 2017, counterfeit Marlboro and Fortune cigarettes with an estimated amount of Php 294,000 were seized in Tondo, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. On September 19, 2017, counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 51,934,000 were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 22, 2017, counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 21,800,000 were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various warehouses where the counterfeit products were seized.

body: As a symbol of trust and confidence in the leadership of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), President Rodrigo Roa Duterte (PRRD) appointed current NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor to Director V as Senior Deputy Director (SDD). The President also promoted to Director V (Deputy Director) Atty. Antonio M. Pagatpat, incumbent Assistant Director for Regional Operations Service (ADROS). Both Distor and Pagatpat previously held the positions of Director IV and are career agents who graduated from the NBI Academy and rose from the ranks to their present positions. Along with the appointments of Distor and Pagatpat, thirteen (13) other career Agents got their appointment from the President. Six (6) were promoted to Director III (Regional Director) namely: Atty. Renan Augustus T. Oliva, Atty. Emeterio A. Dongallo, Jr., Atty. Arcelito Cernal Albao, Atty. Claro C. De Castro, Jr., Atty. Victor John Paul H. Ronquillo, and Atty. Janet M. Francisco. Seven (7) Career Agents were likewise promoted to Director II (Assistant Regional Director), namely: Investigation Agent IV Noel C. Bocaling, Investigation Agent VI Glenn A. Ricarte, Investigation Agent III Joel R. Ayop, Investigation Agent VI Victor V. Lorenzo, Investigation Agent V Hazel P. Roxas, Investigation Agent III Gerald L. Intes, and Investigation Agent V Isaac R. Carpeso, Jr. The newly appointed NBI officials committed to exert their full effort and dedication to perform their duties and responsibilities as public officials. Distor emphasized, that “the government and the people deserve our service and we will continue to perform what is expected of us. This is our way of expressing our appreciation to the President.” Distor added, “the NBI needs to cater to the expanding functions of the Bureau as we respond to the increasing cases of criminality confronting our society such as cybercrimes, human trafficking, illegal drugs, white collar crimes,and other cases of fraud and crimes against environmental laws”. Distor stressed that NBI now responds quickly, solves crimes immediately and clears the headlines. “Quick law enforcement and police actions including the arrests and neutralizations of criminal elements will result in Political stability, Investor confidence, Bigger Economic Gains, Many job opportunities in the country and will finally result in attaining lasting Peace and Order, and Prosperity that will lift up and save more Filipino lives from hunger and poverty”, Distor added.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES ₱761K WORTH OF COUNTERFEIT SKINCARE PRODUCTS IN MANILA AND BULACAN RAIDS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has dealt a significant blow to the trade of counterfeit cosmetics following a coordinated enforcement operation targeting the proliferation of fake Korean skincare products. The operation was launched following a complaint and request for investigation into the widespread proliferation and illicit distribution of counterfeit skincare products bearing the ‘Beauty of Joseon’ trademark. On March 12, 2026, operatives from the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), supported by representatives from the NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD), implemented a series of search warrants at various retail stores in Binondo, Manila, and a distribution warehouse in Marilao, Bulacan. The operation resulted in the seizure of Eight Hundred Forty-Six (846) pieces of assorted counterfeit serum bearing the trademark of the popular Korean skincare brand, “BEAUTY OF JOSEON.” The confiscated items have an estimated market value of approximately Seven Hundred Sixty-One Thousand Four Hundred Pesos (₱761,400.00). The NBI-IPRD is set to file criminal cases for Trademark Infringement under Section 155, in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) against the identified perpetrators and owners of the establishments involved. The NBI remains committed to purging the market of hazardous, unauthorized goods. Beyond the economic impact, counterfeit skincare products often contain unregulated ingredients that can cause severe allergic reactions, chemical burns, or long-term health issues. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag stated that “Our priority is not only to protect the intellectual property rights of legitimate brands but, more importantly, to safeguard Filipino consumers from the health risks associated with fake cosmetics. We urge the public to be vigilant and purchase only from authorized distributors to ensure their safety.”
