body: On April 1, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested RONNIE RIVERA y DELA CRUZ a.k.a. OGIE, a convicted felon for the killing of Ervick Limpin in Manila in 2002 and a fugitive who went on hiding for thirteen (13) years. In December 2016, five (5) Warrants of Arrest were issued by the RTC of Manila against Subject RIVERA and his group based on the criminal cases filed by the NBI on the death of PO2 Gabriel of the Presidential Security Group-Malacanang. PO2 Gabriel was shot to death on June 19, 2016 in Tondo, Manila when his (RIVERA’s) group assaulted indiscriminately all the residents of Coral St., Brgy.66 by shooting everyone in sight after a fistfight that erupted when Subject RIVERA got irritated by the loud voices of the victim’s group. A certain Crisanto Giovanni Lozano was also killed during the incident that were all captured thru the CCTV cameras. On March 19, 2019, the NBI-TFAID received information that Subject RIVERA was sighted in Harmony Homes, San Pedro, Laguna. Series of casing and surveillance on the alleged whereabouts of the Subject were conducted until on April 1, 2019, the Warrant of Arrest was served against him. He was caught off-guard and did not resist arrest. A caliber .45 Armscor pistol, five (5) pieces .45 ammunition, fourteen (14) pieces .38 ammunition, and one (1) magazine for .45 were recovered in his room. Also recovered were BIR Tin ID under the name Randy Reyes De Guzman and PhilHealth ID under the name Mike Dela Cruz Viola. Verification from PNP FEO revealed that the .45 Armscor pistol was registered to one Fontanos Florante Red of Bacoor, Cavite. Subject RIVERA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office, City of San Pedro for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), Batas Pambansa 881 (Omnibus Election Code of the Philippines), and RA 6085 (Illegal Use of Alias). On April 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MAGTOTO, YUGOSLAV y SALAS for Murder. Subject allegedly murdered his fellow Filipino worker in Korea while they were employed as factory workers thereat. Subject and victim, Angelo Camen Claveria worked as factory workers at Shinwa Meister Co. Ltd., Republic of Korea. While they were working together, Subject used to display affection to the victim but the latter had complaints and tried to move to another company. The victim’s rejection infuriated the Subject. By taking advantage of the victim’s submissive personality, Subject lured the victim out to the vicinity of DOIL Industrial Technologies Co., Ltd, a paint factory and allegedly murdered the victim in an unknown way. In April 2018, the skeletal remains of the victim was found in the septic tank of DOIL. The representatives from the Korean Consulate in Cebu City went to the DFA Consular Office in Iloilo to perform a DNA test on the victim’s mother, which eventually matched to that of the dead man in South Korea. On April 1, 2019, a Provisional Arrest Warrant was applied and granted by the RTC Branch 20, City of Manila. On the ensuing day, April 2, 2019, Subject Magtoto was located and arrested in the Municipality of Candaba, Pampanga thru the joint effort of the NBI-IOD, NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO), and PNP CIDG Police Provincial Office. The Provisional Arrest Warrant was returned to the issuing court looking forward that Subject remains under the custody of the NBI pending his Extradition to the Republic of Korea to face charges for Murder, Exploring Tombs, etc., Larceny and Specialized Credit Finance Business Act under Article 250, 161, 32, and 70 of the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea at the Suwon District Court. On April 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested EDGARDO LACSON y TORRES and ABEGAIL A. LACSON for Estafa. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against the Subjects. Complainant Baby Rohelnie Besario y Maningas alleged that Subject was her team leader in Hydrocarbon Management, Shell Company, Makati City and represented himself as authorized to solicit investments from public with promise that the investments will be invested in government bonds, particularly agrarian reform bonds and sugar trading and it will earn 9-15% interest monthly. Complainant decided to invest Php 500,000 with the promise that it will earn 10% interest for the first six months and 9% for the last six months. From November 2016 to December 2017, Complainant invested a total amount of Php 14.660 Million with unpaid amount of Php 8.160 Million. Complainant had already doubted the Subject and verification with the Security and Exchange Commission (SEC) revealed that the Subject is not authorized to solicit investments. When Subject arranged a meeting the complainant to collect additional investment, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subjects EDGARDO and ABEGAIL. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office. On Apri l 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested six (6) Chinese nationals for violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998). In coordination with the Manila Police District and the Security Management of the Malate Bayview Mansion, Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 141, Makati City were implemented by operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA. The operation resulted in the seizure of the items properly inventoried and duly listed in the respective inventory sheets and were duly signed and received by respondent’s representatives and his witnesses. All the items were taken under custody pending submission of the Returns of Search Warrants to the issuing court. The Chinese nationals were caught in flagrante delicto operating/using online and in possession of several counterfeit credit cards and debit cards. Arrested Subjects are now under temporary custody of NBI-NCR while necessary documents are being prepared for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice (DOJ). On April 3, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ROWENA DE LEON, MARVIN ALMENARIO y JUANITEZ, MANUEL ASISTIN y AVILLANO, and ARNALDO CASIÑO y TABIGUE for violation of RA 9287 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law). Chairman Abraham Kahlil B. Mitra, Chairman of Gamers and Amusement Board (GAB) requested the apprehension on suspected illegal bookies operation at 1600 Barrio Kapampangan Street, Sta. Ana, Manila. Surveillance operation confirmed the illegal bookies operation. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest for the above-mentioned violation. On April 3, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested EMMALYN CHAN y MERELOS for illegal bookies operation. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report received regarding the illegal operation of bookies or horse race bettings without license or permit from Games and Amusement Board (GAB). Surveillance operations were conducted confirming the report. With the information gathered, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who acted as bet collector. Certification from GAB stated that any permit/license authorizing the taking of horse racing bets is not issued to the Subject. Charges for violation of RA 9287 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law) were filed against the Subject before the City Prosecutor of Manila. On April 3, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) rescued seven (7) minors and arrested five (5) Subjects namely MARIA ESTER CABLING y CASTILLO, JOHN MARK NOFUENTE y BANABAN, JOHN KENNETH AREVALO y QUIAMBAO, DAVID HEINRICH CORONEL y VILLANUEVA, and SCHAN EVIAN SORIANO y RIVERA. A complaint was filed against MARIA ESTER CABLING a.k.a. ELLA who was allegedly recruiting, harboring, and exploiting women including minors for sexual purposes. With this, a rescue operation was conducted with the help of DSWD Putatan, Muntinlupa resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects and the rescue of 7 victims. Charges for violation of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) were filed against the Subjects before the DOJ Task Force on Violence Against Women and Children. On April 4, 2019 , operatives of NBI- Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested JOSEPHINE CORTEZ SEVERINO for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 2002) as amended by RA 10022. NBI received numerous complainants who became interested in applying for a job in Japan after hearing the news that the Japanese government opened its doors in hiring workers from the Philippines. Complainants averred that they came to know Subject and Unpack. Inc. through Facebook and they were told that Unpack, Inc. is a Japanese consultancy firm and training center for those who wish to be employed in Japan. Complainants were entertained by Subject Josephine who introduced herself as Unpack’s secretary. According to a complainant, Subject promised her that she could employ complainant as housekeeping crew in Japan with a monthly compensation of Php 100,000.00. No placement fee was collected but complainant was asked to pay Php 1,380.00 for mailing her documents and bills. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals in simultaneous operations conducted by the NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) in three (3) establishments in Solano, Nueva Vizcaya for selling chainsaw without necessary permit from the government. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as EMERO MENDOZA SAGUID, ISAGANI B. FORNODA, and RANDY RAMIREZ y BENICO. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from information l that several establishments in Solano, Nueva Viscaya are selling chainsaw without permit, namely: POWERSA TRADING (Powersaw), GANIE SAW CENTER (Ganie), and BLANCO AGRICULTURAL FARM MACHINERY TRADING (Blanco). Validation made by the NBI-BAYDO operatives revealed that the said establishments are offering chainsaw and cutting implements for sale to the general public. Distor stressed that a Certification issued by the PENR Sub-office of the DENR Office, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya revealed that no authority nor permit to sell and distribute the subject cutting machines were issued to Powersaw, Ganie, and Blanco. Under strict instruction from Distor, 3 composite teams from NBI-BAYDO conducted the simultaneous entrapment operations in the morning of May 6, 2021 on Powersaw, Ganie, and Blanco establishment that led to the immediate arrest of subjects after receiving the marked money. The operation also resulted in the seizure of two (2) local assemble chainsaws from Powersaw, two (2) big Stihl chainsaw from Ganie, and one (1) chainsaw from Blanco. The 3 subjects and another subject, ALEX P. NEGRILLO (at-large) who owns Powersaw Trading, were presented for inquest proceedings on the same day before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya for violation of R.A. 9175, otherwise known as the Chainsaw Act of 2002.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI THROWBACK CASE Ang ilang pugante ay tumatakbo. Ang ilan sa kanila ay nakakapagtago. And some of them reinvent themselves. MARY ANN MASLOG did them all. A key figure in the ₱24-million textbook scam that deprived Filipino schoolchildren of essential resources, Maslog evaded justice for years by staging her own death and assuming new identities. Under an alias, she rebuilt a life built on illusion and lies. But deception leaves fingerprints. Through coordinated investigation and forensic validation, the NBI uncovered the truth. A fingerprint match shattered the narrative she had carefully constructed. TheNBI – Fraud and Financial Crimes Division methodically built the evidentiary chain while maintaining strategic contact with her, ensuring the case was airtight before her eventual arrest in Quezon City. JUSTICE SERVED Before the Sandiganbayan, the Agent-on-Case delivered testimony that proved decisive — clearly tracing the link between her assumed identities and the misuse of public funds. The Chief of the NBI Dactyloscopy Division reinforced this with expert fingerprint analysis, scientifically confirming her true identity and dismantling years of evasion. The combined weight of testimonial, forensic, and documentary evidence established the continuity between Maslog’s assumed identities and her involvement in the misuse of public funds. The clarity, credibility, and technical precision of the testimonies strengthened the evidentiary chain and ultimately contributed to securing her conviction — sealing the fate of a deception that had endured for years. The Court convicted her. In a separate ruling, the Metropolitan Trial Court of Quezon City likewise convicted Maslog after she pleaded guilty to Falsification of Public Document and Violation of the Anti-Alias Law — formally acknowledging the identities she fabricated. Maaaring ang financial crimes na katulad nito ay hindi kasing-ingay ng ibang mga kaso which dominate the headlines, but their impact runs deep , lalo na kung ang public funds na para sana sa edukasyon ay sinasalbahe at kino- kompromiso. Ang throwback case na ito ay isang paalaala na hindi nabubura ng panahon ang pananagutan. False identities do not override forensic truth. And no alias and fabricated death can permanently bury justice and outrun the law. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 20, 2024 In compliance with NBI Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO’s directive to suppress criminality, NBI-CEMRO operatives in coordination and collaboration with the Koronadal City Police Station and CIDG Provincial Field Unit – South Cotabato, served the Warrant of Arrest against WALTER ZULLA ADVINCULA a.k.a BURADOR on November 19, 2024 in San Roque, Koronadal City, South Cotabato. NBI CEMRO agents acted on the complaints of the parents of the minor victims, ages 10 and 15 year old, when they discovered series of sexual abuses perpetrated by the accused against the minors. It was learned that Subject ADVINCULA began molesting the children since September 2024. ADVINCULA, accused of sexually abusing two minors aged 10 and aged 15, has been charged with Statutory Rape under Par. (1) (D), Art. 266-A of the Revised Penal Code as amended by R.A. 8353, Sexual Assault (2 counts) in relation to Section 5 (B) of R.A. No. 7610, Acts of Lasciviousness (3 counts) under Art. 336 of the RPC in relation to Section 5 (B) of R.A. 7610 and Lascivious Conduct (4 counts) under Section 5 (B) of R.A. 7610. Immediately after the issuance of the Warrant of Arrest by the RTC Branch 62, the manhunt to arrest the subject began that resulted to the immediate apprehension of Subject in his hideout. Republic Act 7610 mandates heavy penalties for crimes against children, including rape and sexual abuse. Subject ADVINCULA faces multiple charges with severe consequences under this law. Subject ADVINCULA is detained at NBI CEMRO located in Koronadal City, South Cotabato pending the return of the warrant of arrest and the issuance of the commitment order by the Honorable Court to the appropriate detention facility. Director Santiago said that the NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to help victims in obtaining justice, especially with respect to crimes committed against minor children and urged the public to support the legal process. The victims and their families are receiving the necessary support from government agencies and protection as the hearing of the case continues.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of the prime suspect in the illegal SIM replacement to gain access to mobile banking and perform money transfer illegally. In a Post-Operation Report, the NBI-Investigation Service (NBI-InvS) said its operatives have arrested Subject FRANCO YAP DE LARA and his companion, RAMIL MAPALAD PASCUAL while securing a car loan in Toyota, Calamba Laguna for one (1) Fortuner 2015 model. Also found in the possession of Subject De Lara were ATM cards that do not belong to him, an offense which falls within the provisions of the Security Device Act. Both Subjects were then brought to the NBI headquarters. Subjects De Lara and Pascual were thereafter charged before the Office of the Special Prosecutor of the Department of Justice for Violation of RA 8484 (Access Device Act), Attempted Estafa through Falsification of Documents, and Violation of Sec. 4 (3) Computer Related Identify Theft. The NBI-InvS said the case stemmed from a request filed by Globe Telecoms, Inc. seeking an investigation for a complaint of illegal SIM replacement from a certain IAN CABALLERO who claimed to Globe Telecoms, Inc. that his number lost signal and after verification, it was discovered that he was victimized by an impostor and later learned that his mobile banking was accessed. The NIBI-InvS also stated that three (3) employees of Toyota Motors, namely: Marlon Uy, Christian Jan Paredes and one Kristine Hernaez came forward and ventilated the same complaint. Prompt coordination with Globe Telecoms, Inc. and from the evidence adduced, the impostor was identified as Subject FRANCO DE LARA y YAP who was recognized by his former officemates through CCTV footages provided by Globe Telecoms. Likewise, several identification cards were tampered to make it appear that they belong to Subject De Lara. On Saturday afternoon, July 25, 2015, after being informed by one of victims, Kristine Hernaez, that Subject De Lara was in Toyota, Calamba Laguna to secure a car loan for a certain Raymund San Jose Tia, NBI-InvS operatives proceeded and positioned in the area. As soon as Subjects submitted the documents and paid the downpayment, he and his companion were arrested.

body: On April 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested alias “OPAO” and certain MORRES for selling and using shabu. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Brgy. Kauswagan, Cagayan de Oro City which stemmed from an information that a certain “OPAO” is selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro City. With this, the buy-bust operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects who were also caught in the act of using shabu. The Cagayan de Oro Prosecutor’s Office charged the Subjects of violating RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested alias RONNIE “DONGDONG” M. TABAMO for selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro City. Subject was arrested in buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information received that a certain “HONEY” is selling shabu. On the aforementioned date, a certain RONNIE “DONGDONG” M. TABAMO, former Police Officer, was apprehended in a buy-bust operation at Brgy. 40, Cagayan de Oro City. HONEY sent DONGDONG to transact with the poseur-buyer. The Cagayan de Oro Prosecutor’s Office charged DONGDONG for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ALGREAN REYES y FERNANDEZ for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol and other prime commodities, taking advantage of Covid-19 crisis. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted in San Carlos City, Pangasinan. Recovered from the Subject were boodle money and four (4) bottles of 500ml Green Cross Isopropyl Alcohol worth Php560.00 and 500ml Doctor J Isopropyl Alcohol worth Php340.00 and sales notebook. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before San Carlos City Prosecutors Office for violation of RA 7581 as amended by RA 10623 (Price Act). On May 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested PSSgt MARK PALMA and RODNIE TAMAYO alias AFUANG for selling illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation by joint operation of NBI-SEMRO XI, PDEA RO XI (RSET) and PDEA RO XI (SIU) at Jasa 1 Km 13, Panacan, Davao City. The operation also resulted to the confiscation of the following: a) two (2) pcs large transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu b) three (3) pcs medium transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu c) one (1) pc small transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu d) one (1) pc small elongated transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing a combined of more or less 15 grams with an estimated street value of Php 102,000.00 and other drug paraphernalia. Cases of violation of RA 9165 are being prepared for filing in Court against the Subjects. On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested SHANON APRIL MEJIA ALEGRE and ESSELINE RAISA SY ONG for illegal selling of Covid-19 test kits. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information received that there are individuals selling test kits online to the public through Facebook and that orders are privately messaged by the buyers to the sellers and payments are made through cash on delivery (COD) or online banking. Operatives were able to identify the online seller of test kits when it posted pictures for COD. Acting on the information, an entrapment operation was conducted wherein poseur-buyers ordered 200 boxes of test kits for Php2,400,000.00 at Php 12,000 per box. Seller even gave a discounted price of Php2,360,000.00 for 200 boxes. The meet up was set at PDP Village, Concha Cruz, BF Homes, Paranaque. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects SHANON and ESSELINE and the seizure of 200 boxes of test kits. Certification issued by the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) states that the online sellers do not have License-to-Operate or Special Certification for selling or distribution of antibody test kit or any other Covid-19 test kit. Criminal charges will be filed against the Subjects before the Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 07, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (OTCD), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested Spouses CHRISTOPHER CAPITULO and MARIA ELENA CAPITULO in Dagat-Dagatan, Caloocan City. The case originated from the complaint of a Filipino businessman who reported to the NBI-OTCD, citing years of threats from an individual identifying himself as “Ka Ferdie,” allegedly affiliated with the NPA. Since 2018, the suspect had extorted Complainant and his family, demanding annual payments for their safety. Threats were made through a cellphone number 0910-525-3340, with funds exceeding P2.6 million deposited into a BDO account. After investigation and verification, NBI traced the extortion number to individuals linked to Christopher and Maria Elena Capitulo. On July 2, 2025, following another deposit by Complainant under NBI supervision, an entrapment operation was conducted. The bank account holder, upon questioning, admitted her account was used to receive money for her neighbor, Chris Capitulo, in exchange for a cut per transaction. She cooperated with NBI-OTCD, and using marked bills, delivered the cash to the Capitulo couple as part of a controlled follow-up operation. Once Chris received the money, NBI operatives arrested both suspects. Chris Capitulo admitted his role in the extortion and surrendered his cellphone containing the SIM used to send threats. An inventory of items seized was conducted in the presence of barangay officials. The suspects were brought to the NBI-OTCD for booking and undergone inquest proceedings before the Caloocan City Prosecutor’s Office for multiple charges: Robbery (Extortion) under the Revised Penal Code, Violation of Section 11(d) of RA 11934 (SIM Registration Act), Violation of Section 4 of RA 10168 (Financing of Terrorism), and Money Laundering under RA 9160, as amended. Subjects were temporarily detained at the NBI Detention Facility in Muntinlupa. The NBI emphasizes its continued commitment to dismantle criminal networks involved in extortion, financial fraud, money laundering and terrorism financing.

body: A revenue officer who demanded money from a business firm in consideration for having a request for an installment basis on his compromise settlement for a tax liability, was arrested during an entrapment in Caloocan City last week. The subject is identified as THELMA BINUYA, Revenue Officer I, 53, of Calumpit, Bulacan, assigned at the BIR Revenue Region No. 5, Revenue District Office No. 27, Caloocan City. On November 9, 2012, the NBI received a complaint from Mr. Joselito B. Ramos, President/General Manager of Sinusoidal Electrical Support, Inc. (SES) against a certain revenue officer for extortion. It was bared that SES, Inc. received a preliminary collection letter from BIR-RDO Albino M. Galanza, about the company’s tax liability for 2006 amounting to P2,408,703.91. The company’s External Auditor Mr. Gerardo Espino talked to RDO Albino M. Galanza and asked RDO Galanza if they can avail of the compromise settlement pursuant to Revenue Regulation 30-2002 wherein the Company will only be required to pay the 40% of the assessed tax liability. Mr. Espino also informed him that they would like to make the payment in installment for the period of 18 months. RDO Galanza instructed Mr. Espino to talk with Ms. Thelma Binuya, Revenue Officer I, since the case has been forwarded to the Collection Department. When Mr. Espino talked to Ms. Binuya, she reassured Mr. Espino that their request will be approved. She also made a computation on the 40% that the company has to pay in the amount of PHP 541,186.60. However, in consideration of her help to have the request approved, Ms. Binuya demanded an additional amount of Php 100,000.00; On November 9, 2012, SES, Inc. received a Final Notice Before Seizure which prompted the company to seek NBI investigative assistance. Two days after, Espino, went to talk to Binuya who asked for the money but the former requested that the amount be reduced to P80,000 to which Binuya agreed. They agreed to meet in the afternoon of November 15 at chicken house near the BIR office. However, the meeting was cancelled at the last minute and was reset the following day in a certain restaurant also near the BIR office. At 1:00 PM of November 16, 2012, Espino and Ramos, accompanied by NBI agents went to the place and strategically positioned themselves. After some time, Binuya changed the plan anew, and instead instructed Espino, to meet her at the BIR office. At 3:00 PM, Ramos met Binuya and handed the marked money to her. Moments later, Espino signalled the operatives nearby who rushed to Binuya. After introducing themselves, NBI agents arrested her. On November 17, she was brought before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Caloocan City for inquest. Charges for Robbery (Extortion) and violation of Section 3 (b) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) were filed against the suspect.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said Agents of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) have arrested 2 subjects at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Pasay City for using documents with falsified information. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD a.k.a. SANDRA LIPOLES and GRETCHEN ABLAN. OIC Director Distor said that Subject Mukamad was about to depart on May 3, 2021 for Saudi Arabia via Saudi Airlines. The subject was intercepted at the Immigration and questioned to verify her age and previous travels. According to Subject Mukamad, she is 30 years old, having been born on May 15, 1990. Subject was not allowed to depart due to her appearance, which is obviously too young for a 30 years old. The subject was then turned-over to NBI-IAID for further questioning and validation. Subject Mukamad told the NBI-IAID that she has already been to Saudi Arabia in 2017 using her current passport. However, the subject stated in the identification card she voluntarily filled out that her correct date of birth is May 5, 2000 & her true name ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD. The subject also revealed that she secured her passport from Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) in Cotabatao City. Subject Mukamad was then placed under arrest and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of Section 19 (b)(2) (Uses or attempts to use any passport which was secured in any way by reason of any false statements) of R.A. 8239 otherwise known as the Philippine Passport Act of 1996. Subject GRETCHEN ABLAN, on the other hand, was about to depart on May 4, 2021 as a tourist for Dubai, UAE, when she was referred for secondary inspection after being discovered that she was previously off-loaded on April 22, 2021 for misrepresentation. During inspection, subject claimed she was visiting her husband, JOEY DAMASCO MANALIGOD and showed copies of passport bio-page and UAE Visa sticker of MANALIGOD. With discrepancies and alteration in documents different as reflected in the Central Query Support System of the Bureau of Immigration, subject ABLAN admitted both verbally and in writing that she was not married and does not actually know MANALIGOD. She stated that all her documents for her May 4 flight were sent to her on May 3, 2021 by her recruiter through another person in Baclaran, Paranaque City. When confronted by the NBI regarding the COVID-19 Test Report issued by Dagupan Doctors Villaflor Memorial Hospital under her name, she said she had not undergone any COVID-19 test. Upon verification with said hospital on the COVID-19 of subject, the hospital declared that subject ABLAN did not appear in their list as one of their patients. Subject ABLAN was placed under arrest for violation of Art. 172 in relation to Art. 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Use of Falsified Documents. Subjects ARBAYA LINTUKAN MUKAMAD and GRETCHEN ABLAN were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City.

body: An impostor claiming to be a Professional Regulations Commission (PRC) employee and asked money from a Nursing examinee to ensure a passing grade in the 2011 licensure board examination was arrested in an entrapment by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation in Manila the other day. The subject is identified as FRANKLIN CINCO TANJUTCO, 54, and a resident of 45 A. Lower Jasmin, Payatas, Quezon City. In 2009, complainant Rosita F. Tambalo, met suspect Tanjuco in Pangasinan who introduced himself as a PRC employee. Tambalo said that she has a niece, who is a nursing graduate. Tanjutco demanded P80,000 from complainant so that her niece would pass the December 2009 Nursing Licensure Examination (NLE). Complainant gave him the initial amount of P40,000, the balance to be paid in installment. When the result of the nursing board exam was released in March 2010, her niece was not included in the list of board passers. Tanjutco told her niece to take the next NLE and would surely pass. She took the NLE again in July 2010 but failed anew. Tanjutco told the complainant that the name of her niece is in the master list of the board passers. He asked her to pay the balance so that he would give her the said master list. On March 22, 2011, complainant deposited P25,000 at PNB Dagupan Branch, Pangasinan to the account of suspect’s wife, and another P20,000 deposit days later. However, suspect did not give her the alleged master list. On July 4, 2012, Tanjutco asked for P6,000 so that her niece would be included in the list of passers when the result of 2011 NLE would be released in September 2012. They were to meet in the afternoon of July 17, 2012 at a fast food chain in Sta. Cruz, Manila. This prompted Tambalo to seek NBI assistance. An entrapment was planned. In the afternoon of July 17, 2012, at a fast food parlor, NBI agents accompanied the complainant and positioned themselves strategically at the place. Moments after, Tanjutco received the marked money from Tambalo, NBI agents approached and arrested him. Tanjutco was detained at the NBI. Charges for violation of Art. 315, No. 2(a) (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code are readied against the suspect before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | MILLIONS WORTH OF SHABU INTERCEPTED; ONE ARRESTED In two separate operations, joint operatives seized significant quantities of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride or commonly known as shabu, and arrested an individual involved in its illegal transport and distribution. On April 3, 2026, an operation conducted by the composite elements of the NAIA-Inter-Agency Interdiction Task Group, which includes the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), at NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City led to the arrest of an individual who arrived from Kuala Lumpur via Malaysian Airlines. Authorities recovered one (1) backpack containing approximately 3,120 grams of white crystalline substance, which tested positive for Shabu, with an estimated value of Php 21,216,000.00. The arrested Subject was presented for inquest proceedings on April 4, 2026 before the Department of Justice in Manila for violation of R.A. No. 9165 and is currently under detention pending further proceedings. Subsequently, on April 14, 2026, a separate operation resulted in the interception of one (1) inbound parcel declared as Auto Gear Bearings, which was found to contain approximately 1,234 grams of shabu with an estimated value of Php 8,391,200.00. The parcel came from Mbuya Uganda and was consigned to a recipient in Dasmariñas, Cavite. All the seized items were inventoried in the presence of the required witnesses and submitted to the PDEA Laboratory Service in Quezon City for examination, custody, and proper disposition. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings on April 4, 2026 before the Department of Justice in Manila for violation of the pertinent provisions of law and is currently under detention pending further legal proceedings. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag said that the NBI continues to strengthen its intelligence and enforcement efforts, in close coordination with partner agencies, to dismantle drug networks and hold those responsible fully accountable under the law. He also calls on the public to remain vigilant and to support the collective fight against illegal drugs for the safety and well-being of the communities.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual engaged in the selling Agarwood which is a forest product categorized as an endangered species. body: In the continuing probe of the June 28, 2012 seizure of 55 container vans containing illegal lumber in Manila, a team of NBI agents later dispatched successfully traced the loading area in Davao City leading to the confiscation of eighteen (18) more twenty-footer vans suspected to contain illegal timber today. The pinpointed places are in Pasian, Monkayo and Campostela Valley where the truckers load the illegally cut timbers and hauled these products to Davao City Port. An undetermined quantity of illegal timber, Red Lawa-an, were discovered in the same rebel-infested area where the loading of lumber was done roughly a week before. Coordination with the DENR Office was immediately made. Upon arrival of the DENR team, the illegally sourced forest products were properly turned over to the DENR team leader. Another NBI group collated all pertinent documents from the Community Environment & Natural Resources Office (CENRO), Provincial Environment & Natural Resources Office (PENRO) and the Department of Environment & Natural Resources (DENR) Regional Office (Region XI). In the early morning of July 6, 2012, the NBI received a written request from the management of Lorenzo Container Yard in Davao City that their company is willing to cooperate into the on-going probe by the NBI. Consequently, eighteen (18) 20-footer vans suspected containing illegal timber were voluntarily opened in the presence of the NBI, representatives from the DENR Region XI, Task force Against Illegal Logging and media. The aggregate value of all the 73 container vans is estimated to be over P20 million, excluding those discovered in Monkayo, Campostela Valley.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI-Organized Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested two (2) female pimps in Marilao, Bulacan for sexual trafficking activities. The case stemmed from a case referral by Destiny Rescue Philippines, Inc. (DESTINY) on the case of two female pimps who are offering female victims, including minors, sexual services for a fee ranging from Php 3,000.00 -5,000.00. NBI-OTCD agents, together with the staff from DESTINY, conducted a surveillance and met the Subjects who brought two (2) girls and offered their sexual services in the amount of Php3,000.00 for every girl. The undercover team then asked for postponement as to not consummate the crime. Instead, the team mentioned that they would have a party at a private resort on June 04, 2025. The Subjects offered to bring more girls. On June 04, 2025, NBI-OTCD and DESTINY hatched an entrapment operation, Subjects met with the undercover team at the agreed location at Seven Villa, Marilao, Bulacan. Subjects brought along eleven (11) other victims. Subjects reiterated their transaction to the poseur client that each girl costs Php3,000.00 that would include sexual services. Poseur client handed the marked money amounting to Php33,000.00 to one of the Subjects. Thus, the arrests of the Subjects for utilizing and offering the victims for sexual purposes and exploitation i fechange for sum of money. Eleven (11) trafficked victims were rescued, four (4) of whom are minors. Investigation revealed that two victims are siblings, while one of the victims is the daughter of one of the Subjects. Also, both Subjects live in the same household. Rescued victims were turned over to MSWDO. body: Three cyber technology specialists engaged in unauthorized use of facilities belonging to a legitimate telephone company was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents in Makati City recently. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: DANDIN CALVEZ VARONA, IT Specialist of East West Placement Center, Inc., and a resident of No. 11 Leonardo St., Tramo Lane, Pasay City; ADRIAN JAY CARDENAS GARCIA, IT Technical Support of East West Placement Center Inc., and a resident of No. 7715 Coronado St., Guadalupe Viejo, Makati City; and JEFFERSON MADRID BOLIVAR, Computer Technician, of East West Placement Center Inc., and a resident of No. 5 Calleja St., Signal Village, Taguig City. At-large is Rizaline O. Dormiendo, President and CEO of East West Placement Center Inc. Investigation by the Anti-Fraud and Action Division (AFAD) headed by Atty. Cesar A. Bacani disclosed that on June 17, 2013, the Smart Communications, Inc. through its counsel sought NBI investigative assistance about the illegal international simple resale (ISR) activities, known as “Toll By Pass” against the suspects. ISR is a fraud committed against network operators (Smart included) by routing and completing international long distance calls, without proper authority to local subscribers using cables, antenna, air wave or frequency, broadband/internet protocol (IP) services, telephone switching equipment and SIM cards. With this illegal activity, the ISR operator is able to evade payment of IGF fees and taxes due the Philippine government by routing the international calls directly to an unauthorized device and thereby gaining undue advantage over legitimate networks and operators because they can charge lower fees. In the course of the investigation, Smart’s representatives Engrs. Marlouie Ramos and Kris Anne Joy Domingo of Smart’s Anti-Fraud’s Engineers and Integrated Revenue Management’s Voice Fraud Management Team (VFMT) disclosed the illicit activities of suspects. A certification of the Compliance, Fraud and Investigation Services, Department of Smart Communications shows that their offices has incurred losses in the amount of P932,036.71 due to IRS committed by suspects. A series of test calls was conducted by Smart representative and was confirmed that ISR activity is being committed at the suspects’ office, East West Placement Center Inc. located at No. 1059 Metropolitan Avenue, Rizz Building, San Antonio Village, Makati City. Surveillance was conducted and was further confirmed the illegal activities of the suspects at the said place. On July 1, 2013, a search warrant was applied for and issued by the Regional Trial Court, Malabon City against the premises of suspects in Makati City. On July 2, 2013, after proper coordination with the local police, operatives of the NBI-AFAD, together with lawyers and representatives of Smart Communication Inc. served the search warrant in the presence of John Patrick Libongco, Legal Associate of East West Placement Center, Inc. Consequently, Varona, Garcia and Bolivar were caught inside the server room located at the 3rd floor office of their office where the illegal international simple resale (ISR) activities is being committed. Two test calls were again conducted by Domingo as was further confirmed that ISR is being committed using the SIM cards found at the said premises. A certification from Bala shows that Smart Communications Inc. has incurred losses during the service of the said search warrant. Consequently, articles subject of the offense were seized such as computer, SIM boxes, SIM cards, switching equipment and among others. Suspects were arrested and brought to the NBI. However, Dormiendo was not present during the implementation of the said warrant. Charges for violation of Art. 308 of the Revised Penal Code (Theft) were filed against the suspects before the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI NABS SUSPECT IN BRUTAL ABUSE OF 7-YEAR-OLD Pasay City, Philippines- The National Bureau of Investigation – Homicide Division (NBI-HD) has apprehended an individual identified as alias “AMBO” for the physical and psychological abuse of a seven-year-old child. The case stemmed from reports of relatives and was backed by witness accounts and communications showing a pattern of harm and threats inflicted on the minor while under the suspect’s custody. Acting on validated information, NBI-HD operatives tracked the suspect to Dasmariñas City, Cavite. On April 21, 2026, authorities moved in and successfully arrested the suspect, who is now under NBI custody. The subject has undergone inquest proceedings, which have already been completed, paving the way for the immediate filing of charges. Evidence gathered establishes probable cause for violation of Republic Act No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act), covering acts of child abuse, cruelty, and exploitation. The NBI underscores its zero tolerance for crimes against children and assures the public that offenders will be pursued relentlessly and held fully accountable under the law. The minor victim is now under the care of proper authorities, with coordination ongoing with the Department of Social Welfare and Development to ensure necessary medical and psychological intervention. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1499467481577139/?s=single_unit

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 09, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS SHAM PRIEST IN ONLINE DONATION SCAM PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation – Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) has apprehended a Subject for allegedly posing as a parish priest in an online scheme designed to solicit fraudulent donations from unsuspecting victims. The investigation was launched following a complaint from a member of the clergy, whose name and photograph were used to deceive acquaintances into sending funds. In response, NBI-NADO agents organized a strategic entrapment operation. The Subject was arrested immediately after claiming the illicitly obtained money through a mobile wallet account linked to the scam. During the operation, NBI agents recovered the marked money and a mobile device believed to have been utilized in the commission of the fraud. The Subject is currently facing charges for Identity Theft under the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 and Estafa under the Revised Penal Code. “We will not allow criminals to exploit the trust and goodwill of the public through fake online identities. The NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to pursuing cyber fraudsters and protecting our communities,” stated Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno, NBI Acting Director. The NBI urges the public to exercise heightened caution by verifying all online requests for financial assistance and reporting suspicious social media accounts or activities to the Bureau immediately. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) in an entrapment operation in Ilagan City for Human Trafficking. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as NINA CARLOTA BAQUIRAN- MANSIBANG. OIC Distor said that the operation stemmed from an intelligence report that Subject Nina is engaged in the illicit sex trade, offering young women for sexual services in exchange for a fee. Acting on the said information, NBI-ISDO operatives conducted a surveillance operation against Subject Nina and were able to confirm the information. Two (2) members of the NBI-ISDO acted as poseur-customers and communicated with the subject thru her cellphone. The poseur-clients were able to request two (2) young ladies from the subject for sexual services. As part of the agreement the poseur-client will pay the subject Php 2,000.00 each for the two (2) women and another Php 800.00 each for her own pocket money. Thus, on August 11, 2021, NBI-ISDO operatives together with the poseur-client proceeded to Barangay Alibagu, Ilagan City and strategically positioned themselves in the vicinity. A few minutes later, Subject Nina arrived together with the 2 young ladies. One of the poseur-clients brought the ladies into their car and went back to Subject Nina to hand-over the entrapment money. As soon as the marked money was received by the subject, the rest of the operatives immediately approached the subject and placed her under arrest. The 2 young ladies rescued were turned-over to the Provincial Social Welfare and Development of Isabela. Subject Nina was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Ilagan City, Isabela for violation of R.A. 9208 as amended by R.A. 10364, otherwise known as “The Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act”.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested four (4) Korean nationals, evening of February 5, 2018 in Manila. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as YOUNG TAE YOUN , BYUNG WOOK AHN , KIM MIN DUNG , and PARK HYUN . The case stemmed from the a complainant who sought the assistance of NBI for alleged carnapping. Complainant alleged that she normally allows PARK HYUN, a tour guide, to use her Ford EcoSports whenever they have Korean guests. Sometime last week, complainant asked PARK HYUN to get her other car, Kia Picanto and bring it to her place in Makati. However, PARK HYUN failed to do so and said that he will borrow the car until February 5 since he will use it in transferring to another condo unit. Moreover, complainant’s partner received a call from PARK HYUN asking for help as he was caught by persons whom he owed money and that her cars were taken and were demanding for Php 1 Million plus Php 360,000 interest before the complainant could get her cars back. Complainant was instructed to bring the money at Casino Filipino – Manila Bay. Under strict orders from Director Gierran, operatives of NBI-AOTCD planned and conducted the entrapment operation at the place where the complainant was instructed to deliver the money. PARK HYUN arrived first and talked to the complainant. Afterwards, YOUNG TAE YOUN and BYUNG WOOK AHN came in. After an hour, complainant’s Ford EcoSports driven by KIM MIN DUNG arrived followed by the Kia Picanto. Subjects were arrested after YOUNG TAE YOUN took the marked money. Investigation revealed that PARK HYUN is in cahoots with the other Subjects. Subjects were brought at the NBI for the proper booking procedures and were charged on inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violation of RA 10883 (Carnapping).

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested four (4) Korean nationals, evening of February 5, 2018 in Manila. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as YOUNG TAE YOUN , BYUNG WOOK AHN , KIM MIN DUNG , and PARK HYUN . The case stemmed from the a complainant who sought the assistance of NBI for alleged carnapping. Complainant alleged that she normally allows PARK HYUN, a tour guide, to use her Ford EcoSports whenever they have Korean guests. Sometime last week, complainant asked PARK HYUN to get her other car, Kia Picanto and bring it to her place in Makati. However, PARK HYUN failed to do so and said that he will borrow the car until February 5 since he will use it in transferring to another condo unit. Moreover, complainant’s partner received a call from PARK HYUN asking for help as he was caught by persons whom he owed money and that her cars were taken and were demanding for Php 1 Million plus Php 360,000 interest before the complainant could get her cars back. Complainant was instructed to bring the money at Casino Filipino – Manila Bay. Under strict orders from Director Gierran, operatives of NBI-AOTCD planned and conducted the entrapment operation at the place where the complainant was instructed to deliver the money. PARK HYUN arrived first and talked to the complainant. Afterwards, YOUNG TAE YOUN and BYUNG WOOK AHN came in. After an hour, complainant’s Ford EcoSports driven by KIM MIN DUNG arrived followed by the Kia Picanto. Subjects were arrested after YOUNG TAE YOUN took the marked money. Investigation revealed that PARK HYUN is in cahoots with the other Subjects. Subjects were brought at the NBI for the proper booking procedures and were charged on inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violation of RA 10883 (Carnapping).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested two Chinese nationals, evening of January 20, 2018 in Pasay City. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN and CHENWIN BIN . The case stemmed from a report that Subjects might be involved in an illegal activity. According to the report received by the NBI-AOTCD, CYX Manpower Services (CYX) with office address at Diplomat Condominium, Russel Avenue, Roxas Blvd., Pasay City, was in need of bodyguards. The hired bodyguards were then introduced to foreigners as their “bosses”. They were informed that the persons they will secure was in a room and they must not be allowed to escape because they owe millions to their would-be bosses. Allegedly, instead of being interviewed, they were asked to demonstrate how to use handcuffs. In the evening of January 18, 2018, NBI-AOTCD was informed that a handcuffed couple from Scape Building located at Diosdado Macapagal, Pasay City was brought to a house at Moonwalk, Paranaque City. With this, NBI-AOTCD operatives conducted a rescue operation on January 19, 2018 which resulted in the rescue of AI XIAO FENG and XIAO QZAO LING, both Chinese nationals. Also present during the operation were the four (4) bodyguards who later on gave their sworn statements similar to the initial report received by the NBI-AOTCD. Rescued victims, on the other hand, narrated that Subject SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN accused them of the lost RMB 700,000 (equivalent to Php 5.5 Million) but they denied any knowledge thereto. A follow-up operation was then conducted at Shell Residence located at Pasay City resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were positively identified by the victims as those who handcuffed and took them away. Subjects were brought to NBI-AOTCD for proper booking procedures. On January 20, 2018, Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Article 267 (Serious Illegal Detention) of the Revised Penal Code. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Detention Jail.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today denied in the strongest possible terms reports that the Agency is involved in the alleged harassment and threat on the life of Charlie “Atong” Ang. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said that the NBI is a professional organization that adheres to high moral and ethical standards and its Officials and Agents will not be involved in highly unethical and illegal activities as alleged by Ang. Gierran stressed that the alleged threat that Charlie “Atong” Ang said in an interview is baseless and without merit and is just a product of his own wild imaginations. Gierran said the baseless and unfounded allegations of Charlie ”Atong” Ang may have something to do with the series of operations conducted by the NBI in Isabela Province. On March 29, 2017, the NBI received a letter from the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) seeking the assistance of the NBI in stopping illegal gambling and such other forms of illegal numbers game, including Jai Alai and such other forms of illegal gambling or numbers game using or based on Jail Alai in the Province of Isabela. The letter also stated that the PCSO has gathered information and received reports that illegal gambling, including Jai Alai and such illegal numbers games using or based on Jai Alai results, are being openly conducted and proliferates in the Province of Isabela. The PCSO emphasized that under the law, PCSO is the only authorized agency to hold and conduct lotteries and similar games in the country and Small Town Lottery (STL) is the only legal and authorized numbers game nationwide. Promptly acting on the request, the NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) conducted an operation on April 19, 2017 in Ilagan, Province of Isabela resulting in the arrest of forty (40) individuals and gambling paraphernalia of Meredian Gaming Corporation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 13, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS AN INDIVIDUAL FOR ILLEGALLY ACCESSING AND DISTRIBUTING MINOR’S EXPLICIT VIDEO The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), arrested an individual in the city of Manila for illegally accessing and distributing an explicit video of a minor from a woman’s mobile phone, in violation of anti-online child exploitation and cybercrime laws. On 20 February 2026, a complaint was formally filed for violations of R.A. No. 11930, otherwise known as the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM), and Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. Complainant alleged that the Subject illegally accessed child sexual abuse or exploitation material in her phone’s gallery and distributed the same to his own Facebook Account and to his friend. During a birthday party on 07 February 2026, Subject borrowed the Complainant’s mobile phone under the pretense of taking photographs. Instead, he accessed a restricted folder labeled “Hidden Photos and Videos” and retrieved an explicit video of the Complainant recorded when she was a minor. The Subject then transmitted the said video to himself and another individual through Facebook Messenger. Thereafter, he further distributed the material to a group chat, causing the video to circulate within the Complainant’s barangay and school community. Investigation and cyber-surveillance established that the Subject operated his Facebook account using a mobile device at his residence located at Sikat Street, San Miguel, Manila. Based on the evidence gathered, CCD operatives applied for and secured a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD). The warrant was subsequently implemented at the Subject’s residence. Examination of seized devices revealed digital evidence confirming unauthorized access to the Complainant’s phone and the subsequent distribution of the illicit material. The Subject was arrested in flagrante delicto for Illegal Access under Section 4(a)(1) of Republic Act No. 10175. He was informed of his constitutional rights at the time of arrest. All seized items were properly inventoried, and the Subject underwent standard post-arrest procedures, including medical examination, booking, and documentation. The Subject is currently undergoing post-operation processing and will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag said that the NBI remains firm in its commitment to uphold the law and protect individuals, especially minors, from all forms of online exploitation. “We recognize that our work is strengthened through continued public trust and vigilance. We encourage everyone to report similar incidents so that appropriate action can be taken without delay,” he added. #NBIServes

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested a call center agent who misrepresented herself as a Fil-Norwegian model in the social network Facebook to lure an Australian national into an on-line relationship for financial reasons in Cavite last week. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: LOUELLA DE GUZMAN TAN , 29, of B4 Lot 17 Bgy. St. Peter, Dasmariñas, Cavite. Investigation report of the Technical Investigation Division – Intelligence Services under Deputy Director Ruel M. Lasala, disclosed that Louella Tan befriended Hans Mathieu Patrick de Kraker, an Australian national thru the Facebook account in the name “Jen Matheson” using the photos of Janka Cederstam, a Filipino-Norwegian model. She enticed him into having a supposed on-line relationship and succeeded in making him send money to the Philippines via Western Union received by a certain Louella Tan, supposedly “Jen Matheson’s” representative. However, Hans discovered the scam through a friend who recognized the pictures to be that of the complainant, Janka. On March 21, 2012, Hans contacted Janka during which she told him that she does not know Hans and that she does not have a Facebook account in the name Jen Matheson, nor authorized anyone to use her name and photographs. Consequently, Janka searched for the name Jen Martheson and saw dozens of her pictures saved in the Photos folder including that of her family. Thus, an NBI investigative assistance was sought. Tan using the name “Matheson” constantly asked Hans to send more money supposedly for her daily subsistence claiming her parents have died in accidents and other personal misfortunes. Despite Tan’s abuses, Hans played along and on April 19, 2012, sent money again. A sting operation was set up. At 3:30 pm, Tan arrived and claimed the money. NBI operatives who were posted nearby immediately arrested Tan and brought to the NBI for questioning. Charges for violation of RA 8972 Section 33a (Electronic Commerce Act of the Philippines), Art. 315 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa), Commonwealth Act 142 as amended by RA 6085 (Anti-Alias L aw) and Art. 178 of the RPC (Using Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name) were filed against the suspect before the Imus, Cavite Prosecutor’s Office.

body: Fourteen (14) Chinese undocumented nationals found working for a mining company allegedly involved in illegal black sand mining in Aparri, Cagayan were arrested following a raid by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) the other day. The subjects are identified as: 1) HE, JING TAO, male, 53, of Liao Hing, China, engineer; 2) SUN, JING, female, 48, of Heilong Jiang, China; 3) GUO, QUIANG, male, 31, of Shan Xi, China, interpreter; 4) YANG, XUEZHI, male, 25, of Hebei, China; 5) DENG, TAO, male, 24, of Jianxi, China 6) FENG, GUO JUN, male, 48, of Zejiang, China, engineer; 7) XU, JINFA, male, 48, of Jiang Xi, China, mechanic; 8) HE, JING TAO, male, 53, engineer; 9) FENG, DAO GUANG, male, 54, of Guang Xi, China, engineer; 10) LU, QING BO, male, 28, of Guang Xi, China; 11) LEI, DE HUI, male, 40, of Hunan, China, mechanic; 12) QING, HE PING, male, 49, of Shan Xi, China, engineer; 13) YANG, DONG, male, 41, of Lian Ning, China, mechanic; and 14) WANG, YAN HAI, male, 43, of Ganzu, China. All with given address at #25 McKinley, Ave., South Forbes, Makati. The NBI also took custody of a 16-year-old Filipino boy who was also caught working at the mine site. The raid was done upon request for assistance from Mines and Geosciences Bureau about the numerous complaints over illegal mining for magnetite sand in Cagayan. Investigation report revealed that Yinyi Mining Corporation and/or Well Resources Corp. in Barangay Dodan, Aparri, Cagayan is operating despite having no mineral processing permit. The firm was allowed only to extract sand and gravel. Through this information, the NBI Environmental and Wildlife Protection Investigation Division (EAWPID), NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (CAVRO), Isabela District Office (ISDO), and the Bayombong District Office (BAYDO) coordinated with MGB-DENR, Central Office; MGB-DENR, Tuguegarao, some local PNP with the assistance from the 17th IB Philippine Army –Masin, Alcala, Tuguegarao, Cagayan and some members of media trooped to the site. The raiding team caught Yingyi’s operation in full swing with six backhoes and six pay loaders at the site. It was also revealed that up to 40 trucks haul magnetite sand daily to Port Irene in Sta. Ana town, where the sand is loaded to ships bound for China. Since January this year, the NBI has embarked on a relentless campaign against violation of environmental laws. In June, the NBI seized at Pier 16 Manila North Harbor 55 container vans loaded with hot lumber coming from Davao City. Subsequent operations yielded more hot lumber in CARAGA. Likewise, the NBI acted on reports of alleged illegal smuggling and/or possession of elephant tusks last month. The suspects were referred for inquest before the Cagayan Valley Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Section 55 of RA No. 7942 (RA 7942) otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act of 1995, and Section 109 of Department of Environment and Natural Resources Administrative Order 201-21 (DAO 201-21), otherwise known as the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 7942, violation of Section 62 of RA 7942 and Section 141 of DAO 2010-21; and violation of RA No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) and RA No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act).

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A female con artist who had swindled several wealthy victims of their expensive jewelry, was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Parañaque City yesterday. The suspect was identified by Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: FRANCESCA LIM SANTIAGO, 40, married, housewife, and a resident of No. 30A Zobel St., BF Homes, Parañaque City. At-large is her husband, Benjamin Lacson Santiago, 40. Investigation conducted by the Reaction, Arrest and Interdiction Division (RAID) under Head Agent Ross Jonathan V. Galicia disclosed that the couple would befriend a prospective victim who they know have expensive jewelry. They would gypped mostly wealthy persons. One of the victims who filed their complaints with the NBI is celebrity Helen Gamboa Sotto, wife of Sen. Vicente Sotto III. The modus operandi starts with Francesca initially sweet-talking her victim into selling to her jewelry for which she would pay the cost. A series of purchases would be made and good checks are issued as payments. Thereafter, after more costly jewelry are bought by her, the checks that she would issue would bounce and she disappears. Her husband, Benjamin, assists her in their nefarious activity. Recently, complainant Helen Gamboa Sotto requested investigative assistance. Acting on said request, the NBI-RAID conducted investigation during which it was found out that Francesca has a string of cases in various courts. Among the cases, was that filed by Mrs. Helen Gamboa Sotto at the Quezon City Metropolitan Trial Court Branch 39 for violation of BP 22 (Anti-Bouncing Checks Law). Mrs. Sotto was defrauded of jewelry sold amounting to P8 million of which P4.5 million in checks issued eventually bounced. A warrant of arrest was issued against her. On May 23, 2012 at around 5:30 PM, by virtue of said warrant, suspect Santiago was apprehended by RAID agents. She was brought to the NBI where she is detained. The NBI is calling on all possible victims to come to the NBI and file their case.

body: A job recruitment/consultancy firm that victimized a hundred prospective overseas job workers was raided by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and arrested a key official in Baguio City last week. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the firm as: Humanitarian Migrant Management International Inc. (HMMII), a consultancy agency processing tourist visas, with office address at Room 303, 3rd Floor, Jose Miguel Bldg. 2, #1 Yandoc St. cor. Naguilian Road, Baguio City. The officers of the agency are: 1. SYDNEY ROCHE with aliases JOSEPH FERNANDEZ, JOSEPH CLIFFORD and KENNEY STEWART, founder and foreign principal of said agency; 2. MAYMA IMPERIAL, president and CEO; 3. GINA EBENG, personal assistant to the president and CEC; and 4. LIBERTY LEBENG, accounting and finance management officer/cashier. Arrested was LIBERTY LEBENG, accounting and finance management officer/cashier of the HMMII. Investigation by the NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) headed by Regional Director Jose A. body: Law enforcement Agents of the Government seized P3.031 Million worth of illegal drugs in a joint operation on August 12, 2021 in Baguio City. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric Distor said the controlled delivery operation was undertaken by the NAIA- Inter- Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (IADITG) composed of NBI- International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), PNP Aviation Security and Drug Enforcement Group, and Bureau of Customs. Distor added that the operation also resulted in the arrest of an individual identified as ELISA AGGUIRRE MILLARE. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the interception of a parcel by the Bureau of Customs at NAIA. Said parcel was declared as bed sheets and shoes but upon inspection the parcel in fact contains 1, 783 tablets of Ecstasy or Party Drugs wih an estimated street value of more than P1,300,000.00 which was shipped by Fostina Obobo of Neuss, Germany and consigned to Joyce Annsan Antono of Rm. 101 Brisle Ridge Residences, Pacdal Rd., Baguio City. Thus, the NAIA-IADITG members proceeded to Baguio City for a controlled delivery operation. On August 11, 2021, consignee was expected to claim the subject parcel from Baguio Post Office, the NAIA-IADITG members positioned themselves near the area to arrest the claimant. Unfortunately, the consignee did not claim the parcel and gave information that she will claim the said parcel at her residence in Bristle Ridge Residences. The next day, the joint operatives proceeded and positioned themselves in front of Bristle Ridge Condominium. A few moments later, a woman who was later identified as Subject Millare went outside to claim the subject parcel. At this juncture, the joint operatives immediately approached Subject Millare and placed her under arrest. Mayor Benjamin Magalong of Baguio City went to see the arrested Subject and express appreciation to the joint operatives for the arrest of the subject. Subject Millare was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Baguio City for violation of Section 4 (Importation of Dangerous Drugs) of R.A. 9165. In addition, the consignee, JOYCE ANNSAN ANTONO a.k.a. JOYCE ANN SAN ANTONIO (at-large) was also included in the charge.

title: All Covered Persons to Deal Only with Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions Registered with the AMLC
body: AMLC Resolution No. 81 dated 09 May 2019 directed the issuance of an advisory to covered persons (CPs) dealing with clients who are classified under the sector of Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) to demand presentation of their Certificate of Registration (COR) or Provisional COR (PCOR) with the AMLC as part of Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures under Section 3.5(b)(1) of the 2018 Implementing Rules and Regulations of the AMLA, as amended. Failure of a DNFBP to supply its P/COR is a ground to conduct enhanced due diligence measure (EDD) and/or to re-evaluate the business relationship. On the part of the CP failing to comply with this directive, it may be cited for the applicable administrative sanctions under the Rules of Procedure in Administrative Cases (RPAC). All CPs must deal only with registered DNFBPs with valid or subsisting P/COR or may risk being cited for a Serious Violation under Section 2(C)(25), Rule IV, of the RPAC. The updated list of Registered DNFBPs as of 31 March 2026 is posted at Registered DNFBPs . title: Court of Appeals Issues Another Freeze Order Against Assets of a Legislator Linked to Flood Control Anomalies
body: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) has taken action against another public official as it continues its probe of flood control project anomalies. On 23 April 2026, the Court of Appeals (CA) issued a Freeze Order on the properties of a prominent incumbent legislator, a business associate, and a corporate entity that were found to have been involved in the flood control project anomalies. The CA found probable cause to link their assets to Plunder under Republic Act (R.A.) No. 7659, to Direct and Indirect Bribery under the Revised Penal Code, and to violations of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (R.A. No. 3019). The Freeze Order covers a wide range of assets including 25 bank accounts and ten insurance policies registered under the name of the said legislator. They also include 27 bank accounts, ten insurance policies, and one investment account under the name of the legislator's alleged business associate; and two bank accounts, seven property accounts, and one real estate property registered under the name of the corporate entity. The filing of this Petition for Freeze Order underscores the AMLC's continuous commitment to uphold public accountability and protecting the integrity of the Philippine financial system," said AMLC Executive Director Atty. Ronel U. Buenaventura. A Freeze Order is a provisional remedy that preserves the assets which have probable connection to any unlawful activity prior to the filing of a forfeiture case. As of date, the AMLC has filed twelve (12) petitions for civil forfeiture before various Regional Trial Courts (RTC) against properties linked with the flood-control anomalies. These properties are currently preserved through Provisional Asset Preservation Orders issued by the RTCs, which prohibit their transfer, disposal, or movement while the civil forfeiture cases are pending.

title: Reminder to the Covered Persons on the Acceptability of Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) Number, National ID, and the Verified Information from the National ID Authentication Services (NIDAS) for Transactions with Covered Persons under the Anti-Money Laundering Act
body: T he Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) reminds covered persons that the presentation of the PhilSys Number (PSN) or the Philippine Identification Card (National ID) are recognized forms of identification for customers transacting business with financial institutions. The AMLC highlights that under Rule 18, Section 3.7 of the 2018 Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 9160, otherwise known as the Anti-Money Laundering Act, as amended (AMLA), the PSN and National ID shall be considered official and sufficient proof of identity of customers of covered persons, subject to the authentication requirements of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). This is in line with Section 12 of Republic Act No. 11055, otherwise known as the Philippine Identification System Act, which mandates that the presentation of the PSN or National ID shall constitute sufficient proof of identity for transacting business with government agencies or private entities, subject to proper authentication. Additionally, the requirement for First-Time Customers to present the original and submit a clear copy of an ID is satisfied through the generated confirmation from the PSA’s National ID Authentication Services (NIDAS). The AMLC confirms that this is also a sufficient proof of identity in the conduct of its customer due diligence (CDD), e.g., customer identification process and customer verification process. For record-keeping purposes, covered persons may screenshot, take a photo, and/or print the NIDAS confirmation. When conducting CDD using the National ID or the NIDAS facility, the presentation of a physical ID may already be dispensed with. Covered persons are likewise encouraged to use the NIDAS to assist in the conduct of its CDD in addition to existing processes related to beneficial ownership verification, determination of the purpose of relationship, and ongoing monitoring process. Notwithstanding the foregoing, covered persons are reminded that should a customer’s level of risk is high during the initial profiling or becomes high during the ongoing monitoring process, enhanced due diligence is warranted. In which case, the covered persons are expected to conduct additional due diligence measures and should not rely solely on the PSN, National ID, or NIDAS facility. Please be guided accordingly.

title: AMLC Secures Money Laundering Convictions
body: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) has made significant progress in the fight against financial crime with two judgments convicting individuals for money laundering predicated on violations of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC). Conviction of Conspirator of the Founders of a Religious Organization On 7 April 2026, the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Davao City rendered a Judgment convicting one person for thirteen (13) counts of money laundering predicated on violations of the Securities Regulation Code. The case arose from the unlawful activities of a religious organization and its founders who were charged with violations of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC), for illegally soliciting investments from the public. Financial investigation revealed that convicted launder conspired with the founders of the religious organization in carrying out the illicit scheme. For each count money laundering, he was sentenced to imprisonment ranging from a minimum of seven (7) years to a maximum of eight (8) years and one (1) month. In addition, a fine of Php 3 million was imposed for each count. Conviction of Founders of Trading Company On 23 April 2026, the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Zamboanga City rendered a decision convicting two money launderers for violating Section 4(b) of Republic Act (RA) No. 9160, as amended, otherwise known as the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2001 (AMLA). The case stemmed from an investigation into the activities of a trading company, which is owned and operated by one of the convicted launderers. The trading company was found to have engaged in the illegal solicitation of investments from the public, offering exorbitant returns despite lacking the required secondary license and registration from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The launderers were sentenced to an indeterminate penalty of imprisonment ranging from a minimum of four (4) years to a maximum of six (6) years. Each was also ordered to pay a fine of Php 1,500,000.00. These successful convictions were made possible through the close collaboration of the AMLC with its partner agencies, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the National Bureau of Investigation, and the Department of Justice. As the foregoing cases are currently under appeal, the AMLC shall continue to work closely with these agencies to safeguard the integrity of the Philippines' financial system against criminal activities.
